nesquena/hermes-webui#161.body:
Three fixes for custom endpoint model visibility, originally contributed in #157 by @hannesss81 (follow-up to #138). That PR was branched from v0.38.2 and would have reverted the v0.38.3/v0.38.4 provider-auth work, so the fixes are applied cleanly here on current master instead. PR #157 is closed in favour of this one.

**Bug 1 — URL construction (#157):** When `base_url` ends in `/v1`, the models endpoint was incorrectly constructed as `http://host/models` instead of `http://host/v1/models`. The old code stripped the `/v1` suffix before appending `/models`.

```python
# Before (wrong): strips /v1
endpoint_url = base_url[:-3] + '/models'  # http://host/models

# After (correct): appends /models to the existing /v1
endpoint_url = base_url + '/models'       # http://host/v1/models
```

**Bug 2 — `custom_providers` not in dropdown (#157):** `config.yaml` `custom_providers` entries (e.g. Ollama model aliases, Azure model overrides) were never added to the dropdown — only models auto-fetched from the `/v1/models` endpoint appeared. Now reads `custom_providers` from config and includes any entries not already in the auto-detected list.

**Bug 3 — API key from .env not used for custom endpoints (#157):** The custom endpoint auth code only checked `os.getenv()`. Keys defined in `~/.hermes/.env` (loaded at server startup) were already in `all_env` but not consulted. Now checks `all_env` first, falls back to `os.getenv`.

Tests: 466 passed. Closes #157. Fixes #138 (remaining gap).

nesquena/hermes-webui#2.title: Hermes Web UI ΓÇö Sprints 11-14: multi-provider models, settings, sessiΓÇª
nesquena/hermes-webui#2.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#2.body:
ΓÇªon QoL, alerts, polish

Sprint 11 (v0.13): multi-provider model support, streaming smoothness
- Dynamic model dropdown populated from configured API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Nous Portal)
- Scroll pinning during streaming (no forced scroll when user has scrolled up)
- All route handlers extracted to api/routes.py (server.py now ~76 lines)

Sprint 12 (v0.14): settings panel, SSE reconnect, session QoL
- Settings panel (gear icon) -- persist default model and workspace server-side
- SSE auto-reconnect on network blips
- Pin/star sessions to top of sidebar
- Import session from JSON export

Sprint 13 (v0.15): cron alerts, background errors, session duplicate, tab title
- Cron completion alerts: toast per completion + unread badge on Tasks tab
- Background agent error banner when a non-active session errors mid-stream
- Session duplicate button
- Browser tab title reflects active session name

Sprint 14 (v0.16): Mermaid diagrams, file ops, session archive/tags, timestamps
- Mermaid diagram rendering inline (dark theme, lazy CDN load)
- File rename (double-click in file tree) and create folder
- Session archive (hide without deleting, toggle to show)
- Session tags -- #hashtag in title becomes colored chip + click-to-filter
- Message timestamps (HH:MM on hover, full date as tooltip)

Test suite: 224 tests across 14 sprint files + regression gate, 0 failures.

nesquena/hermes-webui#3676.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#3676.body:
## Release v0.51.271 ΓÇö Release IM (stage-m1)

Medium-risk round, first batch. Shipping **#3626** alone; **#3629 dropped + re-held** after the regression gate found its singleton gateway-watcher design steals SSE observation from other-profile tabs (needs a profile-keyed registry rework ΓÇö details in the PR thread).

### Fixed
- **#3626** (@rodboev) ΓÇö preserve a named custom provider binding (`@custom:name:model`) when starting a chat instead of forcing the bare-model family fallback; live model options/optgroups carry `data-provider` for accurate selection. Frontend only.

### Gates
- Pre-Opus gate: merge-markers clean, `node -c` clean, ruff CLEAN, ESLint runtime CLEAN, browser smoke CLEAN
- Full suite: **7831 passed, 0 failed**
- Codex regression gate: **SAFE TO SHIP** (verified named-custom binding self-identifies + dropped stale-fallback falls through to existing server slow path, no new-chat failure)
- Opus advisor: confirmed clean within the prior 2-PR stage

Dropped + re-held: **#3629** (gateway watcher profile-scoping ΓÇö singleton-watcher cross-profile SSE theft + client reconnect both documented for rework).

Closes #3626

nesquena/hermes-webui#4253.title: Release OW (v0.51.436): cron sessions mark unread on new runs (#3460)
nesquena/hermes-webui#4253.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#4253.body:
## Release OW ΓÇö v0.51.436

Ships **#3921** (rodboev) ΓÇö cron sessions mark unread in the sidebar when a new run lands (#3460). Self-rebased onto v0.51.435 and gated fresh (Codex + Opus + full suite).

### The bounce ΓåÆ fix
Prior review found a cross-attribution bug: the unread resolver built `cron_<jobid>_` prefixes only from the just-completed jobs, so a job id that's a prefix of another (`backup` vs `backup_full`) could steal the other's session ΓÇö `cron_backup_full_ΓÇª` resolving to `backup`.

The re-push resolves sessions against **all** known job ids and attributes each session to the **longest** matching prefix. This is provably unambiguous: the matching prefixes of a single session id are nested, so the longest is unique (no tie case). The specific re-bounce scenario (only the short job completed, a newer long-prefix session exists) is dropped rather than stolen, and is explicitly tested.

### Gate results
- **Codex:** SAFE TO SHIP ΓÇö longest-prefix attribution verified, JS helper loads before panels.js, no global collision.
- **Opus:** SHIP ΓÇö proved the disambiguation mathematically sound for all id shapes (underscores, strict-prefix nesting); read-only `state.db` scan with graceful error handling, fires only on real completions, filters in Python not SQL `LIKE`; JS wiring references only existing symbols with sound null/zero handling.
- **Full suite:** touched tests pass (14 cron/sidebar tests incl. the new disambiguation test); local cascade is this box's process-group artifact (affected tests pass in isolation), CI's 3-shard isolation is authoritative.

Closes #3460.

Co-authored-by: rodboev

nesquena/hermes-webui#4270.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#4270.body:
## Release PE ΓÇö v0.51.444

Ships **#4268** (rodboev) ΓÇö refresh the sidebar session list on uncommitted writes + settings changes. This is the standalone version of the sidebar-cache fix that was bundled into #4133; split out per maintainer request, now its own clean PR.

### What it does
When CLI-session visibility is on, `/api/sessions` is cached and invalidated by a fingerprint of its source files. That fingerprint stamped `state.db` + the session index but **not** the SQLite write-ahead log (`state.db-wal`) ΓÇö so a freshly-written CLI/agent session still sitting in the WAL (not yet checkpointed into the main db) could be missed until the next checkpoint, leaving the sidebar stale. The fingerprint now also stamps `state.db-wal` and the settings file. Invalidation stays scoped to the CLI-session cache keys.

### Gate results
- **Codex SAFE:** tuple arity consistent on both the show_cli=on and early-return paths (and never unpacked downstream), WAL-path derivation double-guarded, no `api.configΓåÆapi.routes` import cycle, over-invalidation correctness-favoring + bounded.
- **Opus SHIP:** `SETTINGS_FILE` is the same object `save_settings` writes (so settings writes genuinely move its stamp), single clean import, no cycle.
- **Full suite:** 9 sidebar-cache tests green in isolation; wider failures are this box's process-group cascade artifact (CI authoritative).

Scope: `api/routes.py` (+77/-2) + `tests/test_session_sidebar_cache.py`. Closes #4268.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4275.title: Release PF (v0.51.445): scope gateway watcher to active profile (#2848)
nesquena/hermes-webui#4275.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#4275.body:
## Release PF ΓÇö v0.51.445

Ships **#3629** (rodboev) ΓÇö scope the gateway session watcher to the active profile (#2848). Self-rebased onto v0.51.444 and gated fresh (Codex + Opus + full suite). Both prior bounce findings resolved by the contributor; two additional CORE races caught by the gate and fixed inline.

### What it fixes
The gateway-session-SSE watcher was a single process-wide instance: one browser tab switching profiles stopped and replaced that global watcher, **silently stealing the gateway event stream from tabs on other profiles**. Now watchers are keyed by profile (registry, not singleton), each request's SSE subscribes to its own active-profile watcher, a profile switch restarts only that profile's watcher (never one another tab observes), and idle subscriber-free watchers are reaped.

### Bounce findings (both resolved by re-push)
1. Client now reconnects `_gatewaySSE` after a profile-switch restart.
2. The architectural fix: singleton `_watcher` ΓåÆ profile-keyed `_watchers` registry with subscriber-aware reaping + per-profile start/stop.

### Two CORE races caught by the gate + fixed inline (Codex)
- **Stop/subscribe TOCTOU:** a watcher reaped as subscriber-free during a concurrent switch left a late subscriber without the `None` sentinel ΓåÆ SSE hung open (keepalives, no events). `subscribe()` now checks `_stop_event` under `_sub_lock` after appending and self-enqueues the sentinel. Regression test added (`test_subscribe_after_stop_gets_sentinel_immediately`). *(Opus independently flagged the same race.)*
- **Switching tab's own SSE stayed on the old profile:** `switchToProfile()` never restarted `_gatewaySSE`, and the probe-reattach is gated on `!_gatewaySSE`. It now calls `startGatewaySSE()` after `S.activeProfile` is set (closes the old EventSource, reconnects with the new profile cookie; self-gates on `_showCliSessions`).

### Gate results
- **Codex SAFE** (final): both races closed, load-order verified (sessions.js before panels.js, typeof-guarded call), no new issue.
- **Opus SHIP:** registry concurrency sound (lock held for all mutations, joins outside lock, no deadlock), reaping protects live subscribers, no FD/thread leak, single-profile backward-compat holds.
- **Full suite:** gateway-watcher + reconnect-dedupe + memory tests green in isolation (36 passed); wider failures are this box's process-group cascade artifact (CI authoritative).

Closes #2848.

Co-authored-by: rodboev

nesquena/hermes-webui#4337.title: Release v0.51.467 ΓÇö symlinks in workspace file tree (#4228)
nesquena/hermes-webui#4337.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#4337.body:
## Summary

Ships **#4228** (display symlinks in the workspace file tree, issue #4226, by @rodboev) as **v0.51.467**.

Rebased onto current master (v0.51.466) ΓÇö the contributor's branch was 73 commits behind; the rebased code-diff was verified byte-identical to the PR head before staging.

## What it does

- Symlinks (directory and file) render with a distinct **chain-link icon** instead of the regular file/folder icon.
- Hovering a symlink shows **"Symlink ΓåÆ {target}"**, long targets middle-elided.
- Directory symlinks still expand / navigate like folders; regular files and folders are unchanged.

## Review / gate

- **XSS-safe (the key question ΓÇö attacker can name a symlink target):** the target reaches the DOM only via `nameEl.title` (a DOM property assignment, no HTML parsing). It is never concatenated into any `innerHTML`. Backend defense-in-depth: the target is the server-*resolved* path, dropped if it resolves outside the workspace / into a blocked path / forms a cycle (`api/workspace.py`). Independently confirmed by both Codex and Opus.
- **Opus cosmetic nit fixed:** `String.replace('{target}', value)` interprets `$&`/`` $` ``/`$'`/`$$` in the replacement ΓÇö a symlink target literally containing those would render garbled. Switched to a function replacer so the target text is inserted verbatim. (No security impact; cosmetic only.)
- **Gate (all three):** Codex SAFE TO SHIP ┬╖ Opus SAFE TO SHIP ┬╖ full suite **9268 passed, 0 failed** ┬╖ ESLint runtime gate clean.

## Attribution

Original author **@rodboev** (#4228). Commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer; CHANGELOG and this release credit the author.

Closes #4228. Resolves #4226.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4342.title: Release v0.51.469 ΓÇö resolve transcript virtualization freeze/jump + add opt-out (#4325)
nesquena/hermes-webui#4342.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#4342.body:
## Summary

Fully resolves **#4325** (transcript virtualization causes freeze + scroll-jump + reload after a streaming response finalizes; regression from #4214/#500, v0.51.440) and ships as **v0.51.469**. Two parts:

### Part A ΓÇö stream-end scroll fix (by @rodboev, #4328)
Semantic viewport anchoring for scroll restore. `_captureMessageViewportAnchor` records the first-visible message row by `data-msg-idx` + its pixel offset; `_restoreMessageViewportAnchor` re-pins **that message id** to the same offset after re-render, instead of a stale pixel `scrollTop` that mapped to the wrong message once virtual row heights changed. Plus: clear `_programmaticScroll` after the innerHTML wipe (stuck-flag fix), remove a synchronous toggle around the DOM clear, and mount a virtualized-out anchor row before a same-frame restore.

This supersedes PR **#4328** (its 4 commits are carried here byte-for-byte with @rodboev's authorship preserved + `Co-authored-by`).

### Part B ΓÇö virtualization opt-out toggle
A Preferences setting **"Virtualize long transcripts"** (default **ON** ΓÇö opt-out). When disabled, `_currentMessageVirtualWindow` returns a full non-virtualized window so the entire transcript renders at once (pre-#4214 behavior). Server-persisted (`virtualize_transcript`, default `True`), hot-applies on toggle, i18n in all 13 locales.

## Why this fully resolves every known virtualization symptom

`_currentMessageVirtualWindow` is the **single chokepoint**. When the toggle is OFF it returns `virtualized:false`, and every virtualization path bails:

| #4325 symptom | Eliminated by (toggle OFF) |
|---|---|
| Freeze (window recalc across re-renders) | `_updateMessageVirtualMeasurements` bails on `!virtualized` ΓÇö re-measure loop never runs |
| Jump to old message (pixel-scrollTop) | all rows mounted ΓåÆ anchor restore always finds the exact message row |
| Scroll back down | each re-render re-pins to the identical anchored message |
| Manual reload (blank viewport) | `_maybeRecoverVirtualizedBlankViewport` bails on `!virtualized` |

Default-ON users get Part A's anchor fix; opt-out users get a structural guarantee.

## Verification

- **Live browser (CDP), 120-msg transcript:** OFF ΓåÆ 120/120 DOM rows mounted, 0 virtual spacers, **scroll-drift across stream-done re-renders = 0**. ON (with Part A) ΓåÆ drift = 0 with realistic rAF-settled timing.
- **Gate (all three):** Codex **SAFE TO SHIP** (confirmed no production path computes virtualization state independently of the chokepoint) ┬╖ Opus **SAFE TO SHIP** (traced every consumer; confirmed the only other virtualization code is the unrelated sidebar list; boot ordering avoids opt-out flash) ┬╖ full suite **9285 passed, 0 failed**.
- Settings persistence round-trips (default `True`, accepts `false`); i18n 13/13 locales; live UI toggle hot-applies.

## Attribution

Part A is **@rodboev**'s work (#4328) ΓÇö authorship preserved on all 4 commits + credited in the CHANGELOG and release notes. Part B is maintainer-authored.

Closes #4325. Supersedes #4328.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4389.body:
## Release v0.51.483 ΓÇö QS (virtual-scroll height + measurement scroll-jump fixes)

Joint release of the #4346 transcript-virtualization scroll-jump cluster. **Contributor (@rodboev) gave the go-ahead** after the deep reviews on #4367 + #4368; shipped together because both touch `static/ui.js` + the same virtualization test file and interact in `_clearMessageVirtualHeightCache`. **Kept default-OFF / experimental** ΓÇö both fixes only run when "Virtualize long transcripts (experimental)" is enabled (#4343), so blast radius is opt-in users only.

### Included (both @rodboev)
- **#4367** ΓÇö per-role virtual scroll height estimates (user 120 / assistant 160 / tool_call 400 / default 140) so large tool-call rows aren't under-counted before measurement, which threw off the initial scroll position.
- **#4368** ΓÇö anchor-based scroll compensation during measurement (capture anchor + scrollTop ΓåÆ render ΓåÆ re-pin scrollTop by the anchor's measured delta; null/<2px guards; programmatic-scroll flag), plus a 150ms scroll-active guard that defers measurement refresh while scrolling, and session-switch cleanup of three scroll-settle globals.

### The combination
Both edit `_clearMessageVirtualHeightCache` ΓåÆ the merged function is the union: #4367's per-role-default estimate reset + #4368's scroll-settle-globals cleanup. The `test_clear_height_cache_resets_scroll_settle_globals` harness was updated to eval `_messageVirtualDefaultHeightForRole` + define the role map (since the combined function calls #4367's helper). Both PRs' test sets retained.

### Gate
- **Codex:** SAFE TO SHIP ΓÇö merged cache reset correct, default-off virtualization gate verified, scroll-compensation latch cleanup sound; 55 focused virtualization tests pass.
- **Opus:** SAFE TO SHIP ΓÇö no window-math regression, scroll compensation loop-bounded with no stuck-flag path, and **genuinely inert when the experimental setting is off (render byte-identical to master)**. One optional non-blocking micro-opt noted (not required).
- **Full suite:** 9386 passed, 0 failed. Ruff + ESLint clean. revert-guard: origin/master ancestor of HEAD.

Both PRs were deep-reviewed earlier (reviews posted on each); this is the contributor-approved ship. Attribution preserved via `Co-authored-by`.

Closes #4367, closes #4368.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4574.title: feat(mobile): prioritize titlebar session title with tap-to-reveal and long-press actions
nesquena/hermes-webui#4574.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#4574.body:
## Thinking Path

- The mobile titlebar squeezes the session title between a hamburger button and a metadata chip that is `flex-shrink:0`, so the title is always the loser when a source badge appears. The `max-width:60vw` cap on `.app-titlebar-title` (style.css:989) compounds this: once the badge and its surrounding space are accounted for, titles longer than ~8 characters are cut off with no recovery path.
- The maintainer's direction on #4520 was clear: title is primary, metadata is secondary, tap for full title, long-press for actions. The existing `ondblclick` rename in `syncAppTitlebar()` (panels.js:97-152) is the right model; it wires behavior directly on `titleEl` inside that function, so we follow the same pattern.
- For the popover I chose a lightweight fixed-position `div` (not a modal) because the maintainer explicitly said "not a modal dialog". Positioning it below the title rect gives a tooltip-like feel with zero layout disruption.
- For long-press I copied the project-chip pattern (sessions.js:5362-5407) verbatim: same `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend`/`touchcancel` quartet, same 10px drift cancel, same `long-pressing` class, same timer-clear-before-reschedule. The only differences are the delay constant (`SESSION_LONG_PRESS_DELAY_MS`) and the action (`_openSessionActionMenu(S.session, titleEl)`).
- The `_mobileTouchWired` guard is necessary because `syncAppTitlebar()` is called on every panel switch and session load; without it, each call would add another listener pair to the same element.

## What Changed

- `static/panels.js`: In `syncAppTitlebar()`, replaced `t('n_messages', vis.length)` with `String(vis.length)` for compact metadata. Added tap-to-reveal popover logic (gated on `'ontouchstart' in window`, wired once via `_mobileTouchWired`). Added long-press wiring using the project-chip pattern to call `_openSessionActionMenu` (separate `_mobileLpWired` guard, deferred until a writable session is loaded so late-arriving sessions still attach). Stale popovers are dismissed at the top of each `syncAppTitlebar()` call.
- `static/style.css`: In `@media(max-width:640px)`, widened `.app-titlebar-title` to `max-width:72vw` and compacted `.app-titlebar-sub` padding/font. Added `.app-titlebar-title-popover` rule for the full-title overlay. Added `.app-titlebar-title.long-pressing` feedback rule.
- `tests/test_mobile_titlebar_session_actions.py`: New focused static regression file with four tests pinning the HTML structure, compact metadata format, long-press infrastructure presence, and `_openSessionActionMenu` integration.

## Why It Matters

On mobile, session titles are the most important piece of context in the titlebar, but they were routinely cropped with no escape hatch. This change makes the title primary, gives users a tap path to the full title and a long-press path to rename/archive/delete, matching the UX pattern already established in session rows and project chips, without changing any desktop behavior.

## Verification

```
pytest tests/test_mobile_titlebar_session_actions.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- `syncAppTitlebar()` is called from multiple sites; the `_mobileTouchWired` and `_mobileLpWired` guards must be reset if the `titleEl` element is ever replaced (e.g., during the inline rename flow where `titleEl.replaceWith(inp)` and then `inp.replaceWith(titleEl)` are called). The flags set on the original element persist on re-insertion, so this is safe, but worth noting.
- The popover is positioned with `position:fixed` coordinates taken at click time. Rotation or soft-keyboard appearance after the popover is open will leave it mispositioned. A follow-up could reposition on `visualViewport.resize`.
- Source label compaction (abbreviating `CLI`, `Cron`, `API` etc.) was considered but deferred to keep this PR focused on the issue's stated scope.

## Upstream

Closes #4520.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 4.6 via Claude Code CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#4738.title: UI/UX - Two Neon theme additions
nesquena/hermes-webui#4738.author: savagebread
nesquena/hermes-webui#4738.body: - Neon Soft: lighter dark-mode surfaces with the same neon purple/cyan palette as the existing Neon skin. - Neon Paint: cyberpunk-themed skin with hot pink + electric cyan + warm amber on a deep purple-gray background. ## Neon Soft: ## Neon Paint: ### Thinking Path - Hermes WebUI supports a growing set of appearance skins (Neon, Zeus, Verdigris, Geist Contrast, Hepburn, etc.), each scoped to `data-skin` CSS variable tokens - The existing "Neon" skin uses a high-contrast purple/cyan palette. I found during day time usage the oled black was too dark for my tastes. I wanted a bit more vibrant neon colors. - This PR adds two new skins following the established skin pattern: full `:root` / `:root.dark` variable sets plus component-level overrides ### What Changed - **`static/style.css`** (+132 lines): - **Neon Soft** ΓÇö lighter dark-mode surfaces with the same neon purple/cyan palette as the existing Neon skin, but with softer contrast and glow intensity. Full light + dark palette under `:root[data-skin="neon-soft"]` / `:root.dark[data-skin="neon-soft"]`, plus component-level overrides for selection, titlebar, sidebar, inputs, buttons, scrollbars, tool cards, tree nodes, session badges/tags, diff blocks, and links. - **Neon Paint** ΓÇö cyberpunk "noodle bar" theme: hot pink (`#FF2D95`) + electric cyan (`#00E5FF`) + warm amber (`#FFB800`) on deep purple-gray backgrounds. Same scoped pattern as all other skins. - **`static/boot.js`** (+2 lines): Registered both skins in the `_SKINS` array with their `value` identifiers and accent colors. - **`static/index.html`** (1 line): Added `'neon-soft'` and `'neon-paint'` to the inline skin whitelist so they pass the localStorage gate. ### Why It Matters Expands the appearance picker with two more neon-inspired options ΓÇö a softer variant for users who find the original Neon too harsh, and a multi-color cyberpunk palette for a more vibrant look. Both follow the existing `data-skin` scoping contract so they don't bleed into other skins or the default appearance. ### Verification - Diff reviewed: CSS variables are fully scoped under the correct selectors (`:root[data-skin="neon-soft"]`, `:root.dark[data-skin="neon-paint"]`, etc.) - No new dependencies or build step introduced - Registration pattern matches existing skins (Hepburn, Zeus, Verdigris, etc.) - Inline skin whitelist in `index.html` updated consistently ### Risks / Follow-ups - No known risks ΓÇö skins are fully isolated under their `data-skin` attribute - CHANGELOG.md entry should be added under `[Unreleased]` ΓåÆ `### Added` when merged ### Model Used - **Provider:** llama.cpp - **Model:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q5_K_M

nesquena/hermes-webui#4810.title: feat: add Neuralwatt provider env var mapping
nesquena/hermes-webui#4810.author: b-yelverton
nesquena/hermes-webui#4810.body:
## What this does

Adds `neuralwatt` to `_PROVIDER_ENV_VAR` in `api/providers.py` so the WebUI correctly detects API keys and exposes Neuralwatt as a configurable provider. Also adds regression tests mirroring the existing `test_issue2025_xiaomi_env_key.py` pattern.

**Before:** Neuralwatt configured in Hermes `config.yaml` would not appear in the WebUI provider/model picker because the WebUI had no mapping from the `neuralwatt` provider ID to the `NEURALWATT_API_KEY` environment variable. The key was invisible to `has_key` detection and the provider could not appear as `configurable`.

**After:** Neuralwatt users who have `providers.neuralwatt` in their `config.yaml` and `NEURALWATT_API_KEY` in their `.env` will see Neuralwatt in the Providers settings and model picker with key detection working correctly.

## Security review

- **No secrets, keys, tokens, or credentials in this diff.** Only the provider ID string `"neuralwatt"` and the env var name string `"NEURALWATT_API_KEY"` ΓÇö a mapping, not a value.
- **No environment variable values are exposed.** The change adds a key to an internal lookup dict; it never reads or transmits the actual API key value.
- **No new network endpoints or data paths.** Identical pattern to the adjacent `xiaomi` and `opencode-*` entries already in the table.
- **No PII, no configuration leakage, no auth bypass.** This is purely a provider recognition mapping.

## Testing

- Verified key detection: `has_key` = `True`, `key_source` = `"env_file"` via `/api/providers`
- Verified model catalog: Neuralwatt appears as a provider group with models listed from `config.yaml` `providers.neuralwatt.models`
- Verified live fetch: no regression on existing providers
- Manually tested provider/model selection in WebUI
- **New regression tests** (`tests/test_issue_neuralwatt_env_key.py`, 4 tests, all passing):
  - `test_neuralwatt_env_var_mapping` ΓÇö asserts `_PROVIDER_ENV_VAR["neuralwatt"] == "NEURALWATT_API_KEY"`
  - `test_neuralwatt_provider_has_key_when_env_set` ΓÇö asserts `_provider_has_key("neuralwatt")` returns True with env var present
  - `test_neuralwatt_provider_has_key_false_without_env` ΓÇö asserts `_provider_has_key("neuralwatt")` returns False without env var

nesquena/hermes-webui#4871.body:
## Thinking Path

- The shipped Mermaid lightbox solved ΓÇ£make the diagram bigger,ΓÇ¥ but it never added the on-diagram controls the follow-up issue asks for.
- The cleanest implementation is one small viewer controller that mounts inline after Mermaid render and reuses the same interaction model inside the existing lightbox clone.
- Reusing the lightbox as the expanded viewer path keeps the feature set focused while avoiding a second fullscreen subsystem or a new dependency.

## What Changed

- `static/ui.js`: added a shared Mermaid viewer helper for toolbar injection, zoom and pan state, fit/reset behavior, and inline-to-lightbox handoff. Mounted it both after Mermaid render and inside `_openMermaidLightbox`.
- `static/style.css`: added toolbar, viewport, and pan-cursor styles for inline and lightbox Mermaid viewers, and updated the rendered Mermaid interaction styling to match.
- `tests/test_issue4075_mermaid_lightbox.py`: extended the shipped lightbox regression surface to assert the shared viewer shell is mounted without regressing the close and delegate behavior.
- `tests/test_issue4814_mermaid_toolbar.py`: added Node-backed behavioral coverage for toolbar mount, zoom state, fit/reset, drag-to-pan, and inline fullscreen handoff.
- `tests/test_1044_mermaid_csp_font.py`: kept the adjacent Mermaid init guard in the targeted verification bundle.

## Why It Matters

Users can inspect larger Mermaid diagrams directly in chat instead of treating the transcript as a static thumbnail. The shared controller also keeps the inline and expanded Mermaid interactions consistent without bloating the codebase with a third-party zoom library.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4881.body:
## Thinking Path

- The Kanban task create modal already ships workspace-kind and workspace-path inputs (from #4453), but the backend `_create_task_payload` accepts three more fields ΓÇö `skills`, `max_runtime_seconds`, and `parents` ΓÇö that the modal never exposes. Also, priority is a bare number with no hint about the range, and workspace path has no autocomplete.
- The backend already reads and forwards all three missing fields from the POST body; the change is entirely frontend: HTML controls, JS wiring in submit/reset/labels handlers, two datalist populate helpers, and i18n keys.
- Skills map to a comma-separated text input split to an array on submit, matching the CLI usage pattern. Max runtime is an optional number input (omitted when empty, same as optional workspace path). Parents is a single text input with a datalist from `_kanbanLinkableTaskOptions(null)` ΓÇö the same helper the detail view's dependency section reuses. All three are create-only, disabled in edit mode (mirroring workspace_kind/workspace_path).

## What Changed

- `static/index.html`: added skills text input, max_runtime_seconds number input with hint, parents text input with datalist, workspace path datalist, and priority hint element to the Kanban task modal
- `static/panels.js`: wired three new fields in `_kanbanResetTaskModalFields`, refactored `_kanbanSetTaskModalLabels` to use a `createOnlyIds` array that includes the new fields, added `_kanbanPopulateWorkspacePathDatalist` and `_kanbanPopulateParentsDatalist` helpers called from `openKanbanCreate`, and extended `submitKanbanTaskModal` to read and send skills (comma-split array), max_runtime_seconds (integer), and parents (`[parentsRaw]` list) in the create branch
- `static/i18n.js`: added 6 new i18n keys to all 14 locale blocks
- `tests/test_issue4470_kanban_task_editor_fields.py` (new): source-inspection tests covering HTML presence, submit-handler wiring, reset/labels coverage, datalist helper existence, i18n key completeness, and backend acceptance

## Why It Matters

Users who need to create Kanban tasks with specific skill requirements, runtime budgets, or dependencies had to fall back to the CLI or direct API ΓÇö the modal was missing three fields the backend already supported. The priority field showed a number with no context about meaning or range.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4969.title: feat(#4961): support URL query prefill for browser search
nesquena/hermes-webui#4969.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#4969.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes already uses URL state during boot for session targeting, so browser-search prefill belongs on that same surface instead of a separate endpoint.
- The security boundary is the important part here: `q` and `prompt` can stay as boot-time composer input, but URL `send` cannot stay action-bearing because any external link can satisfy it.
- Auth and boot ordering still matter, so the prefill intent has to survive the login/profile bootstrap and only be consumed once the terminal boot branch is ready to populate the composer.
- Draft-only prefill also can't allocate a default-workspace session on the user's behalf; `?q=` needs to leave `S.session` null until an explicit send.

## What Changed

- `static/sessions.js`: keep parsing `q` / `prompt` text and still strip `q`, `prompt`, and `send` during cleanup and session-URL promotion, but stop treating URL `send` as an actionable auto-submit flag.
- `static/boot.js`: capture the prefill intent early, defer URL cleanup to the terminal prefill helper after auth/profile bootstrap, and skip fresh default-workspace session binding on any draft-prefill boot path while still restoring browse-mode panel state.
- `tests/test_4961_url_query_prefill.py` and `tests/test_issue4877_fresh_blank_boot_workspace_bind.py`: extend the Node-harness regressions to pin the deferred cleanup step, the no-session draft prefill invariant, and the updated blank-boot default-workspace bind helper shape.
- `tests/test_new_chat_default_model_frontend.py`: keep the saved-session restore slice aligned with the rebased boot flow after the prefill hook runs.

## Why It Matters

Logged-out browser-search URLs now survive the login redirect and still land with the composer prefilled. Draft-only `?q=` links also stop creating a chat or overwriting the active-session pointer before the user decides to send anything.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_4961_url_query_prefill.py tests/test_issue4877_fresh_blank_boot_workspace_bind.py tests/test_new_chat_default_model_frontend.py tests/test_issue1488_composer_voice_buttons.py tests/test_issue5099_ctrl_k_text_input_guard.py -v --timeout=60
npx eslint --no-config-lookup -c eslint.runtime-guard.config.mjs static/boot.js
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #4961.

Attribution: the reporter's browser-search-engine use case and concrete `?q=` examples on [#4961](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/4961) still define the scope here; the rework keeps that flow on the boot surface while preserving prefill-only semantics.

nesquena/hermes-webui#4988.title: Prune orphan native-WebUI zero-message sessions from sidebar (#4985)
nesquena/hermes-webui#4988.author: enihcam
nesquena/hermes-webui#4988.body:
## Thinking Path

Issue #4985 (sibling of #3238/#4591) reports that clicking a sidebar row whose backing session has zero messages in `state.db.messages` returns 404 indefinitely ("Session not available in web UI."). Root cause verified independently via codebase-memory-mcp, codegraph, and direct file reads:

1. `api/routes.py:_build_session_list_cache_payload` has an orphan-prune loop that probes `state.db.sessions` for rows whose backing agent row was deleted (#3238/#4591).
2. Its predicate is structurally unreachable for native-webui rows: both `is_cli_session_row(s)` and `_is_api_server_sidecar_row(s)` short-circuit on `_session_source_is_webui(session)`, and the `not _session_source_is_webui(s)` guard on top makes the loop dead code for the only rows that need it.
3. The WebUI never exposes a delete affordance for these rows (read-only sidecar treatment was inherited from the #3238 fix and never re-scoped for native webui), so once they accumulate they linger forever ΓÇö every boot re-lists them, every click 404s.
4. Frontend `static/sessions.js:1195` reports the exact 404 string; its self-heal at 1207-1213 only clears localStorage + URL ΓÇö no in-memory sidebar-list mutation, so the row re-appears on next refresh.

The fix adds a parallel probe for native-webui zero-message rows (Option 1 in the issue, recommended over Option 2 client-side mutation since it removes the row at the source rather than papering over it in the UI).

## What Changed

- **`api/models.py`** ΓÇö added `agent_session_zero_message_sids(session_ids, *, profile=None)`, a batched chunked probe that returns the set of session ids whose `state.db.sessions` row exists but `state.db.messages` is empty for them. Mirrors `agent_session_rows_existing`'s safe-degrade contract: returns `frozenset()` (i.e. "no zero-message rows found") on any error / missing DB / missing tables, so a transient failure NEVER causes a stale-prune data loss.
- **`api/routes.py`** ΓÇö added a second pass after the existing CLI/API-server prune in `_build_session_list_cache_payload` (line 2094+). For each row in `_kept_after_orphan_prune` (so already-pruned rows aren't double-probed), if the row is `_session_source_is_webui(s)`, has no `active_stream_id` (inflight safety ΓÇö `_reconcile_stale_stream_state_for_session_rows` has already cleared stale stream ids at line 2068), and `_numeric_count(s["message_count"]) <= 0`, add it to `_webui_orphan_probe_rows`. Bucket by profile, batch-probe via the new helper, and `prune_session_from_index` for any confirmed zero-message sid. Wrapped in the same `try/except logger.debug(...)` pattern as the CLI path. Emits `diag_stage("prune_orphaned_webui_zero_message")` per prune. The existing CLI/API-server block (lines 2096-2140) is untouched.
- **`tests/test_issue4985_orphaned_webui_zero_message.py`** ΓÇö new 16-test regression file mirroring `tests/test_issue3238_orphaned_cli_sidecar_prune.py`. 7 helper-direct tests + 9 sidebar-payload tests covering:
  - Webui row `message_count=0` + state.db empty ΓåÆ pruned
  - Webui row `message_count=0` + state.db.messages has rows ΓåÆ retained
  - Webui row with `active_stream_id` ΓåÆ retained (inflight safety)
  - Webui row `message_count>0` ΓåÆ not even probed
  - CLI orphan / API-server orphan pruned via existing path (no regression)
  - Helper safe-degrades when state.db missing ΓåÆ no prune (no data loss)
  - 600-id batching (chunk_size=500 contract)
  - Mixed-batch integration: each row lands in its correct bucket
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** ΓÇö Unreleased entry under `### Fixed`.

## Why It Matters

The orphan webui rows come from real WebUI flows:
- A boot-time `+` click that opens a session but the first turn never commits (e.g. tab closed, profile switch that resets the active id, settings page nav)
- Sidebar nav that opens a session then closes the tab before any message lands

These are not user error paths ΓÇö they're silent state accumulation. The existing CLI/API-server prune (#3238/#4591) explicitly excluded webui because the read-only sidecar treatment was inherited unchanged, but that exclusion is the bug for native-webui rows whose backing state.db row genuinely has no content. Every click on such a row is a 404 toast that says "Session not available in web UI." with no path forward.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue4985_orphaned_webui_zero_message.py -v` ΓåÆ **16 passed**
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue3238_orphaned_cli_sidecar_prune.py -v` ΓåÆ **16 passed** (no regression in #3238/#4591)
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/` (full suite) ΓåÆ 10,608 passed; 3 unrelated pre-existing failures in `test_tls_aware_probe.py` + `test_v050259_sessiondb_fd_leak.py` (verified independent of this branch via `git stash`).
- `python3 scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff origin/master` ΓåÆ **No findings** on the new lines.

State-layer invariant: `SESSION_INDEX_FILE` rows whose backing `state.db` session has zero messages and no in-flight turn are removed from the index within one `/api/sessions` poll. The `state.db` row itself is untouched (no destructive schema change); future turns that create a new session with the same id would still find a clean slate.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- **Inflight first-turn race:** gated on `s.get("active_stream_id")` ΓÇö any row whose first turn is mid-flight is NOT probed. `_reconcile_stale_stream_state_for_session_rows` (called at line 2068, before the prune) has already cleared stale stream ids, so a row still carrying `active_stream_id` at this point is genuinely streaming.
- **Self-heal vs explicit refresh:** the frontend (`static/sessions.js:1207`) currently only refreshes the sidebar after a user action. Users whose sidebar is open while this fix lands will see the orphan rows persist until their next `/api/sessions` poll (Γëñ the existing poll cadence). No frontend change needed ΓÇö the row is gone at the source on the next rebuild.
- **Option 2 from the issue** (client-side mutation in `static/sessions.js`) was considered and rejected ΓÇö removing at the source is durable across reloads and any other client.

- **Diagnostic count semantics (per Greptile review):** `diag_stage("prune_orphaned_webui_zero_message")` is now inside the `try` block so it counts only *confirmed* prunes, not attempts. The pre-existing CLI-path pattern at `api/routes.py:2147` (`diag_stage("prune_orphaned_agent_sidecar")` outside its `try/except`) has the same misleading structure and is a good follow-up candidate for a one-line refactor in a separate small PR ΓÇö left out of this fix to keep the scope strictly to the #4985 sibling of #3238/#4591.

## Model Used

- Implementation + tests + changelog: `MiniMax-M3` (via `@fixer` subagent, executed on a child session with full source-tree access).
- Root cause analysis + PR composition + verification: `MiniMax-M3` directly.
- Documentation sources consulted: `tests/test_issue3238_orphaned_cli_sidecar_prune.py` (test pattern mirror), `api/agent_sessions.py:165-200` (`is_cli_session_row`), `api/routes.py:6510` (`_is_api_server_sidecar_row`), `api/routes.py:4029` (`_reconcile_stale_stream_state_for_session_rows`), `api/models.py:3202` (`agent_session_rows_existing` ΓÇö pattern mirror).
- Three independent verification paths before fix: codebase-memory-mcp search_graph + trace_path, codegraph_explore, direct file reads.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5002.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5002.body:
## Thinking Path

- The backend project contract is already live, `newSession()` can already carry `project_id`, and the missing piece is a local affordance on the existing project-chip surface.
- The shortcut has to do more than post a payload, because the sidebar currently hides rows outside `_activeProject`; a cross-project quick-create that leaves the old filter behind would create a session and then immediately hide it.
- The narrow fix is a quiet per-project `+` inside the sidebar chips, plus a small `newSession()` override path that preserves the old filtered-project behavior when no explicit project choice is supplied.

## What Changed

- `static/sessions.js`: adds a chip-local quick-create path that can target an explicit project id, while preserving the existing `_activeProject` fallback for the main New Session flow.
- `static/style.css`: adds scoped styling for a quiet inline project quick-create control that stays usable on touch layouts.
- `tests/test_4676_project_new_session_shortcuts.py`: adds focused regression coverage for the explicit project payload, sidebar filter alignment, and legacy fallback behavior.

## Why It Matters

This turns a repetitive two-step sidebar workflow into a one-click project action without redesigning the main New Session control. It also keeps the new active conversation visible instead of creating it in a project that the sidebar immediately filters away.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_4676_project_new_session_shortcuts.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #4676.

Design direction follows [Issue #4676](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/4676), especially the per-project `+` proposal and maintainer guidance to keep the affordance visually quiet.

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5005.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes WebUI already has a configurable composer send key for `enter` and `ctrl+enter`.
- Some users prefer plain Enter to stay inside the textarea for multi-line drafting, but still want a keyboard-only submit path.
- Adding `shift+enter` as a third explicit preference preserves the current default and avoids changing existing user muscle memory.
- The frontend needs to keep autocomplete behavior compatible: in `shift+enter` mode, plain Enter should remain textarea input even when the command dropdown is open.

## What Changed

- Added `shift+enter` as an allowed `send_key` setting and Settings dropdown option.
- Updated composer key handling so `shift+enter` mode sends only on Shift+Enter while plain Enter remains newline input.
- Preserved existing Enter-to-send default and Ctrl/Cmd/Numpad Enter behavior in `ctrl+enter` mode.
- Added static regression coverage for the new mode and expanded settings round-trip coverage.
- Added an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Why It Matters

Users who compose multi-line messages frequently can keep Enter as newline without losing a keyboard submit shortcut. The change is opt-in, so existing desktop and mobile defaults remain compatible.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_sprint17.py tests/test_shift_enter_send_key.py tests/test_numpad_enter_submit.py tests/test_mobile_layout.py -q` ΓåÆ 80 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_index_shell_template_cache.py tests/test_sprint17.py tests/test_shift_enter_send_key.py tests/test_numpad_enter_submit.py tests/test_mobile_layout.py -q` ΓåÆ 85 passed
- `npm run lint:runtime` ΓåÆ passed
- Manual Playwright event probe confirmed:
  - default `enter`: Enter sends, Shift+Enter does not send
  - `shift+enter`: Enter does not send, Shift+Enter sends and prevents default
  - autocomplete open + `shift+enter`: plain Enter does not select/dropdown-submit

## Risks / Follow-ups

- The setting label is English-only, matching the existing send-key labels.
- This is a keyboard interaction change plus one dropdown option; no layout or theme structure changed. Before/after visual evidence is limited to the Settings select containing one additional option.

## Contract Routing

Task type: UI/UX behavior preference and settings validation
Touched areas: composer keyboard handling, Settings send-key enum/dropdown, static regression tests, changelog
Relevant public docs:
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`
- `docs/UIUX-GUIDE.md`
- `DESIGN.md`
Scope boundaries: no streaming, session recovery, persistence-layer, auth, or runtime state contract changes.
Evidence needed before claiming done: focused settings and composer keyboard tests, JS runtime lint, and manual event probe.

AI-assisted: OpenAI GPT-5.5 via Hermes Agent, using local file, terminal, and GitHub API tools. Human requested the behavior and PR submission.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5012.title: feat(auth): add native OIDC login for WebUI sessions (#3825)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5012.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5012.body:
## Thinking Path

- The WebUI already has a clean session-cookie boundary, but it only supports password, passkeys, or no auth.
- The repo already has `api/oauth.py`, yet that module is for onboarding provider credentials, not end-user login, so extending it would blur two distinct OAuth responsibilities.
- The right slice is a dedicated OIDC login path that validates the IdP response and then hands off to the existing `create_session()` flow instead of inventing a second session system.

## What Changed

- `api/auth_oidc.py`: adds WebUI-login OIDC configuration, discovery, PKCE, callback validation, JWT/JWKS verification, allowlist enforcement, outbound OIDC endpoint validation, exact ES-curve binding, and non-finite numeric-claim rejection.
- `api/auth.py`: treats native OIDC as a first-class auth mode and exposes the public start/callback routes so pure-SSO deployments stay gated.
- `api/routes.py`: wires `/api/auth/oidc/start`, `/api/auth/oidc/callback`, additive `/api/auth/status` capability reporting, and the minimal login affordance.
- `tests/test_issue3825_oidc_auth.py`: adds focused regression coverage for start, callback success/failure, auth-status behavior, endpoint safety, JWKS refresh, ES signature validation, curve binding, and numeric-claim parsing.

## Why It Matters

Self-hosted deployments can delegate WebUI login to a real IdP without putting the app behind a second auth proxy. The WebUI keeps owning its own session cookie, so the new path stays compatible with the existing login model instead of creating a parallel auth system.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_issue3825_oidc_auth.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #3825.

## Model Used

GPT 5 via Codex CLI

## Thinking Path

- Hermes WebUI is a mobile-capable browser front door for Hermes.
- The titlebar, drawer controls, send button, and approval cards are primary mobile interaction surfaces.
- On narrow mobile widths, those controls need stable 44px-class targets and approval cards need to fit without clipping.
- This PR keeps the fix in `static/style.css` only, preserving the no-build-step frontend shape.

## What Changed

- Gives mobile titlebar, new-chat, reload, sidebar-close, icon, nav, and send controls stable touch target sizing.
- Keeps SVG/icon layout from resizing or clipping those mobile controls.
- Adjusts the mobile sidebar edge guard to match the taller titlebar.
- Makes mobile approval cards scroll within a bounded panel and lays action buttons out in a narrow-width grid.
- Disables the mobile send-button animation while visible so proof and touch behavior stay stable.

## Why It Matters

This reduces mobile hard stops in the chat flow: opening the drawer, using topbar controls, sending a message, and responding to approval prompts should remain usable at iPhone-width and small Android-width layouts.

- Required assertions passed for 44px primary targets, no horizontal overflow, no clipped controls, model/reasoning dropdown viewport fit, approval viewport fit, and no visible update banner in the Axis runtime proof.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5024.title: Gate reasoning_content replay for provider-facing history
nesquena/hermes-webui#5024.author: Stacey2911
nesquena/hermes-webui#5024.body:
## Problem

Historical assistant `reasoning_content` is currently replayed into subsequent model-facing conversation turns via `_sanitize_messages_for_api()`. For local/generic providers such as LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, and generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints, this can inject stale internal reasoning into future turns, increasing prompt size and potentially affecting model behavior.

## Why this matters for local/generic providers

Local backends generally do not require historical `reasoning_content` replay to maintain conversation continuity. When preserved, this metadata can add unnecessary tokens to later requests and can carry stale internal reasoning from earlier turns into the provider-facing history.

The WebUI can still keep this metadata for session/display purposes; the issue is forwarding it to providers that do not use it.

## Compatibility concern

Some provider protocols may require historical reasoning replay for tool-use continuity. Stripping `reasoning_content` universally could break those integrations.

This patch adds a provider-facing replay policy instead of a blanket strip/preserve decision.

## Policy modes

The sanitizer reads `webui.reasoning_content_replay` with three modes:

- `auto` ΓÇö default; strips for local/generic providers and preserves for explicitly known provider/protocol paths
- `strip` ΓÇö always removes historical assistant `reasoning_content` from provider-facing history
- `preserve` ΓÇö keeps current behavior and preserves `reasoning_content`

### Auto mode behavior

| Provider | Model ID pattern | Action |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | any | Preserve; may require replay for thinking/tool-use continuity |
| Anthropic | starts with `claude` | Preserve; may require replay for structured reasoning/tool-use continuity |
| OpenAI | contains `gpt-5`, `o1-`, `o3-`, or `o4-` | Preserve; may require replay for reasoning/tool-use continuity |
| All others | any | Strip; local/generic backends do not need historical reasoning replay by default |

## Important notes

- Stored session/display reasoning metadata is unchanged.
- This only affects provider-facing sanitized history.
- Input message objects are not mutated.
- Existing sanitizer behavior is preserved, including orphaned tool dropping, OOB block scrubbing, partial handling, and recovered user logic.
- This is separate from PR #4978, which handles literal `[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE]` marker blocks in message `content`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_reasoning_content_replay.py`: 25 passed
- Existing sanitizer/regression coverage: 57 passed across orphaned tools, recovered context replay (#4283), partial bloat handling, cancel/partial preservation (#893), and PR #1375 partial tool-call sanitization

Total validation: 82 passed.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5058.title: fix(chat): prevent stream-end worklog collapse jump
nesquena/hermes-webui#5058.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5058.body:
## Summary

Fix a **new post-#4970 stream-end jump class**: when a pinned reader follows a streamed assistant turn with a large live worklog/tool trace, `STREAM_DONE` collapses the live worklog into a compact settled worklog. That can shrink `scrollHeight` by hundreds of pixels in one frame, causing the browser to clamp `scrollTop` down by the same amount. Scroll state is still correct (`pinned=true`, `gap=0`), but the user sees a large backward jump.

This is distinct from #4934/#4970's earlier classes (spurious upward scroll events / post-render artifacts). Here the page is correctly pinned; the DOM itself shrinks.

## Evidence (Playwright repro on a source build)

Instrumented `#messages` with a 16ms sampler for every `scrollHeight` (`H`) and `scrollTop` (`T`) delta while sending a prompt that triggers multiple tool calls/worklog rows:

**Before this fix:**

```text
H: scrollHeight -367 / -422 px at STREAM_DONE
T: scrollTop    -367 / -422 px at STREAM_DONE
state: pinned=true, userUnpinned=false, stream=no, gap=0
```

The jump magnitude equals the live worklog collapse height. Small reasoning-only answers showed the same signature at ~28px; large tool-worklog answers reproduced the user's "much more than one line" jump at 367-422px.

DOM comparison showed the stream peak had an expanded `agent-activity-group tool-worklog-group` while the settled turn used a compact/collapsed activity group; the net live->settled height drop was the visible jump.

**After this fix:**

Same multi-tool repro:

```json
{
  "nShrinks": 0,
  "shrinks": [],
  "nBack": 0,
  "backs": [],
  "gap": 0,
  "groups": [{
    "cls": "agent-activity-group tool-worklog-group activity open",
    "h": 450,
    "body": [{"h": 402, "display": "block"}]
  }]
}
```

## Fix

- For pinned followers (`_scrollPinned && !_messageUserUnpinned`), keep the just-settled worklog open. This keeps the live->settled DOM swap height-stable and prevents the browser from clamping `scrollTop` backward.
- Unpinned readers still get compact/collapsed settled worklogs and preserve their viewport normally.
- Make `_anchorSceneWorklogGroup()` respect explicit `opts.collapsed`; previously it hard-coded `collapsed: !live`, so callers could not request an open settled group.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_issue4970_stream_done_shrink_regression.py` with source locks for:

- the pinned-follow helper (`_scrollPinned && !_messageUserUnpinned` as authority, not transient bottom distance),
- settled rendering passing `collapsed:!keepSettledWorklogOpen`,
- `_anchorSceneWorklogGroup()` honoring explicit `opts.collapsed`.

Focused local verification on upstream master worktree:

```text
node --check static/ui.js
python -m pytest \
  tests/test_issue4970_stream_done_shrink_regression.py \
  tests/test_issue4856_android_scroll_regression.py \
  tests/test_issue4295_scroll_pin_reentry.py -q

22 passed
```

Suggested labels: `bug`, `scroll`, `streaming`, `size:S`.

## Thinking Path

- The #4657 maintainer feedback was about rebasing/splitting the already-shipped visibility-toggle work from the remaining fit-engine change.
- While testing that composer-control surface, we added a separate UX enhancement: letting users reorder the Settings composer-control chips.

- Supports desktop drag/drop chip sorting.
- Supports touch long-press sorting for phones and Android WebView while preserving normal tap-to-toggle behavior.

## Why It Matters

Users can arrange composer footer controls to match their workflow, similar to the existing sidebar-tab ordering behavior, without changing which controls are visible.

## Relationship To #4657

This is intentionally split from #4657. It does not include the fit engine, `.cf-icons`, `.cf-burger`, compact quota menu, or compact-chip label changes. It only adds ordering for the already-existing composer-control visibility chips.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5079.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5079.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes Agent already supports `tts.openai.{base_url,model,voice}`, but the WebUI still stops at Browser, Edge, and ElevenLabs. The missing work is not just one server branch; the settings panel, speaker button, auto-read path, and voice-mode loop all need to recognize `engine:"openai"`.
- The repo already has the right authority boundary for server TTS. `/api/tts` owns provider dispatch and credential lookup, so the clean fix is to extend that owner instead of adding a browser-direct OpenAI client or a second endpoint.
- The last detail that matters is the voice selector. OpenAI voices are server-configured, not browser SpeechSynthesis voices, so `static/panels.js` must show that clearly instead of falling through to browser-driven behavior.

## What Changed

- `static/index.html`: adds `OpenAI TTS (server)` to the TTS engine dropdown.
- `static/panels.js`: treats OpenAI as a server-configured voice in `window._populateTtsVoices()`.
- `static/ui.js`: adds `_playOpenaiTts()` plus OpenAI branches in `speakMessage()` and `autoReadLastAssistant()`.
- `static/boot.js`: adds the OpenAI server-TTS branch in voice mode.
- `api/routes.py`: extends `/api/tts` with `engine == "openai"`, using `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, then `.env`, and reading `tts.openai.{base_url,model,voice}` with OpenAI-compatible defaults.
- `tests/test_issue4982_openai_tts.py`: adds endpoint and source-contract coverage for the new engine.
- `tests/test_499_tts_playback.py`: extends the existing WebUI TTS regression coverage for the OpenAI setting and routing.

## Why It Matters

Users who already run an OpenAI-compatible TTS backend can finally use it from the WebUI speaker icon, auto-read, and voice mode instead of falling back to unrelated engines. The patch keeps provider config and credentials on the server, where the rest of the repo already expects them.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5120.title: feat(#692): add configurable budget limit with percentage-used tracking
nesquena/hermes-webui#5120.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5120.body:
## Thinking Path

- The cost chart already computes a monthly pace projection from 7-day snapshots. The natural extension is to let the user anchor that projection against a self-defined budget, no new data sources, no new backend infrastructure.
- The budget is one more setting stored in `settings.json`, surfaced in the `/api/provider/cost-history` response as `monthly_budget` so the frontend can compute the percentage inline without a second round-trip. The existing `limit` field stays as the OpenRouter provider credit limit.
- Pace-vs-budget is the right display metric, not month-to-date actual, because the 7-day snapshot window can't reliably reconstruct full-month spend, but the pace projection already answers "am I on track to stay under budget?"

## What Changed

- **`api/config.py`**: added `provider_cost_budget` to `_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`, then centralized validation in `_coerce_provider_cost_budget(...)` so save-time persistence rejects zero, negative, non-finite, over-cap, and rounded-to-zero sub-cent values before they can be stored.
- **`api/providers.py`**: `_get_provider_cost_budget()` now reuses that same helper on read, so manually edited out-of-range values no longer leak back out through `monthly_budget`; `get_provider_cost_history` still includes `monthly_budget` in all three OpenRouter response paths (`no_key`, `unavailable`, `available`) while leaving `limit` as the provider credit limit.
- **`static/panels.js`**: `renderProviderCostChart` annotates the Monthly Pace label with `(N% of budget)` when a budget is configured, amber at `>=80%` and red at `>=100%`; new `_attachBudgetControls` appends a budget input row with Set/Clear buttons and a progress bar with color-coded fill.
- **`static/style.css`**: added compact CSS for the budget row, input group, progress bar, and pace annotation coloring.
- **`static/i18n.js`**: added six new keys in `en`, with the existing locale fallback chain covering the rest.
- **`tests/test_provider_cost_budget.py`**: covers settings persistence, endpoint response shape, frontend wiring, the `0.004` rounded-to-zero regression, and the read-side cap for manually edited settings.

## Why It Matters

Users running OpenRouter for production workloads can now compare their projected monthly spend against a self-defined budget directly on the quota card. "Monthly pace: $142.80 (142% of budget)" turns a number into a decision. The feature stays opt-in, users without a budget configured see no change.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_provider_cost_budget.py -v --timeout=60`
- `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`
- Manual: open Settings -> Providers. Confirm the "Monthly budget" input appears below the cost chart. Set a budget, verify the pace annotation shows `(N% of budget)` and a progress bar appears. Clear the budget, verify the progress bar disappears. Refresh usage, confirm the chart and budget control re-render correctly.

## Upstream

Closes #692.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 4.6 via Claude Code CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5157.title: Fix session-backed HTML media artifact previews
nesquena/hermes-webui#5157.author: santastabber
nesquena/hermes-webui#5157.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes WebUI already supports sandboxed inline previews for local HTML artifacts through `/api/media`.
- Session-scoped `MEDIA:` authorization only covered exact image paths, so assistant-emitted HTML/PDF artifacts outside the active workspace could fail even though they were present in the transcript.
- The chat preview loaders also rebuilt `/api/media` URLs without carrying the active `session_id`, so the backend could not prove the artifact was session-emitted.
- This PR keeps the existing deny-list and sandboxing model, but extends the session-token authorization path to safe preview MIME types and makes HTML/PDF preview requests session-aware.

## What Changed

- Generalized the session MEDIA-token helper from image-only to a safe MIME whitelist.
- Kept the existing image-only wrapper for compatibility with existing callers/tests.
- Added `text/html`, PDF, audio, and video preview MIME types to the session-emitted artifact allowlist.
- Updated chat HTML/PDF lazy preview URLs to include the current `session_id` for fetch, open, and fallback download links.
- Added focused regressions for:
  - exact assistant-emitted HTML `MEDIA:` paths outside the workspace;
  - user-authored `MEDIA:` paths staying unauthorized;
  - MIME allowlist enforcement;
  - frontend HTML/PDF preview fetches carrying `session_id`.

## Why It Matters

HTML artifacts generated by an assistant can now open consistently from chat even when they are not under the active workspace, while still preserving the important security boundary:

- user-authored `MEDIA:` paths cannot mint access;
- unmentioned paths remain blocked;
- Hermes state/secrets deny-list still runs before serving;
- HTML continues to use the existing sandboxed preview path.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_media_inline.py tests/test_pdf_html_preview.py tests/test_issue1800_file_html_interactions.py -q`
  - `115 passed`
- `node --check static/ui.js`
- `python3 -m py_compile api/routes.py`
- `python3 scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff origin/master`
  - no new violations on added/modified lines
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`

## Risks / Follow-ups

- This intentionally does not allow arbitrary local HTML browsing. The file still needs to be either under an allowed media root or exactly present in an assistant/tool `MEDIA:` token for the requested session.
- SVG remains download-only.
- The PR does not change workspace file browser behavior; it only fixes chat `MEDIA:` artifact preview authorization.

## Model Used

OpenAI GPT-5.5 via OpenRouter, with Hermes Agent tool use for local implementation and verification.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5165.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5165.body:
## Thinking Path

- Extensions already have browser-session authority, but the docs deliberately stop short of arbitrary backend proxying, so a quota panel still has no same-origin path to a remote or credentialed llm-proxy.
- `/api/provider/quota` was the obvious reuse candidate, but it returns a provider-card payload rather than the llm-proxy quota document or its reload contract.
- The narrow fix is one core-owned authenticated bridge for one fixed upstream path, `/v1/quota-stats`, under the extension namespace.

## What Changed

- `api/providers.py`: add a dedicated llm-proxy quota-stats helper that reuses the existing named `custom:llm-proxy` connection authority when present, keeps the bridge scoped to that exact provider, blocks upstream redirects on the credentialed request, bounds the upstream response size, validates supported GET and POST inputs, redacts echoed bearer material from successful JSON, and sanitizes failures.
- `api/routes.py`: add authenticated `GET` and `POST` handling for `/api/extensions/proxies/llm-proxy/quota-stats`, wrapped in `profile_env_for_active_request_readonly(...)`, while keeping the GET query parsing aligned with the rest of `routes.py`.
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`: document the exact extension-facing quota-stats contract and keep the no-generic-proxy boundary explicit.
- `tests/test_extension_llm_proxy_quota_stats.py`, `tests/test_issue3957_profile_providers_models.py`, and `tests/test_provider_quota_status.py`: cover forwarding, oversized-response rejection, validation, named custom-provider reuse, rejection of unrelated custom providers, profile isolation, route guards, and negative-space paths.

## Why It Matters

Extension authors can ship a reviewed quota panel without exposing llm-proxy credentials in browser code and without turning WebUI into a general-purpose extension proxy. The review surface stays narrow and the server-held bearer now stays server-side even if upstream redirects or echoes secrets.

## Verification

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_extension_llm_proxy_quota_stats.py tests/test_issue3957_profile_providers_models.py tests/test_provider_quota_status.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context: `python -m pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5033.

This route follows the maintainer's 2026-06-27 scoping note that narrowed the issue to a fixed allowlisted quota-stats bridge rather than a generic extension proxy, and the 2026-06-29 follow-up closes the reproduced redirect and echo leak paths on that bridge.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5168.body:
## Thinking Path

- WebUI already knows that `/pet` exists, but today it only uses that metadata to hide the command from autocomplete and return the generic CLI-only dead end.
- The maintainerΓÇÖs latest scope split is narrower than the original issue title: core should own the WebUI `/pet` surface, while Desktop Companion owns the actual mascot experience and desktop-parity behavior.
- The fix therefore stays on the slash-command path: surface `/pet`, return install or start guidance when Desktop Companion is not ready, and hand off to an extension hook once the extension provides one.

## What Changed

- `static/commands.js`: add a narrow `/pet` WebUI override helper, keep CLI-only autocomplete filtering for every other command, let `/pet` surface with Desktop Companion-specific guidance, and treat a truthy extension-owned handoff result as authoritative.
- `static/messages.js`: intercept `/pet` before the generic CLI-only fallback, route it through the new helper, and leave the rest of the CLI-only flow unchanged.
- `tests/test_cli_only_slash_commands.py`: preserve the generic CLI-only fallback expectations, prove `/pet` stays visible with real CLI-only metadata, and keep other CLI-only commands hidden.
- `tests/test_issue4843_pet_webui_command.py`: add focused browserless coverage for missing, disabled, disconnected, hook-handled, and hook-failure `/pet` states, plus a send-path harness that proves `/pet` bypasses the generic CLI-only dead end while `/browser` still uses it.

## Why It Matters

`/pet` stops being a dead-end in WebUI and starts telling users what to do next. Core owns the command surface it can actually guarantee today, while Desktop Companion stays responsible for the mascot experience and the richer `/pet` behavior once installed and connected.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_cli_only_slash_commands.py tests/test_issue4843_pet_webui_command.py -v --timeout=60`
- `npx eslint --no-config-lookup -c eslint.runtime-guard.config.mjs "static/commands.js" "static/messages.js"`

Full-suite CI context: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #4843.

Follows the maintainer's scoped split in the [issue discussion](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/4843#issuecomment-4827531529): core owns the WebUI `/pet` surface, while Desktop Companion owns the mascot behavior and richer `/pet` semantics.

Related scope: Desktop Companion already defines the gallery install and local start flow, so this change stays on the WebUI slash surface instead of moving mascot behavior into core.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5170.title: fix(ux): honor busy input mode preference on first send after load (#5167)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5170.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5170.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5167 ΓÇö the **Busy input mode** preference (`queue` / `interrupt` / `steer`) was ignored for any send that happened before the async boot IIFE resolved `await api('/api/settings')`. Sends in that window silently fell back to `queue`, ignoring a saved `steer`/`interrupt` preference until the user re-saved the setting.

Reported by **@b3nw**.

## Root cause (client-side boot race)

`window._busyInputMode` had **no eager default**. It was only assigned:

- `static/boot.js` (success path, inside the async boot IIFE that awaits `/api/settings`)
- `static/boot.js` (catch fallback ΓåÆ `'queue'`)
- `static/panels.js` (on settings save)

Both send-path read sites use `const busyMode=window._busyInputMode||'queue'` (`static/messages.js`, `static/ui.js`). So between page load and the settings fetch resolving, `window._busyInputMode` was `undefined` ΓåÆ every send defaulted to `queue`. Saving from the panel set the global synchronously, which is exactly why "re-save fixes it". The window is widened on slow/contended environments like WSL2 (#5132).

## Fix

Give `window._busyInputMode` a **deterministic value at `boot.js` script top**, read synchronously from a localStorage mirror (`hermes-busy-input-mode`) ΓÇö mirroring how `hermes-lang` / `hermes-theme` bootstrap from a synchronous source:

- New module-scope helpers in `boot.js`: `_normalizeBusyInputMode` (validates against `{queue, interrupt, steer}`), `_persistBusyInputMode` (writes the mirror, returns the normalized value), `_readPersistedBusyInputMode` (reads + normalizes). Both localStorage accesses are `try/catch`-guarded. The persist/read helpers are exposed on `window`.
- **Eager default** `window._busyInputMode=_readPersistedBusyInputMode()` set at top level, *before* the async `/api/settings` fetch ΓÇö so the very first send after a reload honors the persisted choice.
- The resolved `/api/settings` value now routes through `_persistBusyInputMode(...)`, keeping the mirror in sync and remaining the single source of truth once it resolves.
- The **catch path** now keeps the persisted preference (`_readPersistedBusyInputMode()`) instead of clobbering it to `queue` when the server is unreachable.
- The **panels.js save handler** persists via `_persistBusyInputMode(...)` (typeof-guarded for load-order safety) so the next reload's eager default honors the save.

The defensive `||'queue'` read sites in `messages.js` / `ui.js` are unchanged (belt + braces).

## Tests

- New `tests/test_5167_busy_input_mode_boot.py` (14 tests): pins the eager default is set **before** the async settings fetch, the sync-mirror helpers + guards, every assignment site keeps the mirror in sync, and the read sites remain intact.
- Updated `tests/test_1062_busy_input_modes.py` boot/panels wiring assertions to match the new persist-through-mirror wiring.
- `node --check static/boot.js` and `node --check static/panels.js`: pass.
- `python3 scripts/scope_undef_gate.py .`: **CLEAN** (17 static files, no undefined references).
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_5167_busy_input_mode_boot.py tests/test_1062_busy_input_modes.py`: **42 passed**.

## Manual verification

1. Set Busy input mode to `steer`, save, hard-reload with `/api/settings` throttled (DevTools ΓåÆ Slow 3G).
2. Start a run and send a follow-up before the UI settles ΓåÆ the follow-up now **steers** instead of queueing.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5172.title: fix(webui): render server-initiated turns in a hidden tab without a refresh
nesquena/hermes-webui#5172.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5172.body:
## Problem

A turn started **server-side** ΓÇö self-wake, cron, or a restart hook ΓÇö fans a `server_turn_started` frame onto the per-session live-view SSE channel so an open tab renders it live (the path added in #2968). But while a tab is **hidden**, the WebUI deliberately does **not** hold that persistent per-session SSE open, to stay within the browser's 6-connection-per-origin budget (#3992 / #4151). So at fan-out time `get_session_channel()` returns `None` and the turn is silently dropped for that tab ΓÇö the user only sees it after a manual interaction (refresh / send) re-subscribes the channel and replays it.

Repro: open a session, switch the tab to the background, trigger a server-initiated turn for that session (self-wake / cron). Nothing renders until you interact with the tab.

## Fix

Bridge the hidden window with a **lightweight poll** of `/api/session/status` ΓÇö one short GET per ~6s tick, **not** a held connection, so the connection-pool budget the hidden guard protects is preserved. When the poll sees a live active stream it attaches the existing renderer via the reconnecting/replay path (the turn is already mid-flight), then stops.

**Backend** (`api/session_ops.py`):
- `session_status()` now exposes `active_stream_id`, derived through a new `_live_active_stream_id()` helper that returns the id **only when the stream is genuinely live** (present in `STREAMS` / `ACTIVE_RUNS`). A stale id left by a crashed/restarted run surfaces as `None`, so the poller never attaches a renderer to a dead stream. Additive field; existing consumers ignore it.

**Frontend** (`static/messages.js`):
- `_startHiddenActiveStreamPoll` / `_stopHiddenActiveStreamPoll` / `_attachServerInitiatedStream` implement the poll lifecycle. It fires one immediate tick on hide (catches an already-running turn without waiting a full interval), attaches mid-flight turns as replay, and stops on re-show (the real SSE takes over again), on session switch, and once a stream is already rendering.
- Started on **both** ways a tab ends up hidden with a session: the `visibilitychange` hook's hidden branch (a visible tab going to the background) and `startSessionStream`'s hidden early-return skip (a session opened while already hidden). The visible path and `stopSessionStream` clear it.

## Tests

- `tests/test_hidden_tab_server_initiated_turn.py` (new): backend live-validation (stale id ΓåÆ `None`; an id present in `STREAMS`/`ACTIVE_RUNS` is returned) and frontend source locks for the poll lifecycle, both-hidden-paths start, replay-attach, and teardown-on-session-switch.
- `tests/test_issue3996_sse_visibility.py`: widened the brittle fixed-width source-window slices (1600/1700 ΓåÆ 2400) so the existing `visibilitychange` / hidden-skip assertions still find their markers after the poll-start lines were inserted into `startSessionStream`. No behavior assertions changed.

Local: `node --check static/messages.js` clean; 95 passed across the new test plus the SSE-visibility / PWA-focus / liveview-perf / live-to-final-anchor suites.

I also verified the full path live on the running source build with Playwright: hid the tab (SSE closed, poll started + immediate tick), fired an external turn, and confirmed the poll detected the live stream and attached the renderer (`recovered=true`) with zero interaction ΓÇö console trace showed `ATTACH` + `LIVESTREAM` for the exact external `stream_id`.
