nesquena/hermes-webui#5178.title: test: de-flake test_skills_stats_cache mtime race
nesquena/hermes-webui#5178.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5178.body:
## Problem

`tests/test_profile_skills_stats.py::test_skills_stats_cache` is an **order-dependent flake**: it passes in isolation but fails intermittently under full-suite ordering. It has been observed failing across multiple unrelated PRs' gate runs (it adds noise to every full-suite run), always passing on an isolated re-run.

## Root cause

The test verifies the #4783 behavior that adding a skill bumps the skills-dir mtime, so the cheap per-call mtime probe in `_get_profile_skills_stats` recomputes counts on the next call instead of serving the cached value:

```python
_write_skill(tmp_path, "alpha")
profiles._get_profile_skills_stats(tmp_path)   # caches (enabled=1, probe=mtime_A)
_write_skill(tmp_path, "beta")
enabled, compat = profiles._get_profile_skills_stats(tmp_path)
assert enabled == 2 and compat == 2            # ΓåÉ flakes here
```

The probe (`_skill_tree_max_mtime_ns`) keys the cache on the max `st_mtime_ns` across the skills dir. When the two `_write_skill()` calls land inside the **same coarse filesystem mtime tick**, the skills-dir mtime after writing `beta` can be byte-identical to the value cached after `alpha`. The probe then sees "no change", serves the stale count of `1`, and `assert enabled == 2` fails. Under full-suite timing the window shifts, which is why it's intermittent rather than deterministic.

## Fix

After writing the second skill, force the skills-dir mtime strictly forward so the probe is guaranteed to detect a genuine mtime change:

```python
_write_skill(tmp_path, "beta")
import os as _os, time as _time
_skills_dir = tmp_path / "skills"
_future = _time.time() + 5
_os.utime(_skills_dir, (_future, _future))
enabled, compat = profiles._get_profile_skills_stats(tmp_path)
assert enabled == 2 and compat == 2
```

This mirrors what a real FS-backed skill-add does (advance the dir mtime) and keeps the assertion honest ΓÇö it still proves recompute-on-mtime-change. Only the race against filesystem mtime granularity is removed. No production code changes.

## Verification

- `test_skills_stats_cache` run 8├ù in isolation, the full file 5├ù on a clean master base: **all green, deterministic.**
- Test-only change; no behavior change to `api/profiles.py`.

Found while running the full suite as part of an independent deep-gate pass; filing the de-flake separately so it lands cleanly on its own.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5179.title: [security] fix(file-manager): enforce active profile for session workspaces
nesquena/hermes-webui#5179.author: Hinotoi-agent
nesquena/hermes-webui#5179.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes WebUI profiles are used to separate sessions, workspaces, and profile-owned state.
- Session export already treats a session whose stored `profile` does not match the active profile as not found.
- The file manager used the same caller-controlled `session_id` to resolve a workspace, but it did not apply the active-profile check before serving files.
- This PR puts the profile check into the shared file-session resolver so read/download/mutation file routes inherit one boundary.

## Summary

This PR hardens the file-manager session boundary so WebUI sessions must belong to the active profile before their workspace can be browsed or mutated.

- Rejects a WebUI session from another profile before returning it to file-manager handlers.
- Keeps the existing state.db / external-session fallback for sessions that do not have a WebUI sidecar.
- Adds regression coverage for both the helper-level authorization failure and a route-level `/api/file` denial.

## Security issues covered

| Issue | Impact | Severity |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Cross-profile file-manager access by `session_id` | A request under one active profile could use a known session id from another profile to read or modify files in that session's workspace. | Moderate |

## Before this PR

- `get_session_for_file_ops()` returned a WebUI session from `get_session(sid, metadata_only=True)` without checking its stored `profile`.
- File-manager routes then used `Path(s.workspace)` for read/download/mutation operations.
- Profile-aware routes such as session export already rejected the same cross-profile session id, so the boundary was enforced inconsistently.

## After this PR

- WebUI sessions returned to file-manager handlers must satisfy `_profiles_match(session.profile, get_active_profile_name())`.
- A found-but-foreign WebUI sidecar is treated as not found and does not fall through to state.db fallback.
- Existing state.db-only external session behavior is preserved for sessions that do not have a WebUI sidecar.
- Tests cover default-profile access to a named-profile workspace returning 404 without leaking marker content.

## Why It Matters

Hermes WebUI workspaces can contain user files, generated artifacts, and project context. Profile isolation should apply to direct file APIs just as it does to session export and profile-scoped session lists. Without this check, a stale or known session id can cross from one active profile into another profile's workspace file surface.

## Attack flow

```text
Known or retained named-profile session_id
    -> file-manager route such as GET /api/file?session_id=...&path=...
        -> get_session_for_file_ops returns the foreign WebUI session
            -> route reads Path(session.workspace) without a profile check
                -> cross-profile workspace file disclosure or mutation
```

## Affected code

| Issue | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Cross-profile file-manager access | `api/models.py`, `tests/test_file_manager_external_session.py` |

## Root cause

Cross-profile file-manager access:
- Direct cause: `get_session_for_file_ops()` returned WebUI sessions by id without applying the active-profile predicate used by other session routes.
- Boundary failure: the shared file-manager resolver treated existence of a session id as sufficient authority to access that session's workspace.

## CVSS assessment

| Issue | CVSS v3.1 | Vector |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Cross-profile file-manager access | 6.5 Medium | `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N` |

Rationale:
- This requires an admitted WebUI caller/profile context and knowledge of a session id, but it can expose files from another profile's workspace and may reach file mutation routes that use the same resolver.

## Safe reproduction steps

1. Create or simulate a WebUI session whose stored `profile` is a named profile such as `research`, with a workspace file containing a harmless marker.
2. Make the active request profile `default`.
3. Request `GET /api/file?session_id=<foreign-session>&path=<marker-file>`.
4. Before this PR, the route returns `200` and includes the marker content. After this PR, it returns `404` and does not include the marker.

## Expected vulnerable behavior

- A named-profile workspace marker should never be returned to a different active profile.
- The pre-patch route returned the marker through the file API even though profile matching returned false.
- The fixed route returns the same not-found behavior as the profile-aware session export path.

## Changes in this PR

- Adds active-profile validation to `get_session_for_file_ops()` for WebUI sessions.
- Treats found-but-foreign WebUI sessions as unauthorized/not found instead of falling through to external session fallback.
- Adds regression tests for foreign-profile helper rejection and route-level file-read denial.
- Keeps the existing state.db fallback tests passing for external sessions.

## Files changed

| Category | Files | What changed |
|----------|-------|--------------|
| Backend authorization | `api/models.py` | Enforces active-profile matching before returning WebUI sessions to file-manager handlers. |
| Regression tests | `tests/test_file_manager_external_session.py` | Covers same-profile passthrough, foreign-profile rejection, no fallback on authorization failure, and route-level 404 behavior. |

## Maintainer impact

- The diff is intentionally small and localized to the file-manager session resolver and its existing regression file.
- File path containment, upload handling, frontend behavior, and session export behavior are not changed.
- External state.db-only sessions still use the existing fallback path when no WebUI sidecar exists.

## Fix rationale

The file-manager resolver is the right choke point because all file-manager handlers already route through it. Enforcing the profile check there keeps sibling read/download/mutation routes aligned and avoids duplicating authorization logic in each handler.

## Type of change

- [x] Security fix
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor with no behavior change

## Verification

- [x] `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_file_manager_external_session.py`
- [x] `./.venv/bin/python -m py_compile api/models.py tests/test_file_manager_external_session.py`
- [x] `./.venv/bin/ruff check tests/test_file_manager_external_session.py`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Docker/container validation with `python:3.11-slim`: copied the mounted repo into `/work`, ran the focused test file, compiled touched Python files, and ran `git diff --check`.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- This intentionally returns not-found for foreign-profile WebUI sessions to match existing profile-scoped routes.
- If maintainers want a different external-session policy for state.db-backed sessions, that can be handled separately; this PR preserves the current fallback behavior when no WebUI sidecar exists.

## Disclosure notes

- Claims are bounded to the file-manager resolver and routes that depend on it.
- No production data or real secrets were used in validation.
- No unrelated files are changed.

## Model Used

AI-assisted with OpenAI GPT-5.5 through Hermes Agent. Tool use included local code inspection, focused tests, Docker validation, and GitHub CLI operations.

- #4958 made settled mixed `content[]` turns feed the Stable Assistant Turn Anchor scene model.

- The test covers process prose, thinking/reasoning, a tool start + tool completion collapsed into completed tool semantics, post-tool process prose, terminal status preservation, and final-answer separation.

## Why It Matters

This gives the Anchor effort a concrete replay/runtime-journal parity guard before any future fallback shrink/removal. It proves the live recovery snapshot and settled read-side hydration agree on the user-visible activity timeline for a representative tool-bearing turn, while keeping #4932-style raw `content[]` behavior as historical/non-anchor fallback.

## Contract Routing

- Contract family: Stable Assistant Turn Anchor / Live-to-Final assistant reply lifecycle / runtime-journal replay.
- Product-semantics tests touched: `tests/test_anchor_scene_persistence.py`.
- Contract change type: test-only invariant; no runtime behavior change.
- Evidence: focused parity test compares the real `_run_journal_live_snapshot` and `_hydrate_anchor_activity_scenes` backend paths.

## Verification

nesquena/hermes-webui#5189.title: fix(webui): keep stale transcript mounted while hidden-tab return reloads new messages (#5177)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5189.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5189.body:
Fixes #5177.

## Problem

After a hidden interval that added real persisted messages (post-turn `bg-review` thread writes `skill_manage`/`memory`, a sibling tab adds, the just-finished main turn flushes), switching the tab back caused the **entire transcript to visibly blank for the round-trip and then reappear** on the source WebUI. The user-reported field repro is in #5177 (`<session>`, `a local LAN client`, a source clone with #5061 and #5122 verified loaded).

## Why neither #5061 nor #5122 caught it

| Fix | Why it didn't apply |
|---|---|
| **#5061** (metadata-only short-circuit) | Only avoids the destructive reload when `remoteCount === localCount && remoteLast > localLast`. Hidden-window-added messages have `remoteCount > localCount` ΓåÆ falls through to the destructive `loadSession(force)` branch. |
| **#5122** (SSE 4-probe staged retry) | When the SSE error arrives while `visibility_state='hidden'`, `_deferStreamErrorIfPageHidden` returns **before** the `_reconnectAttempted` block; the 4-probe never runs. |

`static/sessions.js` itself warns about exactly this disappear/reappear pattern in the inline comment at the top of the `remoteCount`/`remoteLast` guard ΓÇö but only short-circuits the metadata-only branch. The user-visible blank on the count-changed branch is the gap #5177 documents.

## Fix

Keep the stale transcript mounted while the recovery reload runs, then swap the new transcript into place atomically. Three small, additive changes:

1. **`refreshActiveSessionIfExternallyUpdated`** maps the visibility/focus recovery reasons (`{visible, focus}`) to a new `keepStaleUntilLoaded` option, forwarded to `loadSession`. The post-stream idle reconcile and the poll / external-imported-session paths keep their existing behaviour (the design comment captures the rationale).

2. **`loadSession`** ANDs `opts.keepStaleUntilLoaded` with `sameSessionForceReload` (so cross-session switches still clear synchronously ΓÇö leaving a prior session's transcript on screen during a real navigation is the original bug the clear was written for) and, on that path, **skips the synchronous `S.messages` / `S.toolCalls` / `_messagesTruncated` / `_oldestIdx` clear**. The new transcript is **SWAPPED** into `S.messages` by `_ensureMessagesLoaded(sid, {force:true})` so the user sees old DOM directly replaced by new DOM in a single render frame.

3. **`_ensureMessagesLoaded`** grows an `opts.force` escape hatch so its `"messages already populated"` early-return cannot skip the swap when stale messages are still in place.

## Verification

### Source-lock tests

- **New**: `tests/test_issue5177_hidden_tab_blank_gap.py` (7 cases) ΓÇö locks the keep-stale guard shape, the recovery-reason map, the `_ensureMessagesLoaded` `opts.force` escape hatch, and that the synchronous clear is wrapped in `if (!_keepStaleUntilLoaded)`. Also asserts `'poll'` / `'idle-reconcile'` are **not** in the recovery-reason map (so any accidental widening trips the lock).
- **Updated**: `tests/test_webui_external_refresh_frontend.py` and `tests/test_tars_scroll_reset_regressions.py` ΓÇö their anchor strings contained the literal `loadSession` call signature, updated to match the new `keepStaleUntilLoaded:_keepStaleUntilLoaded` form. No behavioural assertions changed.

### Live verification on a source build of nesquena/hermes-webui at HEAD

Reproduced and verified end-to-end with Playwright on the affected session that originated #5177:

nesquena/hermes-webui#5196.title: fix: retry os.replace() on Windows WinError 5 (PermissionError)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5196.author: silent-reader-cn
nesquena/hermes-webui#5196.body:
## Summary

Fixes `[WinError 5] Access is denied` errors that intermittently break WebUI session persistence on Windows, where `os.replace()` can fail if the target file is momentarily locked by another process (antivirus scanner, browser polling, file indexer).

## Root Cause

`api/models.py` performs atomic session writes via `os.replace(tmp, final)`. On Windows, the target file can be locked for brief windows by external processes; when that happens `os.replace()` raises `PermissionError` (WinError 5 / `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) and the entire save fails. Users see an opaque traceback and session data does not persist.

## Fix

Add a small `_safe_replace(src, dst)` helper that wraps `os.replace()` with **exponential-backoff retries on `PermissionError`** on Windows:

- **5 attempts**, **50 ms ΓåÆ 100 ΓåÆ 200 ΓåÆ 400 ΓåÆ 800 ms** backoff
- Re-raises after the final attempt (no swallowed exceptions)
- Thin one-shot wrapper (no sleep) on non-Windows platforms

Replaces all 5 `os.replace()` call sites in `api/models.py`:

| Site | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Session.save()` (main) | Primary session JSON write |
| `Session.save()` (backup) | Backup copy write |
| `_write_session_index()` (full rebuild) | Index file rebuild |
| `_write_session_index()` (fast path) | Index file incremental write |
| `prune_session_from_index()` | Index entry removal |

## Repro (before fix)

1. Run WebUI on Windows with Defender real-time protection enabled.
2. Open a session and start editing.
3. Periodically observe in logs:
   ```
   [WinError 5] µïÆτ╗¥Φ«┐Θù«πÇé: '...sessions\<id>.tmp.<pid>.<tid>' -> '...sessions\<id>.json'
   ```

## Test Plan

- [x] `git apply` of this patch is clean against current `master`.
- [x] All 5 `os.replace()` sites in current `master` are covered (verified by counting call sites pre/post).
- [ ] CI green on Windows + non-Windows jobs.
- [ ] Manual: trigger Defender scan during save, confirm no traceback.

## Notes

- Behaviour change is **strictly on Windows** (`os.name == 'nt'`). Linux/macOS behaviour is unchanged.
- Final-attempt re-raise preserves the original error path ΓÇö no silent failure.
- No new dependencies; no API changes.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5198.title: fix(auth): enforce active-profile session IDs
nesquena/hermes-webui#5198.author: starship-s
nesquena/hermes-webui#5198.body:
## Thinking Path

- Profile-scoped session reads already hide sessions that belong to a different active profile, but several request paths still accepted a request-supplied `session_id` and loaded or mutated that session directly.
- That mismatch made the profile boundary depend on which route was called: detail reads returned `404`, while duplicate/delete/file/upload/chat-start paths could reach the foreign sidecar first.
- The narrow fix is to enforce the same active-profile visibility check at the HTTP request boundary for normal query/body `session_id` inputs, then keep explicit route-level handling only where ownership is created or retagged intentionally.
- Multipart uploads need their own check because they parse `session_id` from form fields before the normal JSON-body preflight can run.
- `POST /api/chat/start` remains special: persisted foreign sessions now 404 before a run can start, while empty placeholders can only be retagged when the requested profile matches the server-selected active profile.

## What Changed

- Added a shared request preflight in `api/routes.py` that checks query/body `session_id` values against the active profile before normal API route dispatch.
- Applied the same `404 Session not found` response shape used by `GET /api/session` for foreign-profile session references.
- Preserved explicit exemptions for import/claim routes and `chat/start`, where the route has additional ownership or placeholder-retag rules.
- Added multipart-upload visibility checks in `api/upload.py` before attachment writes, archive extraction, or workspace resolution.
- Added regression coverage for duplicate, file read, chat start, empty-placeholder retagging, and all three upload handlers.
- Updated existing status/profile-switch coverage so profile-specific status and placeholder retagging are exercised under the matching active-profile context.

## Why It Matters

- Keeps the WebUI profile boundary consistent across read, write, destructive, and upload routes.
- Prevents request-supplied ids from becoming a cross-profile access or write primitive.
- Avoids leaking whether a foreign session exists by returning the same 404 shape as a missing session.
- Preserves legitimate import and empty-placeholder flows instead of blocking them with an overly broad guard.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5201.title: Reduce false Connection Lost flapping under large session state
nesquena/hermes-webui#5201.author: franksong2702
nesquena/hermes-webui#5201.body:
## Thinking Path

- #5132 removed the worst `/api/sessions` `state.db` override bottleneck, but large long-lived installs can still hit false `Connection Lost` flapping when active streams, sidebar refreshes, and session detail loads overlap.
- The failure mode is connection pressure and slow recovery, not a real stopped Hermes run: the browser can run out of same-origin HTTP/1.1 headroom while `/api/sessions` or `/api/session` requests are still waiting.
- This follow-up keeps the UI responsive under that pressure by returning safe stale sidebar data immediately, reducing duplicate same-session SSE sockets during a live turn, and making the offline banner less eager to claim the server is gone.

## What Changed

- Return age-stale `/api/sessions` cache immediately and rebuild it in a background singleflight owner, while rebuilding source-changed stale cache synchronously for the owner so committed external state is visible right away.
- Log and release the singleflight owner if that background rebuild raises, so a failed rebuild does not pin future requests behind a dead owner.
- Suspend `/api/session/stream` while the same session already has an active `/api/chat/stream`, then resume it only if that session is still current and no chat stream is active.
- Keep the longer session-list timeout/retry scoped to the first sidebar boot load, leave warm/streaming sidebar polls single-shot, and reduce active-stream sidebar polling from 5s to 30s.
- Give large transcript loads a 120s timeout, matching the observed power-user state where a session detail fetch can legitimately exceed the generic API timeout.
- Gate fetch-triggered offline banners behind two failed health probes while preserving immediate handling for browser-reported offline/startup paths.

## Why It Matters

Power-user installs with multi-GB `state.db` files can still have Hermes runs progressing normally while the WebUI shows `Connection Lost` or fails to load a clicked session. This narrows that gap: the sidebar keeps painting cached data, active turns use fewer browser connection slots, and transient fetch/probe failures no longer immediately turn into a full-page offline warning.

Follow-up to #5132. Related connection-pool context: #4151.

## Verification

- `node --check static/messages.js && node --check static/sessions.js && python3 -m py_compile api/routes.py api/route_session_list_cache.py`
- `python3 scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff origin/master` ΓÇö no new violations on added/modified lines
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_session_channel_option_x.py tests/test_issue3996_sse_visibility.py tests/test_issue4151_pwa_focus_sse.py tests/test_api_timeout.py tests/test_offline_banner.py tests/test_4170_offline_probe.py tests/test_offline_soft_recovery.py tests/test_session_sidebar_resilience.py tests/test_issue856_background_completion_unread.py tests/test_session_sidebar_cache.py tests/test_issue4759_parallel_sidebar_boot_fetch.py tests/test_performance_polling_hardening.py tests/test_webui_state_db_reconciliation.py` ΓÇö 161 passed
- `node --check static/messages.js && node --check static/sessions.js && node --check static/ui.js`
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_session_sidebar_cache.py tests/test_session_channel_option_x.py tests/test_api_timeout.py tests/test_offline_banner.py tests/test_session_sidebar_resilience.py` ΓÇö 71 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_session_channel_option_x.py tests/test_issue3996_sse_visibility.py tests/test_issue4151_pwa_focus_sse.py tests/test_api_timeout.py tests/test_offline_banner.py tests/test_4170_offline_probe.py tests/test_offline_soft_recovery.py tests/test_session_sidebar_resilience.py tests/test_issue856_background_completion_unread.py tests/test_session_sidebar_cache.py` ΓÇö 116 passed
- Local runtime sanity before the final patch: after restarting the affected 8787 instance, `/api/sessions` returned in ~0.34s instead of timing out behind the earlier pile-up.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- During an active stream, sidebar refresh polling is intentionally less frequent. The tradeoff is lower connection pressure at the cost of slower passive cross-window/sidebar freshness while a turn is running. Warm polls also stay single-shot to avoid doubling request pressure on an already overloaded server.
- The stale sidebar cache can briefly show previous data while the background rebuild catches up, but this is preferable to blocking the active request and surfacing false offline state.
- No tracked docs were changed; this is release-note-worthy behavior, so the notes above are intended for the release workflow rather than editing `CHANGELOG.md` directly.

Touched areas: `/api/sessions` cache behavior, session-scoped SSE lifecycle, active-stream sidebar polling, offline recovery banner gating, large session detail load timeout.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5204.title: fix(redaction): memoize deterministic API response redactor to stop GIL-bound poll storms
nesquena/hermes-webui#5204.author: ducnhung70
nesquena/hermes-webui#5204.body:
## Problem

On a single-process WebUI server, repeated dashboard polling of unchanged session payloads pegged one core at ~50ΓÇô57% CPU **even with zero in-flight requests**, and individual `/api/session` responses ballooned to 10ΓÇô44s under concurrent polling. In the browser this surfaced as repeated "connection lost" / reconnect churn.

Root cause: every `/api/session` response runs `redact_session_data()` over the full message history. The combined redactor (`agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text` with `force=True` + the local fallback) is ~15 regex passes per string. It is CPU-bound, so under the GIL it serializes across the `ThreadingHTTPServer` worker threads. Repeated polls re-run the identical redaction over identical, unchanged strings, queueing requests until the browser/reverse-proxy times out ΓÇö which triggers client retries and a thread pileup, feeding back into the stall.

## Fix

The combined redactor is **pure and deterministic** (`force=True`, fixed masking ΓÇö identical input always yields identical output), so memoizing per-string is safe with no invalidation required.

`api/helpers.py`:
- Wrap the built redactor in `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)`.
- Gate per-entry size at 16 KB (`_REDACT_CACHE_MAX_TEXT_LEN`) so a few giant tool-output dumps can't evict the thousands of small recurring strings that actually benefit, or balloon RSS.
- Keep the public `_redact_fn_cached` name as the call target (the redaction test suite monkeypatches it wholesale, so tests bypass the cache and remain unaffected).

The redaction safety boundary is unchanged: the same patterns run on a cache miss, secrets are still masked, and the `api_redact_enabled=false` fast-path is untouched.

## Benchmark

On a representative ~3 KB string containing a credential marker:

| | per call |
|---|---|
| full redact (cache miss) | 3.718 ms |
| cache hit | 0.0020 ms |

~1900x on the repeated-poll path. A large session has hundreds of such strings, which is the difference between the 10ΓÇô44s responses observed and sub-millisecond ones.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_security_redaction.py` ΓåÆ 69 passed, 1 skipped.
- Manual: confirmed cache hits accumulate (`lru_cache` stats), secrets still masked on hit, `>16 KB` strings bypass the cache, and the `api_redact_enabled=false` bypass still returns text unchanged.
- Idle CPU after deploy dropped from ~57% to ~0%.

## Release note

Fix a CPU/latency regression where repeated session polling re-ran the full API-response redactor over unchanged payloads, serializing behind the GIL and surfacing as "connection lost" in the browser. The deterministic redactor is now memoized.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5206.body:
## Thinking Path

- The left sidebar `+` action intentionally reuses an already-empty conversation by focusing the composer instead of creating another empty session.
- That reuse guard only checked session metadata (`message_count === 0`) plus in-flight state.
- If the loaded frontend transcript still contains visible messages while metadata says zero, the guard can misclassify the current pane as reusable-empty.
- The user-visible result is confusing: clicking `+` focuses the composer immediately, but the message pane still shows the previous conversation because `newSession()` never ran.
- This PR makes the reuse guard check the loaded transcript as well as metadata before it takes the focus-only path.

## What Changed

- Added `_currentSessionIsReusableEmptyChat()` in `static/boot.js`.
- Kept the existing zero-message, not-busy, no-active-stream, no-pending-user-message checks.
- Added a loaded-transcript check so the focus-only path is allowed only when `S.messages` has no visible non-tool messages.
- Reused the same helper for both the sidebar `+` click handler and the Cmd/Ctrl+K handler.
- Added regression coverage in `tests/test_issue_new_chat_draft_restore.py`.

## Why It Matters

Clicking `+ / New conversation` should either reuse a genuinely empty conversation or create/switch to a fresh one. It should not focus the composer while leaving an old transcript on screen. This preserves the existing sidebar hygiene behavior from #1171 while preventing the stale-pane misclassification.

This is unrelated to the recent false `Connection Lost` / large `state.db` work; it is a local frontend guard bug in the new-chat interaction path.

## Verification

## Risks / Follow-ups

- The helper treats any loaded non-tool message as visible transcript content. That is intentional for this guard: if the pane has visible chat content, the focus-only new-chat shortcut should not win.
- No visual layout changed, so before/after screenshots were not added; the behavior is covered by the static interaction regression test.
- No docs update needed; this is a narrow interaction bugfix with no new user-facing feature or setup/runtime contract.

## Contract Routing

nesquena/hermes-webui#5207.title: Improve latest assistant response landmark
nesquena/hermes-webui#5207.author: sheldon-im
nesquena/hermes-webui#5207.body:
## Thinking Path

This is a small screen-reader navigation improvement for the settled final assistant response.

The original accessibility problem appears after streaming completes: the live assistant DOM can be replaced by the settled transcript render, and screen-reader users may need a stable way to return to the final response. To keep the state model simple, this PR does not mark the streaming/live assistant turn. It only marks the latest assistant turn during settled transcript rendering.

## What Changed

- Adds a helper that marks one assistant turn as the `Latest Hermes response` region and clears stale latest-response markers.
- Applies that helper from the settled transcript render path only.
- Keeps the transcript container, live assistant turn paths, and older assistant turns out of the landmark list.
- Adds regression coverage that verifies:
  - the transcript container is not a named region,
  - only settled render owns the latest-response landmark,
  - live/restored-live paths do not own the final-response landmark,
  - no generated headings or `tabindex` are introduced.

## Why It Matters

Assistant responses often contain Markdown headings. A response-level landmark gives screen-reader users a stable boundary for the final response while keeping heading navigation available for structure inside the answer.

Keeping the marker final-only also avoids competing ownership between live streaming DOM and the settled transcript render.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_a11y_transcript_landmarks.py`
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_anchor_fallback_ownership.py::test_render_messages_keeps_anchor_owned_turn_out_of_legacy_activity_rebuilds tests/test_issue4793_dom_recycle_hardening.py::test_recycled_assistant_turn_reuse_clears_live_anchor_attrs tests/test_issue4793_dom_recycle_hardening.py::test_recycled_assistant_turn_reuse_keeps_block_clear_and_role_refresh tests/test_a11y_transcript_landmarks.py`
- `node --check static/ui.js`
- `git diff --check`
- `.venv/bin/python scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff upstream/master`

Manual NVDA check on a live patched server before opening the PR: only the latest assistant response was exposed as the `Latest Hermes response` landmark, and it read cleanly. This update narrows the implementation to the settled final render path.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- This intentionally does not provide a landmark for the currently streaming live response. If live-response navigation is useful, it should be designed separately with explicit ownership across live and settled render paths.
- This intentionally does not solve navigation to older assistant responses. That may need a separate design discussion because headings, landmarks, and transcript navigation each have tradeoffs.

## Model Used

OpenAI GPT-5.5 via Hermes Agent, with local shell/git/test tooling.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5215.title: fix(#5210): bound HTTP worker dispatch under reconnect storms
nesquena/hermes-webui#5215.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5215.body:
## Thinking Path

- The server already isolates TLS handshakes and exposes accept-loop heartbeat data, but request dispatch still inherits the stdlib thread-per-request path with no live worker cap.
- The issue's captured stack wedges in `ThreadingMixIn.process_request()` and `Thread.start()`, so the fix belongs in the HTTP shell at `server.py`, before another worker thread is minted.
- The change keeps API and session logic untouched, bounds the hazardous output directly, and turns overload into a recoverable failure surface instead of a full-instance wedge.

## What Changed

- `server.py`: adds a bounded request-worker gate to `QuietHTTPServer`, releases slots on every exit path, and rejects plain-HTTP overflow before another handler thread starts while keeping the fast `503` readable on Windows with bounded cleanup.
- `tests/test_issue5210_http_worker_bound.py`: adds focused loopback regression coverage for overflow rejection, slot release, and healthy in-cap traffic during a held request.

## Why It Matters

A reconnect storm can no longer create thousands of HTTP handler threads until the accept loop stalls. Normal traffic below the cap keeps the existing behavior, while overload gets a fast, recoverable failure instead of bricking the whole instance.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_issue5210_http_worker_bound.py tests/test_issue1458_stability_hardening.py tests/test_issue1855_request_diagnostics.py tests/test_server_port_exclusivity.py -v --timeout=60`

Full-suite CI context: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5210.

Related: #4973 fixed the same thread-exhaustion failure class in request diagnostics, not the HTTP dispatch layer.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5217.title: fix(webui): keep a following reader pinned through streaming growth and SSE recovery
nesquena/hermes-webui#5217.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5217.body:
## Problem

Two related "jump back" reports where a reader who is **following the live stream** gets stranded mid-transcript instead of staying at the bottom. Both reproduced and fixed live (the A/B below was run against a local source build).

### Class 1 ΓÇö content grew beneath a pinned viewport (`static/ui.js` scroll listener)

While streaming on a tall transcript (most visible on mobile, where chunks land fast), new content increases `scrollHeight` under a stationary viewport. The reader never scrolled ΓÇö `top` did not move up and `_messageUserUnpinned` is `false` ΓÇö but `bottomDistance` crosses the `nearBottom` threshold, so the listener fell through to `_scrollPinned=false`, killing auto-follow mid-stream. The follow writer and the scroll listener then fought frame-by-frame: the viewport stalled while content kept growing and was progressively stranded mid-transcript.

### Class 2 ΓÇö SSE-recovery render restores a stale position (`static/messages.js`)

`_handleStreamError` (SSE drop), the Task-cancelled apply + fallback paths, and the reconnect-stream-dead cleanup all push/replace `S.messages` then call `renderMessages({preserveScroll:true})`. `preserveScroll`'s restore path keys on the pre-render snapshot's bottom-distance, which during a live stream can read large (content was still growing under a followed viewport). So on a process restart / SSE drop / cancel it yanked a following reader up to a stale historical position ΓÇö the "everything jumped back" report.

## Fix

**Class 1:** in the `!_messageUserUnpinned` branch, when the viewport did **not** move up and auto-follow is on, keep the pin and re-snap to the true bottom via `_setMessageScrollToBottom()` instead of unpinning. The genuine scroll-away fallthrough (`else { _scrollPinned=false }`) is unchanged, so a real upward scroll still unpins.

**Class 2:** capture follow-intent (`_isMessagePaneNearBottom(1200)`) **before** mutating `S.messages`, and after the recovery render, `scrollToBottom()` if the reader was following ΓÇö so they see the interruption/cancellation notice in place. Readers who had scrolled up to read history are left where they were (the near-bottom guard is false for them). Applied at all four recovery mutation points: SSE-drop notice, Task-cancelled embedded-payload apply, Task-cancelled fallback, and reconnect-stream-dead placeholder cleanup.

## Verification

Behavioral A/B via Playwright, scenario = disconnect/cancel/recovery while the viewport is 400px from bottom (the `>250px` band that triggers `preserveScroll`'s restore path):

| Path | OLD (stranded) | FIX (at bottom) |
|---|---|---|
| Connection interrupted | 582px from bottom | 1px |
| Task cancelled | 523px | 1px |
| Reconnect-stream-dead | 523px | 1px |
| Content-grew pinned (200-line stream) | stalled, progressively stranded | stays pinned at bottom |

Structural source-locks in `tests/test_sse_recovery_scroll_stranding.py` (4 follow-intent guards + the content-grew re-snap ordering). Local run green: 27 passed across the new file + `test_issue4295_midstream_scroll_anchor.py` + `test_issue4856_android_scroll_regression.py`.

Pure-additive: `git diff origin/master` is +53 lines, 0 deletions in the two JS files.

## Release v0.51.743 ΓÇö server-initiated turns render in a hidden tab (#5172, @allenliang2022)

Ships **#5172** by @allenliang2022. **Maintainer-approved** (Nathan signed off after fresh gate).

### The bug
A server-side-started turn (self-wake / cron / restart hook) fans a `server_turn_started` frame onto the per-session live-view SSE channel. But while a tab is HIDDEN, the WebUI deliberately drops that persistent per-session SSE (the per-origin connection budget, #3992/#3996), so `get_session_channel()` returns None at fan-out time ΓÇö the turn is silently dropped for that tab until a manual refresh/send re-subscribes.

`_live_active_stream_id(session)` (api/session_ops.py) returns the active stream id ONLY if it's live in `config.STREAMS`/`ACTIVE_RUNS` (no ghost id). A lightweight `/api/session/status` poll in a hidden tab detects a genuinely in-flight server turn and attaches the existing live renderer via `_attachServerInitiatedStream` ΓåÆ `attachLiveStream({reconnecting:true})`, idempotency-guarded, torn down on re-show / session switch / stop. +280/-2, 4 files (session_ops.py + messages.js + 2 tests).

- PR's own tests: 11 passed.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5221.body:
## Release v0.51.745 ΓÇö stream-end worklog collapse fixes for pinned readers (#5058, #4970, @allenliang2022)

Ships **#5058** by @allenliang2022. **Maintainer-approved.** This was a contributor-court PR that converged (the 06-27 bounce fix-spec was answered) and then grew one more sub-fix; re-gated fully this session.

### The bug (#4970 family)
Two stream-end (`STREAM_DONE`) cases shrank the transcript by hundreds of px in one frame, so the browser clamped a bottom-pinned viewport backward (the "jump back" report):
1. The just-streamed live worklog collapsing into its compact settled form.
2. A turn that streamed only prose (long plain answer, or a degeneration burst) being promoted into a collapsed worklog despite having no tool/thinking work ΓÇö hiding the whole answer.

### The fix
1. **One-shot keep-open token:** for a pinned follower, the just-settled worklog is kept open (height-stable) via a token scoped to that single stream id ΓÇö armed at STREAM_DONE, disarmed right after the render. Historical worklogs still collapse compact on later pinned re-renders; unpinned readers always get the compact settled worklog.
2. **Worklog-worthiness predicate:** a turn whose activity rows are all prose/terminal is never promoted to a worklog (requires ΓëÑ1 tool/thinking row or a compression card), enforced at BOTH the generation gate (messages.js) and render gate (ui.js, defense-in-depth).
+343/-3, 4 files (ui.js + messages.js + 2 tests).

nesquena/hermes-webui#5223.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5223.body:
## Release v0.51.747 ΓÇö Windows-safe os.replace retry on session saves (#5196, @silent-reader-cn)

Ships **#5196** by @silent-reader-cn. **Reliability fix** (Windows).

### The bug
On Windows, `os.replace()` raises `WinError 5` (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, surfaced as Python `PermissionError`) when the target session JSON / index file is momentarily locked by another process ΓÇö an antivirus scanner, the browser polling the file, etc. That could abort a session save.

### The fix
A new `_safe_replace(src, dst)` helper wraps all 5 session-state `os.replace()` call sites (session index ├ù3, backup, main save). On Windows it retries `PermissionError` with exponential backoff (50 ΓåÆ 100 ΓåÆ 200 ΓåÆ 400 ms, 5 attempts), then re-raises if still failing (no silent success on a save path). Non-Windows platforms are byte-identical to before (single attempt, no delay ΓÇö `os.name != 'nt'` passthrough). `api/models.py` only.

### Gate (this session)
- **Codex (reproduce): SAFE TO SHIP** (per the gate-certifier cert, head `353f548c`) ΓÇö retry behavior verified 5/5 empirically; the implementation is correct, safe, well-scoped.
- **Auto-fix applied:** the gate-fail was a process blocker, not logic ΓÇö non-trivial retry logic shipped with no test (AGENTS.md requires one). Added `tests/test_issue5196_windows_safe_replace.py` (5 tests: posix passthrough / Windows retry-then-succeed / reraise-after-5 / no-retry-on-non-PermissionError / 50-100-200-400ms backoff sequence). Non-vacuous (mocks `os.replace`, asserts attempt counts + delays). 5/5 pass.
- Ruff forward-gate CLEAN; **full suite 11038 passed** (only the 2 pre-existing cron-isolation flakes ΓÇö unrelated).

nesquena/hermes-webui#5226.title: Release v0.51.748 ΓÇö bound HTTP worker dispatch under reconnect storms (#5215, @rodboev)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5226.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5226.body:
## Release v0.51.748 ΓÇö bound HTTP worker dispatch under reconnect storms (#5215, @rodboev)

Ships **#5215** by @rodboev, fixing **#5210**. **Reliability / anti-wedge fix** (server.py).

### The bug
The stdlib `ThreadingMixIn` HTTP server mints a worker thread per request with no live cap. A reconnect storm (flaky network, client retry loop) piles up threads and wedges the whole instance ΓÇö the captured stack in #5210 sits in `ThreadingMixIn.process_request()` / `Thread.start()`.

### The fix
Request dispatch is bounded by a `BoundedSemaphore` worker-slot cap:
- Requests above the cap get a fast `503 Service Unavailable` (input drained non-blocking, socket closed cleanly, via a separately-bounded reject path) instead of spawning unbounded threads.
- Every worker slot is released in a `finally` after `process_request_thread` ΓÇö and on thread-start failure ΓÇö so a handler exception or dropped connection can't leak capacity (no slow brick).
- Normal below-cap load is byte-identical to the stdlib path; TLS-handshake isolation preserved; RLIMIT_NOFILE raised best-effort for persistent hosts.
`server.py` +474/-133 + test.

### Gate (this session ΓÇö high blast radius, gated thoroughly)
- **Codex (reproduce): SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö verified the worker slot is acquired non-blocking before dispatch (`server.py:262`) and **released in `finally`** after `process_request_thread` (`:273`), released+closed on thread-start failure (`:268`), and the overflow path always closes+releases (`:247`). No slot leak, no deadlock between the worker and reject semaphores.
- PR's own tests 7/7 pass in isolation (incl. the slot-release-after-finish test); an earlier single failure was a confirmed timing flake under concurrent-suite CPU contention, green on every clean re-run. Codex's shard check passed.
- `server.py` parses; **full suite green** (only the 2 pre-existing cron-isolation flakes ΓÇö unrelated).

nesquena/hermes-webui#5228.title: feat(#4747): add opt-in extension loopback proxy
nesquena/hermes-webui#5228.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5228.body:
## Thinking Path

- Extensions already declare trusted loopback sidecars, but they still need a same-origin bridge when direct browser calls run into CORS or host-local networking limits.
- The security boundary belongs in one owner, so manifest parsing, consent persistence, status payloads, route resolution, and Settings rendering all consume the same sidecar eligibility decision from `api/extensions.py`.
- The proxy stays intentionally narrow: fixed per-extension path, manifest-declared loopback origin only, explicit per-origin consent, no ambient proxy egress, no WebUI credential forwarding, browser `GET` traffic only when the request proves same-origin provenance, and bounded upstream reads so a consented sidecar cannot exhaust a worker.

## What Changed

- `api/extensions.py`: added shared sidecar proxy consent persistence, public proxy status metadata, shared target resolution, fail-closed handling for malformed consent state, and encoded proxy-path preservation so `%2F` stays encoded when it reaches the sidecar.
- `api/routes.py`: added the fixed `/api/extensions/<id>/sidecar/*` proxy route and `/api/extensions/sidecar-proxy-consent`, kept redirects on the declared origin, preserved non-sensitive request headers, stripped connection-bound hop-by-hop headers, disabled ambient HTTP(S) proxy egress, required `Origin` or `Referer` when `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` asserts browser provenance, and capped upstream response bodies at 512 KB on both success and `HTTPError` paths.
- `static/panels.js`: surfaced proxy consent state in Settings, added approve/revoke controls, and kept direct sidecar health checks credentialless and outside the proxy path.
- `tests/test_extension_sidecar_proxy.py`: covered route, resolver, consent, malformed-state, redirect, ambient-proxy, provenance, header-isolation, oversized upstream bodies, and encoded proxy-path preservation.
- `tests/test_extension_status_endpoint.py`: covered sanitized proxy metadata, consent persistence, origin-change reconsent, and fail-closed extension state handling.
- `tests/test_extensions_settings_panel.py`: covered proxy status rendering, consent POST wiring, and the updated docs contract.
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`: documented the additive opt-in proxy contract, the fixed per-extension path, credential stripping, and the continued Tier B backend-route boundary.

## Why It Matters

This gives an extension frontend a same-origin path to its own approved local sidecar without widening WebUI into a generic extension backend. The reviewed branch now also closes the security edges around origin changes, malformed persisted consent, ambient proxy configuration, hop-by-hop header leakage, cross-site browser navigation, and oversized sidecar responses.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_extension_sidecar_proxy.py -v --timeout=60` (`18 passed`)
- `pytest tests/test_extension_status_endpoint.py tests/test_extensions_settings_panel.py -v --timeout=60` (`60 passed`)

Full-suite CI context, not a local requirement for this slice: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`

## Upstream

Closes #4747.

Design context comes from #4747, which tracks hermes-webui-extensions#5 and the original Templates extension CORS need.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5238.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5238.body:
## Release v0.51.756 ΓÇö collapse post-restart config reload stampede (#5235, @rodboev)

Ships **#5235** by @rodboev, fixing **#5220**. Reliability/concurrency fix on the config owner.

### The problem
Right after a restart (or profile switch), several in-flight requests could all see the config cache as stale and each enter `reload_config()` to re-parse `config.yaml` at once ΓÇö a thundering-herd re-parse that briefly stalls the single-process server.

### The fix
- Extracts the lock-holding cache mutation into `_refresh_config_cache()` (callers hold `_cfg_lock`).
- Adds `reload_config_if_stale()` which acquires `_cfg_lock` then **re-checks staleness inside the lock** (double-checked locking), so N concurrent stale readers collapse to a single refresh.
- `get_config()`'s stale path routes through the gate instead of an unconditional `reload_config()`.
- Forced reloads (writes, profile switches) and the in-memory-override guard keep their existing semantics.
api/config.py +250/-69 + tests/test_issue5220_config_reload_stampede.py.

### Gate (full ΓÇö config owner, concurrency-critical)
- **Codex (reproduce): SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö verified the inner re-check under `_cfg_lock` (config.py:444-454) doesn't skip a genuinely-stale reload nor redo a refresh that already happened, preserves the in-memory-override guard on both checks, keeps forced `reload_config()` semantics for write/profile paths (called outside the lock ΓÇö no deadlock/re-entrancy), and retains the #798 TLS env-pin + #4652 mtime-keyed parse cache.
- 3 stampede + 6 mtime-cache + 18 model-refresh tests pass; 777 config/reload/profile/settings tests pass.
- **Full suite: 11071 passed** (only the 2 pre-existing cron-isolation flakes ΓÇö unrelated, they fail on clean master too).

Closes #5235. Fixes #5220.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5240.title: fix(chat): preserve visible transcript on terminal stream failure (#5224)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5240.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5240.body:
## Thinking Path

- The issue is not "provider failures look ugly"; it is that a terminal failure can make the active pane forget transcript rows the browser already had.
- The live replacement seam is client-side: `_handleStreamError()` appends the inline marker, then `_restoreSettledSession()` can still replace the pane from fetched `session.messages`.
- The fix therefore belongs in transcript reconciliation, with a regression harness that proves shorter stale snapshots stop replacing richer visible history without preserving unrelated later tails from older terminal markers.

## What Changed

- `static/messages.js`: preserve the richer visible transcript only when terminal recovery fetches a stale shorter snapshot that is still a prefix of the visible pane and the visible pane currently ends in the terminal marker, so older historical markers cannot preserve unrelated later live text.
- `tests/test_issue5224_terminal_error_transcript_preserve.py`: add behavioral regressions for stale shorter restores, authoritative shorter replacements, and the historical-marker negative-space case.
- `tests/test_live_stream_ux.py`, `tests/test_offline_banner.py`, and `tests/test_live_to_final_anchor_visible_order.py`: refresh source-shape guards to the helper-based restore and terminal-marker call sites the final branch now uses.
- `tests/test_session_rotate_url_sync.py` and `tests/test_1694_terminal_cleanup_ownership.py`: refresh two additional static guard tests so CI tracks the option-bearing restore call shape and the widened settled-restore block after the terminal-tail guard landed.

## Why It Matters

When a terminal stream failure happens late in a long run, users keep the transcript they were already reading instead of seeing it collapse into an error-only view. At the same time, legitimate shorter authoritative settlements still replace stale live fragments, an old interruption marker from a previous turn can no longer pin unrelated later text in place, and the static guard coverage now follows the real restore/error call shapes the branch ships.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_session_rotate_url_sync.py tests/test_1694_terminal_cleanup_ownership.py tests/test_issue5224_terminal_error_transcript_preserve.py tests/test_live_stream_ux.py tests/test_offline_banner.py tests/test_live_to_final_anchor_visible_order.py -v --timeout=60`

nesquena/hermes-webui#5242.title: Gate settled anchor fallbacks by raw index
nesquena/hermes-webui#5242.author: franksong2702
nesquena/hermes-webui#5242.body:
## Thinking Path

#5197 shipped the behavior-level render ownership harness after #5183 proved runtime-journal to settled-hydration parity for representative anchor scenes. That clears the next #3400 step: the settled renderer should read as anchor-first, while legacy raw-message fallback remains compatibility-only for historical/non-anchor transcripts.

The fragile part was the metadata pre-scan in `renderMessages()`: it excluded anchor-owned messages by calling `S.messages.indexOf(m)` inside `.some()`. The fallback source collection already uses explicit raw indexes, so the pre-scan should use the same raw-index ownership gate instead of object lookup.

Refs #3400.

## What Changed

- Added `_legacySettledFallbackHasToolMetadata()` so legacy fallback eligibility is named and explicitly exits when `_anchor_activity_scene` is present.
- Changed the `renderMessages()` metadata pre-scan to use `(message, rawIdx)` and `anchorOwnedAssistantRawIdxs.has(rawIdx)`, removing the `S.messages.indexOf(m)` guard.
- Kept historical/non-anchor compatibility for `S.toolCalls`, raw `tool_calls`, `_partial_tool_calls`, `content[].tool_use`, role=`tool`, and persisted `session.tool_calls` snippets.
- Strengthened the fallback ownership harness with a mixed anchor/historical case where a stale anchor-side `S.toolCalls` entry must not suppress historical raw-index fallback recovery.
- Updated the phase0 anchor doc to state the current settled-render contract: anchor scenes own settled activity, while fallback paths are compatibility-only rebuilds.
- Updated the existing #401 static fallback guard to assert the extracted helper still covers `_partial_tool_calls` reconstruction.

## Why It Matters

This moves the #3400 Anchor line from ΓÇ£fallbacks guarded by testsΓÇ¥ to ΓÇ£fallbacks are explicitly scoped as historical compatibility.ΓÇ¥ It avoids another renderer-local normalizer becoming an equal owner of settled Worklog/tool activity after `_anchor_activity_scene` is available.

Release note: Internal: demote settled Anchor fallback rebuilds to compatibility-only paths and gate them by raw transcript index.

## Verification

- `node --check static/ui.js`
- `python3 scripts/ruff_lint.py --diff origin/master`
- `git diff --check`
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue401.py::test_rendermessages_rebuilds_tool_cards_from_partial_tool_calls` -> 1 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_anchor_fallback_ownership.py` -> 11 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_live_to_final_anchor_visible_order.py tests/test_anchor_scene_persistence.py` -> 96 passed

No browser/runtime validation was run; this is a settled-renderer internals/test/doc contract slice with no new visible UI surface.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- Full suite was not run locally.
- This intentionally does not remove historical/non-anchor fallback paths. Removing any compatibility path should still require evidence that that transcript shape hydrates through anchors.
- #3400 remains open as the broader live-to-final umbrella; this PR should not close it.

## Contract Routing

- Touched contract/doc surface: `docs/architecture/stable-assistant-turn-anchor-phase0.md`, Settled Fallback Ownership Matrix.
- Touched product-semantics tests: `tests/test_anchor_fallback_ownership.py`, `tests/test_live_to_final_anchor_visible_order.py`.
- State layer: frontend settled rendering over already-hydrated `messages` plus session-level compatibility metadata; no backend persistence mutation.
- Routing decision: local renderer contract update only; no onboarding, provider, runtime, cron, sidebar, composer, or state.db route changes.

## Contract Change

- Old rule: the settled fallback matrix was framed as an audit baseline and fallback removal was waiting on replay/runtime-journal parity tests.
- New rule: runtime-journal hydration parity and behavior-level renderer ownership coverage now back the settled-render contract; fallback paths are compatibility-only rebuilds for historical or genuinely non-anchor transcripts, gated by explicit raw transcript indexes.
- Justification: #5183 and #5197 shipped the prerequisite parity/ownership evidence, and this PR removes the remaining object-lookup guard that made fallback eligibility less explicit than fallback source collection.

## Model Used

AI-assisted implementation and coordination:

- Coordinator/reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5 in Codex.
- Worker: OpenAI GPT-5.5 sub-agent (`Helmholtz`) for the initial implementation.
- Read-only checks: OpenAI Codex Spark sub-agents for code-path, test-gap, doc, and contribution-rule review.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5243.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5243.body:
## Release v0.51.758 ΓÇö gate settled anchor fallbacks by raw index (#5242, @franksong2702)

Ships **#5242** by @franksong2702. Render-correctness fix on the settled-transcript path (#3400 anchor work).

### The bug
In `renderMessages()`, the legacy tool-metadata fallback tested anchor ownership with `S.messages.indexOf(m)` ΓÇö which returns the **first** matching message. With byte-identical (duplicate) assistant messages in a settled transcript, that resolves to the wrong raw index, so an anchor-owned turn could be mis-classified as a legacy fallback (or vice versa), mis-rendering tool output.

### The fix
Ownership is now gated by each message's actual `rawIdx` (from `.some((m, rawIdx) => ...)`), and the repeated top-level/partial/content tool-metadata check is consolidated into one `_legacySettledFallbackHasToolMetadata()` helper used at both call sites (incl. the `_anchor_activity_scene` exclusion). Identical behavior for non-duplicate transcripts; correct for duplicates.

- **Codex (reproduce): SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö rawIdx fix correct for duplicate transcripts + identical for non-dup; helper exactly reproduces both inline call sites; no regression to #140 reload / anchor-owned / liveΓåÆsettled paths.

Continues the #3400 anchor-render series (builds on the #5183/#5197 harness). Closes #5242.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5248.title: fix(webui): render a server-initiated turn that finished during an SSE gap on a visible tab
nesquena/hermes-webui#5248.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5248.body:
## Problem

A **visible** tab can permanently miss a server-initiated turn (self-wake / cron / restart hook) when its per-session SSE happens to be down at the exact instant the turn starts. The turn runs and persists fine server-side, but the open tab's transcript stays stale until a manual hard-refresh.

This is distinct from the hidden-tab gap (#5172) and the visibility-return reload (#5177/#5189). Here the tab is visible the whole time.

### Root cause

`start_session_turn` fans `server_turn_started` onto the per-session channel as a **fire-and-forget** `SessionChannel.emit` with **no replay buffer** ΓÇö only subscribers connected at that exact instant receive it. The chain:

1. The tab's `/api/session/stream` EventSource is momentarily down at the emit instant (a transient SSE drop, a reverse-proxy idle-timeout, or browser connection-pool starvation ΓÇö all common behind a corporate proxy). The broadcast lands on nobody for this tab ΓåÆ missed permanently.
2. The turn is short, finishes within seconds, persists, and clears from `ACTIVE_RUNS`.
3. The tab's `onerror` reconnect fires ~5s later and re-subscribes successfully.
4. The existing on-subscribe self-heal calls `active_stream_id_for_session(sid)` (keyed on `ACTIVE_RUNS`) to replay a synthetic `server_turn_started`. But the turn already finished in step 2 ΓåÆ `ACTIVE_RUNS` is empty ΓåÆ returns `None` ΓåÆ **nothing is replayed**.
5. The frontend `S.messages` stays at the pre-disconnect state; the new user+assistant pair sits in the persisted session unseen until a full refresh.

The existing self-heal only covers "a turn is live RIGHT NOW". It misses "a server-initiated turn started **and finished** during the SSE gap".

## Fix

Extend the on-subscribe self-heal to cover the finished-during-gap case, **without** ever doing a destructive clear+refetch (which would reintroduce the blank-gap jump fixed in #5177/#5189):

**Backend**
- New `persisted_message_count_for_session(session_id)` companion in `background_process.py` ΓÇö a cheap, metadata-only persisted `message_count` lookup (never parses the full transcript; runs on every per-session SSE reconnect). Returns `None` when the count is unknown (legacy sidecar) so the caller treats it as "cannot tell", never a trigger.
- The per-session SSE handler now reads the subscriber's last-known count from `?known_count=N`. In the **else** branch of the live-run replay (i.e. no live run to attach), it compares the persisted count against `known_count`; when the server is **ahead**, it emits a lightweight `session-updated` frame carrying only counts + `updated_at` (no transcript).

**Frontend**
- `startSessionStream` appends `&known_count=<S.session.message_count>` on subscribe. It uses the session's **full** `message_count` (the same basis the server persists), not `S.messages.length` (which is only the rendered tail window for long sessions and would false-trigger a reload on every reconnect).
- A new `session-updated` listener does an **incremental, swap-in-place** sync by reusing the #5189 `keepStaleUntilLoaded` `loadSession(force)` path ΓÇö old DOM is replaced by new DOM in a single render frame, no `old ΓåÆ empty ΓåÆ new` blank gap. It is idle-only (bails when a live turn is rendering, which owns its own message updates) and pane-scoped (bails when the session isn't the one on screen). It re-checks the count just before acting in case a concurrent load already caught the tab up.

The `session-updated` emit fires **only** when a known subscriber count exists AND the persisted count strictly exceeds it ΓÇö equal/behind counts, an absent `known_count`, or an unknown persisted count all no-op, so there is no spurious reload.

## Verification

Reproduced deterministically with a controlled harness (no real restart, no second device): in a fresh session, force-close the per-session EventSource and dispatch its error to run the reconnect path, fire a server-initiated turn while the SSE is down, then wait past the reconnect window. Pre-fix the turn never renders live (the persisted session is ahead while the tab shows the stale count); the reconnect's on-subscribe self-heal finds no live run and does nothing. Post-fix the reconnect carries `known_count`, the handler detects the server is ahead, emits `session-updated`, and the tab swaps in the new transcript with no refresh and no blank gap.

## Tests

Six new tests in `tests/test_optionz_liveview_perf.py`:
- `persisted_message_count_for_session` returns the persisted count, `None` when unknown, and swallows lookup failures.
- It is called with `metadata_only=True` (the perf contract ΓÇö never parse a large transcript on reconnect).
- Source-grep that the SSE handler parses `?known_count`, consults the persisted-count companion in the live-run-absent branch, and gates the `session-updated` emit on `persisted > known_count`.
- The emit gate fires only when the server is strictly ahead (equal / behind / unknown / absent count all no-op).
- Source-grep that the frontend subscribes with `known_count` sourced from `S.session.message_count` (not `S.messages.length`) and routes the `session-updated` frame through the `keepStaleUntilLoaded` swap-in-place path, idle-only and pane-scoped.

Full SSE / session / wakeup / bg-task regression family (205 tests across `test_optionz_liveview_perf`, `test_issue3996_sse_visibility`, `test_session_channel_option_x`, `test_hidden_tab_server_initiated_turn`, `test_issue4151_pwa_focus_sse`, `test_inflight_stream_reuse`, `test_issue_1584_multitab_sse`, `test_gateway_sse_reconnect_dedupe`, the `bg_task_complete_*` / `wakeup` set, and more) passes. The diff is additive-only against master.

The change is the third distinct defect in the "transcript goes stale / jumps" family, kept separate from the scroll-jump and hidden-tab work because each has a different evidence shape (`server_turn_started` presence, `message_count` delta, visibility state). It complements rather than overlaps #5172 (hidden tab) and #5189 (visibility-return reload).


---

**Live end-to-end verification (controlled harness, no manual refresh):**

Reproduced the exact defect against a running source build, then confirmed the fix, with two controlled experiments:

1. **Backend path** ΓÇö created a fresh empty session, started a server-initiated turn, waited for it to finish + persist (`message_count` 0ΓåÆ2, `agent_running:false`, `active_stream_id:null`), then connected `/api/session/stream?...&known_count=0` (stale). Server emitted `event: session-updated {message_count:2, known_count:0, source:subscribe_recovery}`. The prior live-run replay returns nothing here (the run already cleared from the active registry), confirming this is the gap the new branch closes.

2. **Frontend path** ΓÇö in a real browser, force-closed the per-session SSE and suppressed auto-reconnect so the gap spanned the WHOLE turn (the genuine condition ΓÇö SSE down longer than the short turn). The turn finished entirely during the gap; the tab stayed stale (`messages.length=0`, no live update). On reconnect with the stale `known_count`, the tab received `session-updated` (NOT `server_turn_started`) and incrementally rendered `0ΓåÆ2` via the keepStaleUntilLoaded swap-in-place path ΓÇö **zero manual refresh**.

A first harness attempt mis-fired (CHECK, not PASS) because auto-reconnect re-opened the SSE ~0.4s after the drop while the turn was still live, so it correctly hit the existing `server_turn_started` replay ΓÇö confirming the new branch only engages when the turn truly finished during the gap.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5249.title: Release v0.51.760 ΓÇö fail closed on ambiguous truncate matches (#5212, @rodboev)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5249.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5249.body:
## Release v0.51.760 ΓÇö fail closed on ambiguous truncate matches (#5212, @rodboev)

Ships **#5212** by @rodboev (#5134). Data-integrity fix on the fork/truncate path. Converged over two gate rounds.

### The bug
When truncating/forking a conversation mid-history, the row matcher fell back to a weak role+content match when rows lacked a stable id/timestamp (common for provider rows; recovery paths strip timestamps). A duplicate row adjacent to the cut could bind the **wrong** copy ΓÇö dropping the kept user turn, or (in the ambiguous-first-unkept case) the kept assistant turn's trailing tool-result rows.

### The fix
The matcher now compares a richer row signature (role + content + tool_call_id / tool_use_id / tool_name / tool_calls) and **fails closed on ambiguity** ΓÇö when >1 weak match exists it cuts at the earliest ambiguous candidate so the kept turn AND its tool tail survive, instead of greedily binding the first match.

### Gate (converged from 2 bounce rounds)
- Round 1 bounce: weak fallback dropped a kept USER turn on id-less duplicates ΓåÆ fixed (fail-closed).
- Round 2 (my re-gate) bounce: the fail-closed change then dropped a kept ASSISTANT turn's TOOL rows ΓåÆ fixed (preserve kept tool rows via the ambiguous-marker return).
- **Codex (reproduce): SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö both bounced cases fixed, the `(match, ambiguous_marker)` tuple change handled by all callers, distinct tool signatures disambiguate, no regression to id-bearing #5134 cases or the fork/branch-context tests.
- **Full suite 11083 passed** (only the 2 pre-existing cron-isolation flakes ΓÇö unrelated).

Closes #5212.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5251.title: fix(#5092): continue WebUI goals after gateway turns
nesquena/hermes-webui#5251.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5251.body:
## Thinking Path

- The browser-side `/goal` loop already knows how to continue after a turn, but only when the server worker emits the existing `goal_continue` contract.
- The live gap is not in browser code or goal state ownership, it is in the gateway-backed settle path, where the final assistant turn is persisted and the stream ends before the goal judge runs.
- The fix therefore keeps the current ownership split: routes forwards the goal-related signal symmetrically, the gateway worker evaluates the goal after settling the turn, and the browser keeps using the same continuation event it already handles.

## What Changed

- `api/routes.py`: forward `goal_related` to the gateway-backed worker, matching the direct path.
- `api/gateway_chat.py`: evaluate the active goal after a goal-related gateway turn settles, set `PENDING_GOAL_CONTINUATION`, and emit the existing `goal` / `goal_continue` events before `done` and `stream_end`.
- `tests/test_webui_gateway_chat_backend.py`: add the focused gateway continuation regression and the non-goal negative-boundary regression.
- `tests/test_goal_command_webui.py`: add route-level coverage that proves the gateway worker receives `goal_related=True`.

## Why It Matters

With the gateway backend selected, `/goal` should keep taking turns until the goal judge stops it, the same way the direct WebUI path already does. This restores that behavior without adding a new queue, moving goal ownership into the adapter layer, or changing the browser-side continuation contract.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_webui_gateway_chat_backend.py tests/test_goal_command_webui.py tests/test_stage326_pending_goal_continuation_race.py -v --timeout=60`

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

Issue-thread scope and queue-boundary guidance came from https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/5092#issuecomment-4825249360.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5257.author: franksong2702
nesquena/hermes-webui#5257.body:
## Thinking Path

- Live-to-Final rendering treats the anchor activity scene as the durable source of visible live activity.
- Compact Worklog already consumes `runtime_journal_snapshot.anchor_activity_scene` during live reattach/reload.
- Transparent Streaming skipped that live scene because `renderLiveAnchorActivityScene()` returned before the compact-only gate.
- That made the same running session show complete process prose in Compact Worklog but miss process prose in Transparent Streaming.
- This PR keeps Compact Worklog behavior intact and adds the missing Transparent Streaming live anchor-scene render path.

Refs #3400.
Refs #2361.

## What Changed

- Added a Transparent Streaming live anchor-scene renderer that consumes `activity_scene_v1` rows before the compact-only gate.
- Reuses the existing transparent anchor row renderer for prose, tool, and thinking rows.
- Marks live anchor rows with live/session/stream ownership metadata and clears stale legacy live activity rows before rebuilding.
- Keeps legacy live assistant segments hidden as metadata anchors while the anchor scene owns visible live activity.
- Keeps settled Transparent rendering intact by only applying the settled marker for settled rows and adding a behavior regression for that marker.

## Why It Matters

Transparent Streaming should not show less visible progress than Compact Worklog for the same live turn. When a runtime journal snapshot already contains ordered process prose and tool activity, both display modes should rebuild from that same source of truth instead of falling back to a partial live tail.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5260.title: fix(chat): keep just-settled worklog open for unpinned readers too (mobile scroll jump-back)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5260.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5260.body:
## Problem

On **mobile**, a reader who has scrolled **up to read inside the latest assistant turn** gets thrown to the **top of that turn** the moment it finishes (STREAM_DONE). This is the recurring "Θí╡Θ¥óσ╛Çσ¢₧σñºΦ╖│ / jumps back after the answer settles" report, observed on Android Chrome.

## Root cause

The STREAM_DONE keep-open exception (`_shouldKeepSettledWorklogOpenForPinnedFollow`, #4970 round 6/7) keeps the just-settled live worklog expanded so the liveΓåÆsettled DOM swap is height-stable ΓÇö but it was scoped to **pinned followers only**, on the explicit assumption that *"unpinned readers still get compact settled worklogs and preserve their viewport normally."*

That assumption holds on **desktop** (`overflow-anchor:none` + the JS snapshot restore keep an unpinned reader put), but **not on mobile**:

- Mobile CSS resting value is `.messages{overflow-anchor:auto}` (native scroll-anchoring **ON**), while `@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)` gives desktop `overflow-anchor:none`.
- `_fixMobileScrollJank()` flips an **inline `overflow-anchor:none`** over the settle render.
- So during the exact frame the worklog collapses ΓÇö shrinking the transcript by hundreds of px **above** the unpinned reader's viewport ΓÇö native scroll-anchoring is suppressed. Nothing absorbs the above-viewport shrink, and the reader's content leaps up to the top of the turn.

### Measurement (single-variable, faithful mobile emulation)

Reproduced on an isolated debug instance with CDP touch emulation (`setTouchEmulationEnabled` + `setEmulatedMedia(hover:none, pointer:coarse)`), which makes desktop Chromium report the real mobile media-query state (`matchHoverFine:false`, `overflow-anchor:auto`). Reader unpinned mid-turn, worklog collapses 920px above the viewport:

| overflow-anchor during collapse | reader content shift |
|---|---|
| `auto` | **0px** (native anchoring absorbs the shrink) |
| `none` (current mobile settle-render state) | **ΓêÆ248px** (content leaps up = the jump) |

## Fix

Keep the just-settled worklog open for **both** pin states on the settle render ΓÇö still one-shot scoped to the turn that just settled, so historical worklogs still collapse compact. This removes the height shrink entirely, fixing the jump for **every device / anchor-mode combination** instead of fighting the native anchor engine for one device.

- Rename `_shouldKeepSettledWorklogOpenForPinnedFollow` ΓåÆ `_shouldKeepSettledWorklogOpenForStreamSettle` (drops the `_scrollPinned` / `_messageUserUnpinned` gate; keeps the one-shot stream-id token).
- The `_fixMobileScrollJank` guard and the mobile `overflow-anchor:auto` CSS are **untouched**, so @rodboev's #4856 Android DOM-wipe fix and the original #MOBILESCROLL fix both stay intact.

## Tests

- Updated `tests/test_issue4970_stream_done_shrink_regression.py` to assert keep-open is `true` for the armed (just-settled) turn under **both** pin states, and `false` for historical turns / after disarm. The behavioral Node-harness check executes the real function.
- Full related suite green: `test_issue4856_android_scroll_regression.py`, `test_issue1360_streaming_scroll_hardening.py` (#MOBILESCROLL CSS + guard), and the #4970 / worklog-collapse tests ΓÇö no regressions.

## Notes for maintainers

As an external contributor I can't set reviewers/labels. This is a direct follow-up to the #4970 keep-open work and interacts with #4856 / #MOBILESCROLL ΓÇö @nesquena / @rodboev would be the right reviewers. The change is purely the scope of the keep-open exception; no behavior change for desktop or for pinned followers.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5263.title: Release v0.51.762 ΓÇö file-manager active-profile enforcement (#5179, @Hinotoi-agent)

nesquena/hermes-webui#5263.body:
## Release v0.51.762 ΓÇö file-manager active-profile enforcement (security)

Ships **#5179** by @Hinotoi-agent (rebased onto current master by maintainer; authorship preserved in commits).

**Security fix:** On a multi-profile box, `get_session_for_file_ops(sid)` resolved a session by id without checking which profile owns it, so a session belonging to a *different* profile could expose its workspace path to the currently active profile. The resolver now rejects a session whose owning profile doesn't match the request's active profile (raising the not-found the file routes already translate to a 404), failing closed. Same-profile access, single-profile/no-auth deployments, and the external-session (state.db) fallback are unchanged ΓÇö only genuine cross-profile lookups are denied.

### Gate (full authoritative)

(An earlier SHIP-ONLY-WITH-FIXES was the stale-base artifact ΓÇö the worktree was cut before #5240 merged; re-rebasing onto current master cleared it, and Codex itself attributed the findings to the merge-base mismatch.)
- **Opus correctness/architecture: APPROVE** ΓÇö closes the cross-profile workspace leak, fails closed, verified the subtle prerequisite that `profile` survives a metadata-only load, no cron/agent caller relies on the old behavior.
- **Full pytest suite: 11090 passed** (only the known `test_scheduled_jobs_profile_isolation` serial-ordering artifact failed ΓÇö passes in isolation + sharded CI; this PR touches no cron code).
