nesquena/hermes-webui#5265.title: Release v0.51.763 ΓÇö enforce active profile on request-supplied session IDs (#5198, @starship-s)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5265.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5265.body:
## Release v0.51.763 ΓÇö enforce active profile on request-supplied session IDs (security)

Ships **#5198** by @starship-s (rebased onto current master by maintainer; authorship preserved, plus a maintainer hardening commit co-authored back to @starship-s).

**Security fix:** Session-scoped API endpoints that accept a `session_id` (query or body) ΓÇö session read/duplicate/rename/delete, file ops, uploads, chat start ΓÇö looked it up without confirming it belongs to the request's active profile, so a caller could reference another profile's session by id. A central preflight now rejects a request-supplied session id not visible to the active profile (404), wired across all session verbs + upload + chat-start. Stream IDs are authorized via a synchronously-registered owner map (`STREAM_SESSION_OWNERS`) so the check doesn't depend on worker-startup timing. Single-profile / no-auth deployments and same-profile access are unchanged.

### Maintainer hardening (gate-found, fixed on the branch)
The Codex regression gate found the new `STREAM_SESSION_OWNERS` map leaked entries on three paths that bypass the teardown `finally`: worker early-return when the stream was cancelled before startup (`streaming.py`, `gateway_chat.py`) and the direct `ACTIVE_RUNS` stale-zombie prune (`routes.py`). Each now calls `unregister_stream_owner()`, with a regression test (verified to fail without the fix). Committed with `Co-authored-by: starship-s`.

### Gate (full authoritative)
- **Codex adversarial security gate (rebased + fixed worktree): SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö all three owner-map leak paths closed, cleanup uses an independent lock (no deadlock cycle), auth/CSRF/profile guards intact, 57 focused tests pass.
- **Opus correctness/architecture: APPROVE (with nits)** ΓÇö concurrency primitive correct (lock-guarded, owner registered synchronously before publish closing the worker-startup TOCTOU, unregistered in teardown), coverage complete with no fail-open on primary paths, single-profile visibility preserved.
- **Full pytest suite: 11108 passed** (only the known `test_scheduled_jobs_profile_isolation` serial-ordering artifact failed ΓÇö passes in isolation + sharded CI; this PR touches no cron code).
- PR's own `test_session_active_profile_authorization.py`: 18/18 pass (17 original + 1 new leak regression).

Diff: `api/routes.py` +171, `api/config.py` +36, `api/upload.py` +22, `api/streaming.py` +5, `api/gateway_chat.py` +4 + tests.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5266.title: fix(webui): hidden-tab poll keeps retrying when attach defers in multi-pane (#5172 follow-up)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5266.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5266.body:
Follow-up to #5172 (render server-initiated turns in a hidden tab), shipped in v0.51.743 via release #5218. Addresses the non-blocking multi-pane edge flagged in that review.

## Problem

During #5172 review, the Opus gate noted a narrow multi-pane edge: *"a fast attach-then-stop could defer render to the next interaction when the active pane is a different session."* I replied I'd send a small follow-up as a separate PR after #5172 merged so I wouldn't invalidate the cert. #5172 is now merged, so here it is.

Concretely: when a server-initiated turn (self-wake / cron / restart hook) arrives for a session that is **not** the currently-visible pane, `_startHiddenActiveStreamPoll`'s tick calls `_attachServerInitiatedStream(sid, streamId, true)`. But that function returned `undefined` on every path, so the poll had no way to know whether the attach actually happened. The non-current-pane path bailed early (correctly not attaching to a different pane's UI), yet the caller couldn't distinguish that from success ΓÇö and a stop-on-call would cancel the poll while the turn was never rendered, leaving it invisible until the next user interaction.

## Fix

`_attachServerInitiatedStream` now returns a `bool`:
- **`true`** ΓÇö this tab is responsible for rendering the stream: the renderer was attached, OR a renderer was already attached to the same `(sid, streamId)` (both = "stream is in good hands").
- **`false`** ΓÇö the attach was NOT consummated: `sid` is not the current pane (multi-pane), input was invalid, or the attach threw.

`_startHiddenActiveStreamPoll` captures the bool and only calls `_stopHiddenActiveStreamPoll()` when `true`. On `false` it keeps polling and re-tries on a later tick ΓÇö e.g. once the user switches the active pane back to `sid`, or by then the turn finishes and status returns `active_stream_id = null` naturally (both safe). This also stops the timer from spinning indefinitely after a successful attach.

## Tests

`tests/test_hidden_tab_server_initiated_turn.py`:
- every return path of `_attachServerInitiatedStream` is an explicit bool (no bare `return;`);
- the non-current-pane path returns `false`, the catch returns `false`, success paths return `true`;
- `_startHiddenActiveStreamPoll` gates `_stopHiddenActiveStreamPoll()` on the captured `attached` value.

Local: 8 passed, ruff forward-gate clean. Branched off current master.

Refs #5172.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5268.title: fix(security): gate embedded-terminal endpoints to local origins when auth disabled
nesquena/hermes-webui#5268.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5268.body:
## Summary

Gate the embedded-terminal HTTP endpoints to **local-origin requests when authentication is not configured**, closing an unauthenticated-RCE path on a passwordless network-exposed deployment.

The embedded workspace terminal spawns a PTY shell that runs arbitrary commands as the server-process user. When a password/passkey is configured, the existing session-cookie auth already gates these endpoints. But `check_auth()` returns `True` unconditionally when no auth is configured (the default out-of-the-box state), so in that state every terminal endpoint was reachable by any caller able to hit the port ΓÇö which, on a server bound to a non-loopback address with no auth, means a remote unauthenticated caller could drive a shell.

This is the same trust-model gap the onboarding/bootstrap endpoints already close (`#3758`/`#390` lineage). This PR reuses that exact gate.

## What changed

- New `_embedded_terminal_gate_allows(handler)` helper in `api/routes.py`, delegating to the existing `_onboarding_gate_allows` (which ignores spoofable `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` unless `HERMES_WEBUI_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR=1`).
- Applied to all five embedded-terminal endpoints, **before any side-effecting work** (session lookup / PTY spawn / write / resize / close / SSE stream open):
  - `POST /api/terminal/start`
  - `POST /api/terminal/input`
  - `POST /api/terminal/resize`
  - `POST /api/terminal/close`
  - `GET /api/terminal/output`
- Behavior:
  - **Auth enabled** ΓåÆ unaffected (cookie already verified upstream by `check_auth`).
  - **Auth disabled** ΓåÆ only loopback/private origins admitted; public-origin requests get `403`.
  - Operator who secures access another layer (reverse proxy auth / VPN / private net) opts out with `HERMES_WEBUI_ONBOARDING_OPEN=1`.
- Genuine same-host browser clients (the normal case) are unaffected.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_cvd3_terminal_local_origin_gate.py` (12 cases): gate predicate (public blocked / loopback + private allowed / spoofed-header rejected / auth-enabled allowed / `ONBOARDING_OPEN` escape hatch) + handler dispatch (each of the five endpoints returns `403` for a public client **without** reaching the spawn/write path, and a loopback client clears the gate and proceeds to normal lookup).
- Fixed a latent test-isolation leak in `test_extension_route_remains_behind_webui_auth` (it set `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` but never invalidated the process-wide password-hash cache, so its result depended on suite execution order ΓÇö exposed when the new test file shifted ordering). Now invalidates the cache before+after so it reads the env var deterministically.
- Made the `_RouteHandler` test fixture in `test_embedded_workspace_terminal.py` present a loopback `client_address` (real terminal requests are same-host), so those tests exercise the terminal logic they target rather than tripping the new gate.

## Provenance

Reported via a coordinated disclosure (held privately; no public PoC). The root precondition ΓÇö *passwordless + public bind* ΓÇö is separately addressed by the fail-closed startup guard in #5086; this PR is defense-in-depth on the terminal endpoints themselves, so the RCE path is closed even if a passwordless public bind ever slips past that guard.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5271.title: Let extension skins declare their base scheme
nesquena/hermes-webui#5271.author: franksong2702
nesquena/hermes-webui#5271.body:
## Thinking Path

- Hermes WebUI now lets trusted extensions register skins into the native Appearance picker.
- The current API lets a skin provide tokens, but not whether those tokens expect a light or dark base theme.
- That leaves dark editor skins mixed with System/Light base state, or light E-Ink skins mixed with Dark base state, unless each extension carries broad workaround CSS.
- Core already owns the Theme axis and the `.dark` class, so core should also own the effective light/dark base decision for registered skins.
- This PR lets extension skins declare `scheme: "light"` or `scheme: "dark"`; the user's saved Theme preference stays unchanged, while the effective `.dark` class and Prism theme follow the selected skin's scheme.

## Contract Routing

Task type: extension appearance capability / theme contract update
Touched areas: `window.registerHermesSkin()`, Appearance theme resolution, extension docs, theme docs, theme-registration tests
Relevant public docs:
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`
- `docs/UIUX-GUIDE.md`
- `DESIGN.md`
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`
- `THEMES.md`
Scope boundaries:
- This does not add a new picker, a new theme value, or any backend state.
- This does not make arbitrary CSS safe; registered skin tokens still go through the existing allowlist and value sanitizer.
- This does not rewrite the stored Theme preference (`light`, `dark`, or `system`). It only changes the effective base class while a scheme-declared extension skin is active.
Evidence needed before claiming done:
- Sanitizer coverage for accepted/ignored `scheme` values.
- Behavioral coverage that dark-scheme skins force `.dark` on and light-scheme skins force `.dark` off, then default skin restores the saved/base theme.
- Existing theme/skin regression tests still pass.

## Contract Change

Previous contract:
- `registerHermesSkin()` accepted descriptor name/value/label/colors/tokens and emitted one extension skin rule.
- The effective `.dark` class was controlled only by the Theme picker / System preference.
- Extension skins that were light-only or dark-only had no core-supported way to avoid being combined with incompatible base-mode tokens.

New contract:
- `registerHermesSkin()` may accept optional `scheme: "light" | "dark"`.
- Invalid scheme values are ignored.
- When a scheme-declared extension skin is selected, WebUI applies the corresponding effective `.dark` class and Prism CSS while leaving the user's stored Theme preference unchanged.

Compatibility / migration reason:
- Existing skins without `scheme` keep current behavior.
- Existing persisted Theme/Skin settings remain unchanged.
- Extension theme packs can move light/dark composition responsibility into core instead of duplicating broad token/selector workaround CSS.

## What Changed

- Added `_sanitizeSkinScheme()` for `light` / `dark` only.
- Stores an extension skin's sanitized scheme on the registered skin entry.
- Tracks the base resolved theme separately from the effective theme.
- Re-applies the effective theme when skin selection changes, so the active skin scheme can override the `.dark` class and Prism theme.
- Documented `scheme` in `docs/EXTENSIONS.md` and `THEMES.md`.
- Added behavioral Node harness coverage for scheme registration and effective `.dark` class behavior.

## Why It Matters

Dark editor skins and light display skins should not each have to patch around core's Theme/Skin composition rules. Core owns the base theme state, so this gives extension skins a small declarative way to say which base they need while preserving the user's visible Theme preference.

This unblocks cleaner extension skins such as Tokyo Night / Skin Pack and E-Ink without forcing each extension to carry broad fallback CSS for core tokens and selectors.

## Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_extension_theme_registration.py tests/test_theme_color_meta_bridge.py`
  - 20 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_extension_theme_registration.py tests/test_theme_color_meta_bridge.py tests/test_sienna_skin.py tests/test_catppuccin_skin.py tests/test_graphite_skin.py tests/test_1003_appearance_autosave.py tests/test_sprint26.py tests/test_issue3401_deep_review_fixes.py tests/test_zeus_skin.py tests/test_verdigris_skin.py`
  - 76 passed
- `node --check static/boot.js`
- `npm run lint:runtime -- --quiet`
- `git diff --check`
- Manual headless browser check on the local WebUI runtime:
  - registered a `scheme: "dark"` skin while the base theme was light and confirmed `.dark` became active
  - registered a `scheme: "light"` skin while the base theme was dark and confirmed `.dark` was removed
  - selected the default skin afterward and confirmed the base theme was restored

## Risks / Follow-ups

- The pre-paint inline script still cannot know an extension skin's scheme before extension JavaScript registers it, so the no-flash path can only preserve the pending extension skin key. Core corrects the effective theme as soon as the extension registers.
- Existing extension PRs should switch from broad composition workaround CSS to declaring `scheme: "light"` or `scheme: "dark"` after this lands.
- This does not change code-block typography; prose placed inside fenced code blocks still renders as code.

## Model Used

AI-assisted by OpenAI GPT-5 Codex in the Codex desktop app, using local shell, codegraph, Node/Playwright-style browser verification, and GitHub CLI workflows. Human maintainer directed scope and product decision.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5274.title: fix(#5270): preserve first WebUI continuation context for CLI sessions
nesquena/hermes-webui#5274.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5274.body:
## Thinking Path

- The visible CLI transcript already exists by the time WebUI opens the session, so the real failure surface is the provider-facing history used on the first WebUI follow-up, not the DOM or sidebar state.
- The current path has two owners: `_get_or_materialize_session()` resolves a writable CLI-origin session on POST, then `_run_agent_streaming()` immediately rebuilds provider history from sidecar/context plus `state.db` before calling `agent.run_conversation(...)`.
- The fix keeps the stitched CLI transcript authoritative across that handoff so the first WebUI continuation sees the assistant message that just happened instead of reconstructing a partial thread.

## What Changed

- `api/routes.py`: refresh or reconcile the writable CLI-origin session state on the POST continuation path so the stitched CLI transcript remains authoritative for the first WebUI follow-up.
- `api/models.py`: tighten the sidecar plus `state.db` reconciliation path so the first WebUI continuation cannot lose the immediately preceding CLI assistant turn while rebuilding provider-facing history.
- `tests/test_issue5270_cli_webui_continuity.py`: add a base-fails/head-passes regression for the already-claimed writable sidecar path, plus a preservation check for the fresh materialization path, by capturing `agent.run_conversation(..., conversation_history=...)`.

## Why It Matters

Switching from CLI to WebUI mid-conversation should keep a single coherent thread. This patch restores that continuity at the first handoff turn, which is exactly where users are most likely to ask about the answer they just received.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_issue5270_cli_webui_continuity.py tests/test_webui_state_db_context_reconciliation.py tests/test_recovered_journal_context.py tests/test_issue1217_transcript_compaction.py -v --timeout=60`

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5270.

This follows the POST-time CLI claim surface established in [#5111](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/5111), which is why the fix stays on the current continuation path instead of reviving the older pre-claim helper names from the issue body.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5276.title: fix(#5273): sync active viewed count on done settle
nesquena/hermes-webui#5276.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5276.body:
## Thinking Path

- `_restoreSettledSession()` already syncs viewed state for actively viewed sessions, so the stale dot was not a general sidebar-render problem.
- The remaining gap sits in the settled `done` path, where the sidebar cache row picks up the final compacted `message_count` before the actively viewed session advances its persisted `viewed_count`.
- The fix keeps ownership in `static/messages.js`, reuses the final post-compaction session id and count, aligns the viewed-sync fallback with the sidebar cache helper, and adds a focused regression harness for actively viewed versus background completion outcomes.

## What Changed

- `static/messages.js`: syncs `viewed_count` for actively viewed settled `done` completions before `_markSessionCompletedInList()` re-renders the sidebar cache, and uses `completedSession.messages.length` when the settled payload omits `message_count`.
- `tests/test_issue5273_active_done_viewed_sync.py`: adds a browserless behavioral regression harness that simulates compacted `done` settlements for actively viewed and background sessions, including the `completedSession.messages`, `S.session.message_count`, and `S.messages.length` fallback paths.

## Why It Matters

Compacted sessions now stop carrying a stale unread dot after the user is already looking at the finished conversation. Background completions still stay unread until the user actually opens them.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_issue5273_active_done_viewed_sync.py tests/test_issue856_background_completion_unread.py tests/test_issue856_active_session_read_state.py tests/test_bg_task_complete_focus_drop.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5273.

Boundary shaped by [#4946](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/pull/4946), which already covers the visit/load-session race slice.

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5289.title: fix(#5231): unblock Run dispatcher on the default Kanban board
nesquena/hermes-webui#5289.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5289.body:
## Thinking Path

- The default Kanban board is intentionally stored as `null`, and the backend already treats a missing `board` query parameter as "use the default board."
- The dry-run Preview dispatcher already follows that contract, but the real Run dispatcher treats the same `null` value as unavailable and returns before it can call `/api/kanban/dispatch`.
- The fix stays entirely in the browser layer: remove the blocking guard, keep the existing confirmation and in-flight behavior, and lock the change down with a browserless regression plus a small static dispatcher guardrail.

## What Changed

- `static/panels.js`: removes the pre-POST `if (!_kanbanCurrentBoard)` early return in `runKanbanDispatcher()` so the default board can post `/api/kanban/dispatch?max=8` without `board=`.
- `tests/js_source_extract.py`: shares a balanced-brace JavaScript extractor so the dispatcher harness and existing static Kanban checks parse function bodies without depending on exact whitespace.
- `tests/test_kanban_ui_static.py`: adds a secondary source-level assertion so the null-board pre-POST guard cannot quietly return, and reuses the shared extractor for `_kanbanSafeColor` instead of a brittle inline slice.
- `tests/test_issue5231_default_kanban_dispatch.py`: adds behavioral harness coverage for default-board real dispatch, named-board preservation, Preview dry-run preservation, and confirmation decline, and now reuses the shared extractor for the real async dispatcher functions.

## Why It Matters

The default board is the common case, so this guard turned the manual Run dispatcher button into a dead end for many installs. After the fix, clicking Run dispatcher on the default board reaches the existing in-process dispatch endpoint instead of stopping at an unavailable toast with no network request.

## Verification

- `npx eslint --no-config-lookup -c eslint.runtime-guard.config.mjs static/panels.js`
- `pytest tests/test_issue5231_default_kanban_dispatch.py tests/test_kanban_ui_static.py tests/test_kanban_bridge.py::test_kanban_only_mine_bulk_dispatch_and_block_unblock -v --timeout=60`

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5231.

Maintainer analysis in [issuecomment-4841878503](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/5231#issuecomment-4841878503) and [issuecomment-4845478031](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/issues/5231#issuecomment-4845478031) materially shaped this slice by separating the gateway discussion from the WebUI bug and confirming the default-board `null` root cause.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5301.author: promptclickrun
nesquena/hermes-webui#5301.body:
## Thinking Path

- The client-identity PR (#5239) accidentally bundled unrelated model-picker work.
- The maintainer asked for that work to be split so the identity/security review stays focused.
- This PR carries only the Copilot catalog safety-net fix and MoA model-picker support.
- Review caught two real MoA edge cases, so this branch now hardens preset resolution and local-config picker population.

## What Changed

- Treat MoA presets as a virtual WebUI model-provider group with `@moa:<preset>` model ids.
- Resolve selected MoA presets server-side per turn.
- Keep `/moa` unavailable on gateway-backed sessions.
- Prevent `providers.copilot.models` settings maps from being treated as a built-in catalog allowlist.
- Refresh the Copilot static fallback list used only when the live catalog probe misses.
- Split `resolve_moa_preset` into an optional import so older Hermes Agent installs keep the existing graceful-degradation behavior.
- Harden the `resolve_moa_preset` failure path so a preset-resolution exception falls back to the default preset shape instead of raising an unhandled server error.
- Populate the MoA picker directly from configured enabled presets before relying on live `provider_model_ids("moa")`, so older Hermes Agent installs still render the virtual provider.

## Why It Matters

This keeps two separate concerns separate:

- #5239 can be reviewed as client identity metadata and session-key trust behavior only.
- This PR can be reviewed as model-picker/provider behavior only.

The optional import and local-config fallback preserve compatibility with older or partial Hermes Agent installs while still enabling the picker for current configs.

## Verification

```bash
./scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue5057_moa_webui_route.py tests/test_copilot_provider_model_settings_not_allowlist.py tests/test_moa_model_picker_provider.py -q
```

Result:

```text
12 passed, 1 skipped in 6.55s
```

## Risks / Follow-ups

- Copilot's live catalog remains authoritative. The static list is only the cold-start/probe-miss fallback, so it should stay aligned with the Hermes Agent Copilot catalog over time.
- MoA preset selection is deliberately per-turn and server-resolved. The browser does not supply or persist MoA config.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5313.title: feat: support per-provider reasoning_efforts in config.yaml
nesquena/hermes-webui#5313.author: CharlesMcquade
nesquena/hermes-webui#5313.body:
## What
Adds `providers.<name>.reasoning_efforts` config support to `resolve_model_reasoning_efforts()`.

## Why
Some models only support a subset of Hermes's reasoning effort levels. For example, GLM-5.2 on W&B's vLLM endpoint only recognizes "high" and "max" (xhigh) for `reasoning_effort`, plus `enable_thinking: false` for non-think mode. The other levels ("minimal", "low", "medium") are silently ignored.

Without this change, the WebUI reasoning dropdown shows all 5 effort levels for every reasoning-capable model. With this change, users can declare which levels are valid:

```yaml
providers:
  wandb:
    base_url: https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1
    reasoning_efforts:
      - none
      - high
      - xhigh
```

The dropdown then filters to only those options.

## How
Adds a new step 0 in `resolve_model_reasoning_efforts()` that checks `providers.<name>.reasoning_efforts` before falling back to existing heuristics. Handles both `custom:<name>` and bare registered provider names. Falls through gracefully when no config entry is present ΓÇö zero behavior change for existing setups.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5317.title: fix(model): dynamically repair bare custom-provider models using actiΓÇª
nesquena/hermes-webui#5317.author: b3nw
nesquena/hermes-webui#5317.body:
# PR: Dynamically repair bare custom provider models using active custom provider catalog

Closes #5314

## Thinking Path
During our investigation of a recurring bug where conversations using custom provider models crashed with an HTTP 400 "Model not found" error specifically on the 2nd user input, we traced the execution flow:
1. **Client-side Stripping:** After Turn 1 completes, the client-side select dropdown value is synchronized. Due to prefix normalization in `_findModelInDropdown()` (`static/ui.js` line 2222), the namespace prefix `"x-ai/"` is stripped, causing the dropdown value to settle on the bare `"grok-composer-2.5-fast"`.
2. **Subsequent Turn POST:** On Turn 2, the client POSTs the bare model ID (`grok-composer-2.5-fast`).
3. **Server-side Repair Defect:** In the server-side model resolver `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state()`, the suffix repair check was overly restrictive:
   ```python
   _profile_default.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == model
   ```
   This only repaired a bare model if its suffix matched the profile's configured default model (e.g., `umans/umans-glm-5.2` in `steward-llm-proxy`'s configuration). If the user selected any other custom model (e.g. `grok-composer-2.5-fast`), it fell through un-repaired, sending the bare ID upstream which is rejected by the proxy.

We resolved this by updating the resolver to dynamically search the active custom provider's configured model list (`custom_providers`) in `config.yaml` to reconstruct the fully namespaced ID.

## What Changed
- **`api/routes.py` (`_resolve_compatible_session_model_state`)**:
  - Enhanced both the **Fast Path** (lines 5892+) and **Slow Path** (lines 6033+) checks to dynamically look up the active custom provider name in the profile's configuration.
  - If a matching custom provider is found, it extracts all registered model IDs and checks if any namespaced ID's suffix matches the bare model ID. If a match is found, it dynamically repairs it to the full namespaced form.
- **`tests/test_issue5127_process_wakeup_bare_model.py`**:
  - Added `test_fast_path_repairs_non_default_bare_model_of_custom_provider` and `test_slow_path_repairs_non_default_bare_model_of_custom_provider` to ensure that custom-provider models are repaired even when they do not match the profile's configured default model.

## Why It Matters
This fix prevents user conversations from breaking on the second turn when using any custom provider model that is not explicitly configured as the profile's default. It ensures high durability and robust model routing for all multi-model proxies.

## Verification
- **Pytest Suite:**
  - Ran the regression test suite locally inside the `.venv`:
    ```bash
    ./scripts/test.sh tests/test_issue5127_process_wakeup_bare_model.py -q
    ```
  - **Result:** All 12 tests passed (including the 2 new regression test cases).


## Risks / Follow-ups
Zero risk to standard first-party providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) as they are explicitly bypassed in the custom repair check. 

No direct modifications were made to the client-side select dropdown regex normalization behavior, preserving its UI consistency.

## Model Used
- **Provider:** hermes-webui/desktop using gemini-3-flash-preview

nesquena/hermes-webui#5320.title: fix(sidebar): keep active-parent delegate children stably visible (flicker) (#5306)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5320.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5320.body:
## Summary

Fixes two related sidebar bugs for delegated-subagent sessions.

### #5306 ΓÇö delegate subagent rows flicker in the sidebar (primary)

**Root cause:** While a parent WebUI session is the active/streaming session, a linked delegate subagent child that transiently reports `message_count === 0` between `/api/sessions` polls was dropped by `_sidebarRowHasVisibleMessages` **before** `_attachChildSessionsToSidebarRows` ever saw it. The child never entered `sessionsRaw`, so its row vanished from the sidebar entirely, then reappeared on the next refresh once its list metadata caught up ΓÇö the flicker (developer claw-io confirmed the child VANISHED on current master, not under-parent, not top-level).

**Fix (`static/sessions.js`, `_sidebarRowHasVisibleMessages`):** add an active-parent exception that mirrors the existing active-session exception ΓÇö a `child_session` whose `parent_session_id` is the current active sidebar session stays visible even at `message_count === 0`, so it survives partitioning and gets stacked stably under its parent for the duration of the parent's turn. Scoped strictly to children of the **active** parent, so truly-empty unrelated sessions are still hidden (verified by a no-regression test).

### #5305 ΓÇö delegate subagent sessions may still appear as top-level orphans (secondary)

**Determination: still reproduces on current master ΓåÆ fixed here (not a pure dup of #5244).**

`#5244` fixed the common case (child stacks under a visible WebUI parent). The remaining edge case still reproduced: when the WebUI parent is filtered out of the current render (project / profile / source scope) but the delegate child survives that scope, the child was promoted to a contextless top-level **"Subagent Session"** orphan (the `else if(childRenderable)` branch in `_attachChildSessionsToSidebarRows`).

**Fix (`static/sessions.js`, `_attachChildSessionsToSidebarRows`):** suppress a cross-surface `child_session` whose parent row is absent from the current render instead of orphaning it ΓÇö it re-stacks under the parent once that scope is active. This generalizes the existing archived-hidden-parent suppression (`hasHiddenArchivedAncestor`, #4293) from "archived" to "filtered-out". The genuinely-external parent case (messaging / CLI) still orphans via the pre-existing `parentIsExternal` branch, and the common #5244 stack-under-visible-parent case is unchanged (both covered by no-regression tests).

## Files changed

- `static/sessions.js` ΓÇö the two minimal, scoped fixes above (function signatures unchanged, so the existing structural guards in `test_sidebar_session_partition.py` / `test_issue3696_session_attention_scope.py` still hold).
- `tests/test_5306_subagent_sidebar_flicker.py` ΓÇö new; 7 tests executing the real `sessions.js` helper regions under node (same style as `tests/test_session_lineage_collapse.py`).

## Tests

New file `tests/test_5306_subagent_sidebar_flicker.py` (7 tests):

- `test_5306_active_parent_delegate_child_survives_zero_message_partition` ΓÇö the flicker invariant through the full partition ΓåÆ render pipeline; also asserts an unrelated empty session is still hidden.
- `test_5306_child_across_two_renders_stays_present` ΓÇö child stays present across two consecutive polls (0-msg then caught-up), i.e. no flicker.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5329.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5329.body:
## Redistribute the [Unreleased] backlog into per-version blocks (v0.51.693ΓÇô792)

**Docs-only. No code change.**

### The problem
The `[Unreleased]` section had accumulated **116 shipped bullets spanning 100 releases** (v0.51.693 ΓåÆ v0.51.792). The release process was bumping the version + tagging but **never moving each PR's bullet out of `[Unreleased]` into a dated version block** ΓÇö in fact no per-version block has been created since **v0.51.692**. So marquee features (`/moa`, the appearance skins, the custom TTS engine, theme/skin registration, OIDC login, ΓÇª) all sat orphaned in `[Unreleased]`.

Side effect: the Discord release-announcement automation kept re-listing the same items every run, because "what's new" had no version boundary to scope against ΓÇö everything lived in the one growing pile.

### The fix
Every `[Unreleased]` bullet is moved into a dated version block, reconstructed deterministically:
- PR number in the bullet ΓåÆ the first git tag containing that PR's merge commit ΓåÆ that tag's commit date.
- Bullets grouped under their original **Added / Changed / Fixed** subsections.
- `[Unreleased]` emptied to a self-documenting placeholder.

**Integrity:** 116/116 bullets redistributed, **zero lost** (verified by fingerprint), **zero new duplicate headers** introduced. (A pre-existing historical `v0.51.5` double-header from May is untouched ΓÇö out of scope.)

A few bullets whose PR-number grep was ambiguous were pinned to their real shipping tag by feature-content match (brand mark ΓåÆ v0.51.730, Compact-Worklog scroll ΓåÆ v0.51.766, the no-PR extension-capability bullets ΓåÆ v0.51.714/715).

### Recurrence prevention
Paired with a release-process fix (release skill step 4e + a pre-tag guard) so every future release stamps its bullets into its version block the way releases Γëñv0.51.692 did. Tracked separately.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5333.title: fix(sessions): prune index-only ghost sessions (#5331)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5333.author: enihcam
nesquena/hermes-webui#5333.body:
## Problem

Issue #5331: bulk "Untitled" ghost sessions accumulate in the sidebar with no backing .json file. They appear in _index.json as stale entries but cannot be removed ΓÇö _handle_sessions_cleanup only checked file existence, missing index-only orphans entirely.

Additionally, the old code unconditionally deleted _index.json after cleanup, forcing a full rebuild from disk on every sidebar poll (cache-busting with zero benefit).

## Root Cause

The session write path can add entries to _index.json without writing the sidecar .json file. The existing cleanup had no Phase to sweep these index-only ghosts, and unconditional index deletion masked the problem while creating a performance issue.

## Fix

Rewrites _handle_sessions_cleanup (api/routes.py) into 3 phases:

1. Phase 1 (unchanged): file sweep ΓÇö removes orphan .json files with zero-message-count entries
2. Phase 2 (new): index-only ghost sweep ΓÇö removes stale _index.json entries that have no backing file and no in-memory session. Title-agnostic (catches multi-language "Untitled" variants per #5331). Uses the same atomic _safe_replace pattern as prune_session_from_index
3. Phase 3 (fixed): only deletes _index.json when Phase 1 actually removed files, avoiding unnecessary cache invalidation

## Verification

All 9 scenarios pass via direct inline Python verification:

- Phase 2 prunes index-only ghosts
- Phase 2 preserves in-memory (active) sessions
- Phase 2 writes cleaned index in-place when no files were removed
- Phase 3 deletes index only when Phase 1 removed files
- zero_only mode still runs Phase 2
- Edge cases: empty index, missing index, corrupt JSON, entries without session_id key

## Testing

Added tests/test_issue5331_index_only_ghost_cleanup.py with test coverage mirroring all verification scenarios. Follows existing test_issue4985_* conventions.

Closes #5331

nesquena/hermes-webui#5338.title: fix(chat): suppress browser overflow-anchor during JS scroll-anchor realign (mobile scroll jump-back)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5338.author: allenliang2022
nesquena/hermes-webui#5338.body:
## Problem

On phones, a reader watching a message would sometimes be **yanked to an unrelated earlier turn without touching the screen** ΓÇö the recurring mobile scroll jump-back reports. It **never reproduced on desktop**, even with a mobile viewport in Playwright, which is what made it so hard to pin down.

## Root cause

The `.messages` scroll container's resting `overflow-anchor` differs by device:

```css
.messages { ΓÇª overflow-anchor: auto; }                     /* touch devices */
@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){ .messages{ overflow-anchor: none; } }  /* desktop only */
```

So on a phone the browser's **native scroll-anchoring is active** (`auto`), while on a hover+fine-pointer desktop it is off (`none`).

When `_restoreMessageViewportAnchor` writes `scrollTop` to realign the reader's anchor row **and** content height above the viewport changed in that same frame (a background render ΓÇö worklog/tool/activity update, session-updated swap, etc.), the mobile browser's own scroll-anchoring **also** adjusts `scrollTop`. The two compensations stack, and the reader is thrown to a different turn. Desktop never has the browser layer, which is exactly why every desktop repro failed while phones kept jumping.

Measured on an isolated instance (mobile viewport): inserting 800px of above-viewport content compensates `scrollTop` by **+800 in `auto` mode** and **0 in `none` mode** ΓÇö a clean, quantified demonstration of the double-compensation.

## Fix

`_suppressBrowserOverflowAnchor(container)` temporarily sets `overflow-anchor: none` around the JS `scrollTop` write in `_restoreMessageViewportAnchor`, then restores the prior value on the next frame after layout settles. It **engages only when the computed value is `auto`** (mobile) and is a **pure no-op on desktop** (already `none`, returns `null`). This removes the browser layer for exactly the one frame the JS is doing its own compensation, so the two can't stack.

The existing `_fixMobileScrollJank()` already does this for the `innerHTML=''` DOM-wipe path, but only there ΓÇö it does not cover incremental background renders / anchor-realign, which is the gap this closes.

## Verification

Isolated debug instance, mobile-viewport Playwright:

- **mobile `auto`**: above-viewport growth compensation **800 ΓåÆ 0** (browser layer suppressed during the JS write)
- **desktop `none`**: helper returns `null`, inline value untouched ΓÇö byte-identical behavior
- **streaming**: real turn, mid-read follow, 0 jumps, content held
- **regression suite**: scroll/anchor/jump/mobile/unpin tests green (629 passed locally; the single local failure is a Windows-only `WinError 206 command-line-too-long` in `test_anchor_fallback_ownership`'s Node harness ΓÇö unrelated to this change, passes on Linux CI, which is green here)

## Release note wording (per CONTRIBUTING ΓÇö CHANGELOG left to the release workflow)

> **A reader on a phone is no longer yanked to an unrelated earlier turn when a background render shifts content above the viewport.** On touch devices `.messages` rests at `overflow-anchor: auto`, so the browser's native scroll-anchoring double-compensated alongside the JS `scrollTop` realign in `_restoreMessageViewportAnchor`. The realign write now suppresses the browser's `overflow-anchor` for that one frame and restores it next frame (`_suppressBrowserOverflowAnchor`); it engages only when the resting value is `auto` (mobile) and is a pure no-op on desktop (already `none`). Streaming follow, desktop behavior, and the scroll-regression suite are unaffected.

## Notes

- Mobile-only behavioral change; desktop is provably unaffected (no-op path).
- Complements the earlier settle/scroll fixes (#5217, #5248, #5253, #5260) ΓÇö this addresses the distinct browser-vs-JS double-compensation class that those didn't cover.

## AI Usage Disclosure

- **Provider:** GitHub Copilot
- **Model:** claude-opus-4.8
- **Notable tool use:** root cause isolated and the fix verified on an isolated debug WebUI instance driven via Playwright (mobile-viewport), including the decisive `overflow-anchor: auto` vs `none` compensation measurement (800 ΓåÆ 0).

nesquena/hermes-webui#5343.title: fix(webui): handle stale clarify polling after profile switch
nesquena/hermes-webui#5343.author: ruizanthony
nesquena/hermes-webui#5343.body:
## Summary

- handle the stale clarify polling case that can happen immediately after switching profiles
- treat `404 Session not found` from the old session as a terminal stale-session response, not as a missing clarify endpoint
- stop the old clarify poll and hide the stale card instead of telling the user to restart the server

## Why

When the user switches profiles, the old profile's active session can briefly keep polling `/api/clarify/pending` while subsequent requests already carry the new profile cookie. The backend correctly answers `404 Session not found`, but the frontend currently treats any 404 as a missing clarify endpoint and surfaces a misleading restart warning.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD`
- private/site marker scan on the PR diff
- `node --check static/messages.js`
- `pytest -q tests/test_clarify_sse.py tests/test_clarify_unblock.py tests/test_4504_clarify_stuck_on_expiry.py tests/test_1466_sidebar_cancel_clarify.py tests/test_issue2883_clarify_padding.py` ΓÇö 62 passed

nesquena/hermes-webui#5346.title: fix(webui): stop false clarify-unavailable toast; add interrupt provenance (#5345)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5346.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5346.body:
Fixes #5345. Supersedes #5343 (credited below).

## Problem

Issue #5345 reports two related symptoms in a self-hosted deployment:

1. **Misleading clarify toast.** The UI shows *"Clarify endpoint unavailable. Please restart server."* even though `/api/clarify/pending` is present and returning HTTP 200 on every request.
2. **Unclear interrupt provenance.** Tool turns settle as interrupted (`exit_code: 130`, SIGINT), and it's hard to tell whether that was an explicit Stop or a side effect of stream-lifecycle handling.

## Root cause (Part 1)

`_handle_clarify_pending` **always returns HTTP 200** ΓÇö it answers `{"pending": null}` for an unknown session and never returns 404 (verified: `curl /api/clarify/pending?session_id=bogus` ΓåÆ `200 {"pending": null}`). But the front-end poll's catch block fired the restart-server toast on **any** caught error whose message matched the broad regex `/(^|\b)(404|not found)(\b|$)/i`. So the toast could only ever mis-fire ΓÇö triggered by an *unrelated* 404 leaking into the shared error path, e.g. a stale `Session not found` (contains "not found") from an old-profile session still polling briefly after a profile switch.

## Fix

**Part 1 ΓÇö clarify toast (`static/messages.js`):** branch on the structured HTTP status that `api()` attaches to the thrown `Error` (`err.status`) instead of scraping the message string:
- `404 Session not found` ΓåÆ treated as a stale-session poll (stop polling + hide the card silently), no toast.
- The restart-server warning now fires **only** on a genuine route-not-found 404 (`{"error":"not found"}`) whose body is *not* session-scoped.
- Poll failures are logged with request path, HTTP status, polling session id, and current session id (maintainer question #2).

**Part 2 ΓÇö interrupt provenance (`static/boot.js` + explicit call sites):** I traced every cancel path. Passive lifecycle events (session switch via `loadSession`, `beforeunload`, `visibilitychange`) call **local-only `closeLiveStream()`** and never hit `/api/chat/cancel` ΓÇö so they already do **not** interrupt the backend run (answering maintainer question #3: only explicit Stop/cancel interrupts). To make cancellation observable, `cancelStream()`/`cancelSessionStream()` now log `[stream] cancel requested` with a `reason`, and every explicit call site passes a distinct reason (`composer-stop`, `slash-stop`, `slash-interrupt`, `busy-interrupt`, `sidebar-stop`).

## Relationship to #5343

@ruizanthony's #5343 fixed only the profile-switch stale-session sub-case and **kept the broad message-scrape** in the missing-endpoint branch (`status===404 || /...not found.../i`), so that branch could still over-fire on other stale 404s. This PR handles the full issue (both symptoms) and gates the warning strictly on structured status + non-session body. Credited via `Co-authored-by`.

## Validation

- `node --check` on all 4 touched static files Γ£à
- `scripts/scope_undef_gate.py` ΓåÆ CLEAN Γ£à
- New `tests/test_issue5345_clarify_toast_and_interrupt_provenance.py` ΓÇö 9 tests, all pass; verified they **fail 8/9 against pre-fix master** (not vacuous). The 9th (`test_clarify_pending_never_404s`) locks the backend handler shape the whole fix depends on.
- Existing clarify suite green: `test_clarify_sse.py test_clarify_unblock.py test_4504_clarify_stuck_on_expiry.py test_1466_sidebar_cancel_clarify.py test_issue2883_clarify_padding.py test_messages_stale_stream_source_scope.py` ΓåÆ 65 passed.

Reported by @claw-io.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5351.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5351.body:
## Release ΓÇö stop live-streaming message flicker (#5328)

PR #5328 by @ruizanthony. On light themes, the live assistant turn visibly flashed/faded white on every streamed token.

### Root cause & fix (`static/style.css`)
The global dark-mode transition `...div{transition-property:background-color,border-color,color}` applied to *every* div, so each token-by-token markdown rewrite of the live turn animated a color/background fade. nesquena/hermes-webui#5353.title: fix(webui): drop verification-stop synthetic nudge from transcript (#5334)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5353.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5353.body:
## Summary

An internal Hermes Agent **verify-before-finish** control turn was leaking into the visible WebUI transcript. When the agent edits code but lacks fresh passing verification evidence, its verify-on-stop loop appends a synthetic assistant "premature done" answer plus a synthetic `user` nudge whose text looks like:

> `[System: You edited code in this turn, but the workspace does not have fresh passing verification evidence yet...]`

These turns exist only to drive the loop for one more API round-trip. This is the **same class** of internal-control-message leak as #3320 / #3821 / #4373 / #4875.

## Root cause

The agent already marks both scaffolding rows with structured flags ΓÇö `_verification_stop_synthetic` (verify-on-stop) and `_pre_verify_synthetic` (plugin `pre_verify`) ΓÇö and keeps them out of its own durable store via `run_agent._EPHEMERAL_SCAFFOLDING_FLAGS`. **WebUI never learned to honor those markers**, so the synthetic `user` nudge settled into the visible transcript as a real turn.

## The fix (server-side)

Extends the existing suppression mechanism in `api/streaming.py` rather than inventing a new one:

- New `_SYNTHETIC_CONTROL_MESSAGE_FLAGS` (mirrors the agent set) + `_is_synthetic_control_message()` / `_drop_synthetic_control_messages()` helpers, placed next to the existing `_drop_synthetic_max_iteration_summary_requests`.
- Applied inside `_merge_display_messages_after_agent_result()` ΓÇö the single chokepoint every settlement path routes `session.messages` (the visible transcript) through. All three inputs (`previous_display`, `previous_context`, `result_messages`) are filtered so prefix/delta detection stays aligned and any row that leaked in a prior build is scrubbed on the next merge.

The filter is **marker-based, not string-based**: a real user message that merely quotes the nudge copy is preserved.

## Scope

- **Symptom 2 (verification-stop leak): fixed.**
- **Symptom 1 (spurious "No response from provider" card while visible text streamed): intentionally OUT OF SCOPE** ΓÇö the issue flags it as too broad to fix naively, and it isn't touched here.

## Tests

`tests/test_issue5334_verification_stop_leak.py` (8 tests, all passing) pins:
- the marker classifier accepts both synthetic flags and rejects a real message quoting the nudge text;
- **the `_verification_stop_synthetic` nudge never appears in the rendered transcript** (core deliverable), same for `_pre_verify_synthetic`;
- a normal user message is **not** excluded;
- a previously-leaked nudge in prior display is scrubbed on re-settlement.

Adjacent suppression suites (`test_tool_limit_terminal_state`, `test_issue4875_recovery_prompt_filter`, `test_issue3468_duplicate_after_compression`, `test_stable_assistant_turn_anchor_phase0`) still pass ΓÇö no regressions.

Fixes #5334.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5354.title: fix(webui): crash visibility ΓÇö faulthandler + thread excepthook + exit audit (#4633)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5354.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5354.body:
## Problem (#4633)

`server.py` exited **silently** after 9ΓÇô16h: no traceback, no shutdown-audit line, no core dump ΓÇö the log just stopped mid-request.

Two structural gaps made a death invisible:

- It runs a `ThreadingHTTPServer` with `daemon_threads = True`. An **unhandled exception in a request / SSE / long-poll handler thread** is reported through `threading.excepthook`; the stock hook only prints to `sys.stderr` with no context and, if that stream is gone, the report is lost ΓÇö so a single handler-thread exception could vanish.
- **`faulthandler` was not enabled**, so a *native* crash (segfault/abort in a C extension ΓÇö sqlite, ssl, a provider SDK) terminated the interpreter with nothing written.
- Compounding both: the WebUI configures **no logging handlers**, so `INFO`/`ERROR` records are dropped by logging's `lastResort` filter (WARNING+ only). Even the existing `_log_shutdown_audit` `logger.info(...)` never reached the log.

This PR is **crash visibility only** ΓÇö when the process dies we now get a diagnostic, and one handler-thread exception can't silently kill work. The paired **memory root-cause is #4765** (not addressed here).

## What was added

New `api/crash_visibility.py` (stdlib-only; every hook is defensive and **never raises** ΓÇö a raising hook would just be a new silent-failure mode). `install_crash_visibility()` is idempotent and is wired into `server.main()` **before any heavy startup work**:

1. **faulthandler** ΓÇö `faulthandler.enable(all_threads=True)` so a native segfault/abort dumps a C-level traceback of every thread. Also registers `SIGUSR1` (`faulthandler.register`) for on-demand all-thread stack dumps to diagnose a *hang* (`kill -USR1 <pid>`).
2. **threading.excepthook** ΓÇö logs any uncaught daemon/handler-thread exception (thread name, ident, daemon flag, full traceback) instead of losing it. Chains to any prior non-stock hook; ignores clean thread exit (`exc_type=None`) and `SystemExit`.
3. **sys.excepthook** ΓÇö logs uncaught main-thread exceptions; preserves default `KeyboardInterrupt` (Ctrl-C) behaviour.
4. **atexit exit-audit** ΓÇö a breadcrumb on clean/unwound exit. Its *absence* in the log narrows a silent death to an un-unwound kill (OOM / SIGKILL / native abort), which is itself diagnostic.

Every diagnostic is written **directly to the fault stream** (`sys.stderr`, which the bootstrap redirects into the WebUI log file) **and** mirrored through `logging`, so the line is guaranteed to land regardless of logging configuration.

## Not changed

No request-handling behavior change, no new dependencies, standard library only.

## Tests

`tests/test_issue4633_crash_visibility.py` (10 tests, all passing) asserts: faulthandler enabled after install; install idempotent; `threading.excepthook` installed and a **real daemon-thread exception is logged** (name + traceback in both the stream and via logging); clean thread exit / malformed args are swallowed without raising; `sys.excepthook` installed and main-thread exceptions logged; `KeyboardInterrupt` not treated as a crash; atexit audit registered and emits; and `server.py` wires in `install_crash_visibility()`. No live server socket required. Existing `test_shutdown_audit_logging.py` and `test_issue1458_stability_hardening.py` still pass.

Fixes #4633.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5357.title: fix(webui): bound in-memory SESSIONS cache with lazy reload (#4765)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5357.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5357.body:
## Summary

Fixes the unbounded in-memory `SESSIONS` growth that crashes long-running self-hosted WebUI installs ΓÇö the silent-crash-after-hours cluster **#4765 / #2233 / #4633**.

## Root cause

The WebUI keeps every session object + messages in a global in-memory LRU (`api.config.SESSIONS`, an `OrderedDict`). The cache *had* a cap (`SESSIONS_MAX`) and lazy reload in `get_session()`, but eviction was performed with a **blind** `SESSIONS.popitem(last=False)` at 8 call sites. That is unsafe in two ways:

1. It could evict the least-recently-used entry **even if it was actively streaming or held unsaved messages**, dropping an in-flight turn or losing a conversation.
2. Because the cap was only settable via an env var (and the safety concerns above discouraged aggressive eviction), on real installs the effective behavior was **memory that only grows**: RSS climbs ~700MB ΓåÆ 7.5GB@9h ΓåÆ 17.8GB@44h, then the interpreter segfaults. Maintainer triage confirmed this is the root of the crash cluster.

## Fix ΓÇö bounded, lazy, and safe

- **`_session_is_evictable(s)`** ΓÇö a session is evictable **only** when *all* hold:
  - not streaming (`active_stream_id` unset),
  - no in-flight/queued turn (`pending_user_message` and `pending_started_at` unset),
  - full state is provably on disk (sidecar `message_count` ΓëÑ in-memory message count; metadata-only stubs and zero-message shells are trivially safe).
  Anything we cannot *prove* is safe stays resident ΓÇö using a little more RAM beats ever losing a session.
- **`_evict_sessions_over_cap(cap=None)`** ΓÇö replaces all 8 blind `popitem` loops (`api/models.py`, `api/routes.py`, `api/streaming.py`). Walks the LRU oldestΓåÆnewest and removes only provably-safe entries. It **never acquires `LOCK` or any stream lock itself** (every caller already holds `LOCK`), so it introduces no lock-ordering deadlock. If every over-cap candidate is active/unsaved, the cache may briefly exceed the cap ΓÇö the intended safe behavior.
- **Lazy reload unchanged**: an evicted session transparently reloads from its `<sid>.json` sidecar on the next `get_session(sid)` / `SESSIONS[sid]` access. **No call sites changed** ΓÇö the safety lives in the accessor and the eviction helper.
- **`_index.json` sidebar behavior preserved**: the sidebar reads the index, not the full `SESSIONS` cache ΓÇö untouched.

## Config key (no new env var)

The cap is now configurable via **`config.yaml`**:

```yaml
webui:
  sessions_cache_max: 300   # default
```

Resolved by `config.get_sessions_cache_max()` with precedence:
`config.yaml webui.sessions_cache_max` ΓåÆ `HERMES_WEBUI_SESSIONS_MAX` (legacy env fallback) ΓåÆ `DEFAULT_SESSIONS_CACHE_MAX = 300`. A missing / non-numeric / `< 1` value falls back so a typo can never disable the bound and reintroduce the leak. No new `HERMES_*` env var is added (per project policy for non-secret config).

## Safety invariants proven by tests

New `tests/test_issue4765_sessions_lru_eviction.py` (8 tests, all passing):

- eviction happens once the cache grows past the cap;
- an **active / streaming** session is never evicted (even as the oldest / under heavy churn);
- a session with **unsaved in-memory messages** (or an unsaved tail ahead of its sidecar) is never evicted;
- an evicted session **lazily reloads from disk with identical content**;
- **no data loss** ΓÇö every sidecar file survives heavy churn and stays fully retrievable;
- the config knob reads `webui.sessions_cache_max` and fails safe on bad input.

## Verification

```
tests/test_issue4765_sessions_lru_eviction.py .......... 8 passed
# regression sweep (no breakage across the many SESSIONS call sites):
tests/test_issue3506_memory_and_watcher.py, test_session_duplicate_edit.py,
test_route_session_list_cache_extraction.py, test_session_sidebar_cache.py,
test_session_index.py, test_core_data_loss_cases.py, test_session_save_mode.py,
test_empty_session_no_disk_write.py, test_session_lost_response_regression.py,
test_inflight_purge_missing_sessions.py, test_stale_stream_cleanup.py,
test_session_sidecar_repair.py  ΓåÆ 243 passed
python3 -c 'import ast; ast.parse(open("api/config.py").read())'  ΓåÆ OK
```

Fixes #4765.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5360.title: fix(webui): align reconciliation dedup key with workspace-prefix stripping (#5339)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5360.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5360.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5339 ΓÇö after a WebUI container restart, the first user message sent was **permanently prepended** to every subsequent user message, and the contaminated turns rendered out of chronological order (clustered at the restart boundary).

## Root cause: a key-function mismatch between two dedup layers

WebUI sends the model a workspace-prefixed `user_message` (`[Workspace::v1: /path]\n<text>`), while the visible/optimistic bubble **and** the WebUI sidecar row carry only the bare `<text>`. Two layers dedup user turns, but keyed them differently:

- **Reconciliation** (`api/models.py`): `state_db_delta_after_context` keys rows via `_session_message_content_key` ΓåÆ `_normalized_session_message_content`, which normalized whitespace **only** ΓÇö no prefix stripping.
- **Streaming** (`api/streaming.py`): `_message_identity` **strips** the workspace prefix for user turns via `_strip_workspace_prefix(text, include_legacy=True)`.

So a state.db row (prefixed) and a sidecar row (bare) for the *same* completed turn produced **different** keys. The alignment loop in `state_db_delta_after_context` failed to match them, treated the state.db copy as a **new** row, and appended a duplicate user turn. The agent-side `drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users` pass then concatenated the two adjacent user rows with `\n\n` into a **permanent composite** ΓÇö reproduced exactly by *completed turn ΓåÆ restart ΓåÆ new message*.

## The fix

Make `_session_message_content_key` strip the workspace prefix for `role == 'user'`, reusing the **same** `_strip_workspace_prefix` helper the streaming side uses (lazy import, because `api.streaming` imports `api.models` at module load ΓÇö a top-level import would be circular). This stops the duplicate at its WebUI source rather than papering over it downstream.

Scope guarantees (all covered by tests):
- Only `role == 'user'` is stripped ΓÇö assistant/tool keys are unchanged.
- A prefix-free user message keys identically before and after (idempotent).
- Genuinely different user messages still key distinctly.
- The agent-side merge (different repo) is untouched ΓÇö the WebUI-side fix removes the duplicate that fed it.

## Tests

New `tests/test_issue5339_restart_stale_user_dedup.py` (7 tests): unit-level key agreement + idempotence + role scoping + distinctness; delta-level "prefixed state row is a mirror, not a delta" plus a guard that a genuinely new turn is still surfaced; and an end-to-end `/api/session` load asserting the completed turn is not duplicated at the restart boundary (buggy: 6 rows, `first answer` twice; fixed: 4 rows).

- `python3 -c 'import ast; ast.parse(open("api/models.py").read())'` ΓåÆ OK
- `tests/test_issue5339_restart_stale_user_dedup.py` ΓåÆ **7 passed**
- `tests/test_webui_state_db_reconciliation.py` ΓåÆ **41 passed** (no regression)
- `tests/test_issue3709_thinking_double_render.py` ΓåÆ **5 passed**

Fixes #5339.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5361.title: Release ΓÇö bound in-memory SESSIONS cache, fix memory-growth crash cluster (#4765/#2233/#4633)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5361.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5361.body:
## Release ΓÇö bound in-memory SESSIONS cache with safe lazy reload (#4765)

Fixes the unbounded `SESSIONS` growth crash cluster **#4765 / #2233 / #4633** (self-built). On long-running self-hosted installs RSS climbed ~700MB ΓåÆ 7.5GB @ 9h ΓåÆ 17.8GB @ 44h, then the interpreter segfaulted; daily restart was the only workaround.

### Root cause
The global in-memory `SESSIONS` cache (`api.config`, OrderedDict) had a cap + lazy reload, but eviction was a **blind** `SESSIONS.popitem(last=False)` at 8 sites ΓÇö unsafe (could drop a streaming/unsaved session), so in practice eviction was avoided and memory only grew.

### Fix ΓÇö bounded, lazy, and safe
- **`_session_is_evictable(s)`** ΓÇö evict only when ALL hold: not streaming (`active_stream_id` unset), no in-flight/queued turn (`pending_user_message`/`pending_started_at` unset), and full state provably on disk (sidecar `message_count` ΓëÑ in-memory count; metadata-only / zero-message shells trivially safe). Anything not provably safe stays resident.
- All 8 eviction sites now route through the guarded `_evict_sessions_over_cap()` ΓÇö no blind `popitem` remains.
- Evicted sessions lazily reload from their `.json` sidecar via `Session.load()` on next `get_session`.
- Cap is **config.yaml-driven** (`webui.sessions_cache_max`, default 300), typo-proof (falls back to the hardened default; a bad value can never disable the bound) ΓÇö no new env var.

### Gate (this is the core session cache ΓÇö deepest scrutiny)
- **Codex: SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö verified all 8 sites guarded, active/pending turns persisted before streaming (non-evictable), lazy reload uses `Session.load()`, disk-count guard correct, no lock inversion.
- Full suite: **11477 passed** (only the 2 pre-existing `test_scheduled_jobs_profile_isolation` serial artifacts); 8 targeted eviction tests + 21 cache/session tests.
- **Live evictΓåÆreload drive:** with cap=2 and 3 sessions, eviction fired (memory bounded), the evicted session reloaded from disk with byte-identical content, and no session file was deleted ΓÇö empirically no data loss.

Fixes #4765. Also resolves the crash symptom in #2233 and the memory root cause behind #4633.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5365.title: fix(#5340): use local time for pasted-text filenames
nesquena/hermes-webui#5365.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5365.body:
## Thinking Path

- Large plain-text pastes already become `.md` attachments, but their generated `pasted-text-*` filename used `Date#toISOString()`.
- `toISOString()` always formats in UTC, so users outside UTC see attachment filenames that don't match their local paste time.
- The fix keeps the existing filename format and collision suffixing while building the timestamp from local-time `Date` components.

## What Changed

- `static/boot.js`: build pasted-text attachment timestamps from local `Date` getters instead of UTC ISO strings.
- `tests/test_large_text_paste_attachment.py`: add a Node-backed regression for Asia/Shanghai local time and preserve duplicate suffix behavior.

## Why It Matters

Pasted-text attachments now carry the wall-clock time users expect from their own browser and system timezone. The visible filename stays sortable and keeps the existing duplicate suffix behavior.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_large_text_paste_attachment.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5340.

Scope follows the maintainer comment on #5340 confirming the `toISOString()` UTC root cause and recommending local-time components.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5370.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5370.body:
## Thinking Path

- `#4251` reports that a session's model picker choice can get silently reverted, and the next background-task wakeup then resumes on the stale/default model instead of what the user actually picked.
- `routes.start_session_turn` trusts `s.model` as the source of truth, and `_prepare_chat_start_session_for_stream` already persists the correct model synchronously before a turn's worker thread starts, so the session record is right at dispatch time.
- The worker thread (`_run_agent_streaming`) then re-stamps `s.model` and `s.model_provider` a second time from its own dispatch-time closure, with no check for whether a `POST /api/session/update` already moved the session forward in the meantime. That's the clobber, an in-flight turn overwriting a newer picker choice with its own stale value.
- The fix adds a narrow ownership guard at both persistence points in `_run_agent_streaming`: only a turn that actually persisted the session's current model value is allowed to re-write `s.model` or `s.model_provider`, so a picker choice that lands after dispatch survives both the initial writeback and the later profile-repair checkpoint.

## What Changed

- `api/streaming.py`: guard both `_run_agent_streaming` persistence checkpoints with an explicit "this turn still owns the persisted model" flag, so neither the initial stamp nor the later profile-repair writeback can overwrite a newer picker-owned `s.model` or `s.model_provider`.
- `tests/test_issue4251_wakeup_model_picker_race.py`: add focused regression coverage for the raced picker case, provider preservation, the ordinary non-racy path, the empty-session first dispatch path, and the profile-repair race edge.

## Why It Matters

Users who change their model picker while a background task is still running, or while a turn's worker thread is still starting up, no longer have that choice silently reverted the next time a `notify_on_complete` completion wakes the session. The wakeup turn now resumes on the model and provider the user actually last picked, not on stale values left behind by an earlier in-flight turn.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_issue4251_wakeup_model_picker_race.py -v --timeout=60
pytest tests/test_issue3895_opencode_go_model_picker.py tests/test_wakeup_defer_race.py tests/test_bg_task_complete_wakeup.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #4251.

Scope follows the maintainer comment on #4251 identifying the in-flight worker writeback as the load-bearing fix.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5373.title: fix(#4737): retry model catalog fetch once after cold-cache fallback
nesquena/hermes-webui#5373.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5373.body:
## Thinking Path

- The reported symptom is that the model picker looks incomplete on the very first tab after an upgrade and doesn't fix itself, `populateModelDropdown()` (`static/ui.js:2413`) falls back to a configured-only synth list (`static/ui.js:2436`) whenever the server's `/api/models` response has empty `groups`, which is exactly what happens right after an upgrade invalidates the on-disk catalog cache (`_is_loadable_disk_cache()` in `api/config.py:5082-5134`).
- Once that thin list is painted, the only follow-up call, `_fetchLiveModels()` (`static/ui.js:2612`), only ever patches the active provider's `<optgroup>`, never re-requests `/api/models`. The only place that does ask for a fresher catalog is the session-switch handler (`sessions.js:1394`, `freshness:'session_visit'`); boot's own call site (`boot.js:2889`) passes no freshness hint at all, so the first tab has no self-correction path.
- The fix stays entirely in the browser layer: give `populateModelDropdown()` a one-shot retry that reuses the already-whitelisted `freshness:'session_visit'` value (`api/routes.py:10825-10829`) whenever it had to use the synth fallback, guarded so it can never loop or add overhead once the catalog is warm, and forward the caller's existing redirect handler through that retry so the boot unauth budget still applies on the second request.

## What Changed

- `static/ui.js`: `populateModelDropdown()` now tracks whether it used the configured-only synth fallback, empty `data.groups`, and, if so, schedules exactly one follow-up call to itself with `freshness:'session_visit'` after kicking off the existing background live-model fetch. A new one-shot module-level flag prevents this from ever firing more than once per tab, and the retry now preserves the caller's existing `redirectIfUnauth` override instead of falling back to the generic redirect path.
- `tests/test_4737_first_tab_model_catalog_refresh.py`: new node-driver regression test, same pattern as `tests/test_5021_boot_model_redirect_budget.py`, covering the refetch, the no-op case when the server already returns a full catalog, the one-shot retry cap, and the boot redirect-handler preservation path on the retry leg.

## Why It Matters

Users who open a tab right after a Hermes upgrade currently see a truncated model picker that never fills in on its own. This makes the first-tab catalog self-correct without any user action, without adding any extra request on the normal warm-cache path, and without regressing the boot redirect budget that already protects the first-tab auth flow.

## Verification

```text
pytest tests/test_4737_first_tab_model_catalog_refresh.py -v --timeout=60
```

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #4737.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5374.title: Respect auxiliary title timeout for manual regenerate
nesquena/hermes-webui#5374.author: Stacey2911
nesquena/hermes-webui#5374.body:
## Thinking Path

Manual title regeneration uses the frontend `api()` helper. That helper has a 30-second default timeout. The backend title-generation path, however, already honors the user-configured auxiliary title-generation timeout.

When `auxiliary.title_generation.timeout` is set above 30 seconds, a slow-but-valid title generation can outlive the frontend default timeout. The frontend then shows a premature failure toast even though the backend can still finish and persist the title within the configured auxiliary timeout.

The fix keeps backend behavior unchanged and makes the manual title-regeneration frontend call use the configured auxiliary title timeout when available.

## What Changed

- Added manual title-regeneration timeout helpers in `static/sessions.js`.
- Reused already-loaded auxiliary settings when available.
- Added a lazy `/api/model/auxiliary` fetch when settings have not been opened yet.
- Added single-request caching so repeated title regeneration does not repeatedly fetch auxiliary config.
- Passed `timeoutMs` to the manual `/api/session/title/regenerate` call when a valid configured title timeout is available.
- Added regression coverage in `tests/test_manual_title_regenerate_timeout.py`.

Timeout calculation:

```text
valid timeout seconds ΓåÆ max(30000, round((timeoutSeconds + 5) * 1000))
missing/invalid/zero/negative/fetch failure ΓåÆ preserve existing 30s api() default
```

No backend title-generation timeout logic was changed.

## Why It Matters

Users can configure a longer timeout for the auxiliary title-generation model. Manual title regeneration should not show a failure toast at the frontend's old 30-second default when the backend is still operating within the configured auxiliary timeout.

This avoids a confusing false failure state where the UI reports title generation failed, but the title appears afterward.

## Contract Routing

Task type: auxiliary model configuration / frontend request timeout / toast behavior

Touched areas:

* Manual title regeneration request path
* Auxiliary model timeout config read path
* Frontend timeout behavior for `/api/session/title/regenerate`

Relevant docs checked:

* `AGENTS.md`
* `CONTRIBUTING.md`
* `docs/CONTRACTS.md`
* `TESTING.md`
* `DESIGN.md`
* `docs/UIUX-GUIDE.md`

State / behavior invariant:

* Backend title-generation timeout behavior is unchanged.
* Compression/update routes are unchanged.
* Existing `api()` fallback timeout remains unchanged when no valid auxiliary title timeout is available.
* Failed config lookup does not block manual title regeneration.
* Non-timeout errors still surface through the existing failure path.

Contract Change:

* None intended. This aligns the manual title-regeneration frontend timeout with existing auxiliary title-generation timeout configuration.

## Verification

Automated validation:

* `node --check static/sessions.js`
* `node --check static/workspace.js`
* `node --check static/panels.js`
* `./scripts/test.sh tests/test_manual_title_regenerate_timeout.py tests/test_title_aux_routing.py`

Results:

* JS syntax checks passed.
* `tests/test_manual_title_regenerate_timeout.py` and `tests/test_title_aux_routing.py`: 53 passed, 1 skipped.

Manual live validation:

* Deployed commit `da383c56` to a local HermesWebUI install.
* Confirmed service health returned `{"status":"ok"}`.
* Performed a fresh page load.
* Did not open Auxiliary Model settings before testing, validating the lazy config-fetch path.
* With `auxiliary.title_generation.timeout = 180`, triggered manual title regeneration from the session menu.
* Confirmed no premature failure toast appeared at the old 30-second frontend default.
* Confirmed logs showed no relevant errors or exceptions.

## Risks / Follow-ups

* Low risk: the change is limited to the manual title-regeneration frontend request.
* If auxiliary config is missing, invalid, or cannot be fetched, the existing 30-second frontend default remains in effect.
* Compression/update routes were intentionally left unchanged because they are separate routes with existing explicit frontend timeouts and different user-facing behavior.
* A broader audit of auxiliary-model timeout handling can be done separately if maintainers want all auxiliary routes to share a common timeout helper.

## Model Used

Planning/review:

* OpenAI ChatGPT ΓÇö GPT-5.5 Thinking

HermesAgent / local orchestration:

* LM Studio ΓÇö qwen3.6-27b@iq4_nl

Codex implementation/review:

* Codex CLI/version: codex-cli 0.142.4
* Codex model: GPT 5.5 High

Manual validation:

* User performed live browser validation on a local HermesWebUI install.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5376.body:

nesquena/hermes-webui#5377.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5377.body:
## Release ΓÇö stop in-flight wakeups from reverting the picker model/provider (#4251)

PR #5370 by @rodboev. A background-task wakeup could carry the stale/default model and unconditionally overwrite `s.model`/`s.model_provider`, silently reverting a newer model-picker choice so the next turn ran on the wrong model.

### Fix (`api/streaming.py`)
Ownership is tracked as a `(model, provider)` **pair**, and the ownership snapshot + write now happen **inside `_agent_lock`** (consistent with `/api/chat/start`'s per-session lock ordering). A stale wakeup no longer owns the persisted choice when either the model or the provider has moved on; a legitimate current-turn change still persists.

### Gate (two review rounds ΓÇö this is the crown-jewel streaming path)
Round 1 I bounced with two reproduced CORE findings: a provider-only revert (ownership was model-only) and a TOCTOU hole (snapshot/write before the lock). This re-push closes both.
- **Codex: SAFE TO SHIP** ΓÇö verified same-model/different-provider stale wakeup can't clobber, read+write fully under `_agent_lock`, no lock-order inversion, legit changes still persist.
- Full suite: **11523 passed** (only the 2 pre-existing `test_scheduled_jobs_profile_isolation` serial artifacts); 6 targeted (incl. the same-model/different-provider regression) + 28 profile-provider-resolution tests.

Credit: @rodboev.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5387.body:
## Release ΓÇö opt-in extension loopback sidecar proxy (#5228, #4747)

Ships @rodboev's generic, consent-gated extensionΓåÆloopback-sidecar proxy. Nathan's mechanism decision (this session): **#5228 generic is the canonical extension-proxy mechanism; #5165 standalone bridge closed as superseded.** This is the first core-owned extension-proxy route, so `docs/EXTENSIONS.md` is updated to document the new capability (previously the doc forbade it).

### Dual-advisor gate (this session)
Ran **both** gates on the combined stage (rebased onto current master):
- **Codex (round 1): KICK BACK** ΓÇö flagged (1) auth-disabled residual behavior and (2) only GET enforced same-origin browser provenance while unsafe methods fell through the CSRF compatibility path.
- **Fable 5 (senior review): COMMENT, no blocking issues** ΓÇö built an old-vs-new provenance truth table (equal-or-stricter in every header combination, no regression), verified SSRF / path-smuggling / credential-isolation / redirect-confinement / DoS-cap all fail-closed; only asks were the CHANGELOG entry + the mechanism decision.

**Resolution:** applied the provenance hardening ΓÇö `require_provenance=True` now enforced on **every** proxied method (not just GET), with a new regression test (`test_extension_sidecar_proxy_post_requires_browser_provenance`) proving a headerless POST is rejected 403 before the resolver/opener is reached. **Codex re-gate ΓåÆ SAFE TO SHIP**, and it explicitly re-assessed the auth-disabled residual as "matches the app's current passwordless trust posture, not a new blocker" ΓÇö converging with Fable.

### Verification
- **Codex re-gate: SAFE TO SHIP** (fixed worktree, `--workdir`).
- **Fable 5: no blocking code issues.**
- **Full pytest suite: 11660 passed, 0 failures** (pre-hardening; hardening is +1 test / same-file, targeted re-run green).
- **Targeted extension tests: 79/79 passed** (includes the new provenance regression test).

### Security surface (verified by both advisors)
Loopback-only origin (SSRF-safe: hex/decimal/userinfo/port bypasses rejected) ┬╖ path traversal + URL/scheme smuggling rejected on the fully-decoded form ┬╖ consent bound to the exact declared origin (reconsent on change, 512-entry cap) ┬╖ auth+CSRF-gated consent ┬╖ credential isolation (Cookie/Authorization/CSRF/Host/Origin/Referer stripped outbound, Set-Cookie stripped inbound, hop-by-hop both ways) ┬╖ ambient proxies disabled ┬╖ redirects confined to the declared origin ┬╖ 512KB response cap on success + error paths ┬╖ browser provenance required on all methods.
