nesquena/hermes-webui#5398.title: fix(cron): stop auto-creating the Cron Jobs project without project opt-in (#5379)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5398.author: rodboev
nesquena/hermes-webui#5398.body:
## Thinking Path

- Cron already has a home in the sidebar's origin filter, so forcing every cron-heavy install through an implicit "Cron Jobs" project chip duplicates that axis for users who never touched project organization.
- `ensure_cron_project()` in api/models.py has no way to say "look but don't create", so both the sidebar scan and the session recovery endpoint always end up minting and persisting the project the first time a cron row is seen, even on a fresh install with zero projects.
- Gating creation behind whether the active profile already has a real (non-system) project keeps the decision in one place, `ensure_cron_project(create=...)`, instead of duplicating its lookup and back-tag logic at each call site.
- A pre-existing legacy untagged or renamed-root-aliased Cron Jobs project should keep resolving normally, since a project that already exists isn't a new classification being minted, so only the final create branch needed a gate, not the lookup or back-tag loops.
- Webhooks share the identical create pattern, but issue #5379 only asks about cron, and the existing webhook tests pin a zero-argument call signature for `ensure_webhook_project`, so leaving webhook ungated keeps this change small; the predicate is named generically so a webhook follow-up can reuse it.
- The sidebar scan already memoizes the cron project id per build to avoid repeat disk reads (#4842), so the memo's sentinel had to learn to cache a `None` result instead of re-reading projects.json on every cron row once the gate closes.

## What Changed

- `api/models.py`: `ensure_cron_project()` gains a `create: bool = True` parameter. After the existing per-profile lookup and legacy back-tag loop, it returns `None` instead of creating a new project when `create` is False. Direct callers that don't pass `create` keep today's behavior.
- `api/models.py`: added `_profile_has_user_projects()`, true when `load_projects()` has at least one project for the active profile (or its renamed-root alias) whose name isn't `Cron Jobs` or `Webhooks`.
- `api/models.py`: `_cron_pid()` inside `_load_cli_sessions_uncached` now calls `ensure_cron_project(create=_profile_has_user_projects())`, and its memo cache switched from a bare `[None]` sentinel to `[resolved, value]` so a gated-closed `None` result is cached instead of re-querying projects.json per cron row.
- `api/routes.py`: the session recovery endpoint's `cron_project_id = ensure_cron_project()` becomes `ensure_cron_project(create=_profile_has_user_projects())`, so a recovered cron session on a projectless install gets `project_id=None` exactly like a non-cron session already does.
- `tests/test_issue5379_cron_project_optin.py` (new): behavioral coverage for the gate through the real sidebar scan and recovery endpoint, plus preservation cases for installs that already use projects or already have a Cron Jobs project in any shape (tagged, legacy untagged, renamed-root aliased), a predicate contract test, and a negative-space check that webhook project creation is untouched.
- `tests/test_issue4385_cron_archive_reappears.py`: one mock updated from `lambda: "cron-project"` to `lambda **_: "cron-project"` since `_cron_pid()` now passes the `create` keyword.
- `tests/test_issue3930_source_filter_pushdown.py`: the two `ensure_cron_project` mock lambdas gain `**_` for the same reason; the cron-rescue-limit test there feeds a real cron row through the scan, so its strict zero-arg mock would otherwise raise `TypeError`. No assertions change.

## Why It Matters

Installs that never created a project no longer get a surprise "Cron Jobs" chip and a projects.json write just from having cron output show up in the sidebar. Installs that already use projects, or already have a Cron Jobs project in any shape, keep working exactly as before, and cron rows keep their source badge and origin-filter classification either way.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_issue5379_cron_project_optin.py tests/test_1079_cron_session_project.py tests/test_issue3019_cron_project_sessions.py tests/test_issue1614_project_profile_filtering.py tests/test_webhook_project_sessions.py tests/test_issue4842_cron_projection_perf.py tests/test_issue4385_cron_archive_reappears.py tests/test_issue3930_source_filter_pushdown.py tests/test_issue3585_cron_session_overflow.py tests/test_issue3586_cli_session_source_label.py -v --timeout=60`
- Base-check context: `tests/test_issue5379_cron_project_optin.py` goes base-red on the current `origin/master` shape for the zero-project cron auto-create path, and passes on this branch.

Full-suite CI context, not a required local check unless requested: `pytest tests/ -v --timeout=60`.

## Upstream

Closes #5379. Implements the backend half of the split discussed on the issue; the origin-filter default (point 3 there) is a separate frontend change.

## Model Used

GPT 5.5 via Codex CLI

nesquena/hermes-webui#5399.title: fix(sessions): always retry sidebar session-list GET on 502/503/504 (#5394)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5399.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5399.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5394. The sidebar session list would get stuck after a transient 502
during a profile switch (or any warm refresh) and stay stale until a hard
reload (Ctrl+F5).

## The bug

`_runRenderSessionListRefresh()` in `static/sessions.js` already had
502/503/504 retry logic for the sidebar session-list GET ΓÇö but it was gated
to **cold boot only**. Once the first load succeeded, `_sessionListHasLoadedOnce`
flipped to `true`, so every later refresh (profile switch, focus/visible/
reconnect) shipped **no `retryStatuses`**. A transient 502 during an
nginxΓåÆbackend restart window then failed on the first attempt, leaving the
conversations list stale until the user hard-reloaded.

## Root cause (localized)

The retry options (`retries` + `retryStatuses`) lived inside the
`if(!_sessionListHasLoadedOnce){ ΓÇª }` boot gate alongside the large boot
timeout, so warm refreshes never retried transient upstream errors.

## The fix

The session-list GET is idempotent, so retrying it is safe unconditionally.
This moves `retries:1` + `retryStatuses:[502,503,504]` into the base request
options so they apply on **every** refresh, while the boot-only path keeps the
larger `_SESSION_LIST_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS` timeout + `retryTimeouts`:

```js
const sessionRequestOpts={
  timeoutToast:false,
  retries:1,
  retryStatuses:[502,503,504],
};
if(!_sessionListHasLoadedOnce){
  sessionRequestOpts.timeoutMs=_SESSION_LIST_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  sessionRequestOpts.retryTimeouts=true;
}
```

The `api()` wrapper in `static/workspace.js` already retries when the error
status is in `retryStatuses`, so no other change is needed. The `/api/projects`
fallback and all other logic are untouched ΓÇö one localized block.

## Test

Extended the existing source-string regression test
(`test_sessions_api_always_retries_transient_upstream_statuses_and_boot_keeps_longer_timeout`
in `tests/test_session_sidebar_resilience.py`) to assert `retries:1` and
`retryStatuses:[502,503,504]` are declared **before** the boot-only gate (i.e.
always present), while the boot path still carries the timeout + timeout retry.
Adjusted one substring assertion in `tests/test_performance_polling_hardening.py`
to match the reformatted opts object.

All related sidebar/session tests pass:

```
tests/test_session_sidebar_resilience.py
tests/test_performance_polling_hardening.py
tests/test_issue4759_parallel_sidebar_boot_fetch.py
tests/test_api_timeout.py
tests/test_issue4766_sidebar_source_pushdown.py
ΓåÆ 38 passed
```

## Credit

Reported and precisely root-caused by @weidzhou, who traced the boot-only
retry gate. Credited as co-author on the commit.

## Release note

Sidebar session list now retries transient 502/503/504 upstream errors on
every refresh (not just cold boot), so a brief backend restart during a
profile switch no longer leaves the conversations list stale.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5401.title: Release: #5398 ΓÇö stop auto-creating Cron Jobs project without opt-in (#5379)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5401.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5401.body:
## Release: #5398 ΓÇö stop auto-creating the "Cron Jobs" project without opt-in (closes #5379)

Ships the gate-cleared rebase of #5398 (author **@rodboev**) onto current master.

### What it fixes
Issue #5379: on a profile with **no user projects**, opening the sidebar source filter ΓÇö or importing CLI sessions ΓÇö would silently mint a phantom "Cron Jobs" project just to group cron rows, cluttering a filter the user never opted into.

### The fix
- `ensure_cron_project()` gains a `create` gate placed **after** the exact-tag lookup, renamed-root alias match, and legacy-untagged back-tag loop ΓÇö so an **existing** cron project still resolves and back-tags normally; only minting a **brand-new** one is suppressed.
- New read-only `_profile_has_user_projects()` mirrors the same profile/alias matching; both production callers (sidebar scan, CLI-import recovery) pass `create=_profile_has_user_projects()`.
- Cache sentinel `[None]` ΓåÆ `[False, None]` distinguishes unresolved vs resolved-to-None, preserving the #4842 per-scan single-invocation guard.
- The webhook project path is intentionally left ungated (scope-limited to cron per #5379); a follow-up will track the identical webhook-chip inconsistency.

### Gate (all three legs, on live head `e0b3ab03`)
- **Full suite:** 11755 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_issue1567` Nous-portal fetch, verified failing identically on clean master ΓÇö not introduced).
- **Codex (regression gate):** SAFE TO SHIP ΓÇö existing cron projects resolve before the no-create return; None cached; recovery tolerates None.
- **Opus (senior advisor, adaptive/max):** SAFE-TO-SHIP ΓÇö validated all four claims, ran 258 blast-radius tests on the head (base-red / head-green confirmed), found the modified `test_issue3172` fixture actually **fixes** a pre-existing test-pollution bug rather than introducing one.

Attribution: original work by @rodboev; cherry-picked with authorship preserved.

nesquena/hermes-webui#5405.title: Release v0.51.823: #5162 default message mode rename + steer default (#5145)
nesquena/hermes-webui#5405.author: nesquena-hermes
nesquena/hermes-webui#5405.body:
## Release v0.51.823 ΓÇö #5162 default message mode: rename + steer default (closes #5145)

Ships the maintainer-reconciled rebase of #5162 (@rodboev) onto current master.

### What it does
- Renames the Settings ΓåÆ Preferences control "Busy input mode" ΓåÆ **"Default message mode."**
- Flips the default for **fresh/never-configured installs** from `queue` to **`steer`** (inject a mid-turn correction without interrupting).
- Existing users keep their saved mode (Queue/Interrupt/Steer) ΓÇö the migration treats a saved `busy_input_mode` as an explicit preference and carries it over unchanged.

### Reconciliation note (why this is a maintainer rebase, not the raw PR)
#5162 was authored before #5170 shipped. #5170 added a localStorage persistence mirror (so a saved mode survives reload / brief server outage ΓÇö #5167/#5132). The raw PR would have dropped that. This branch reconciles them: the mirror machinery is renamed site-for-site (`_persistDefaultMessageMode`/`_readPersistedDefaultMessageMode`, new key `hermes-default-message-mode` with legacy `hermes-busy-input-mode` fallback), the load-failure path still reads the persisted pref (not a hardcoded default), and config.py migrates a legacy `busy_input_mode` to `default_message_mode` before the enum filter. Authorship preserved (Co-authored-by @rodboev).

### Gate (all three, on reconciled head)
- **Full suite:** 11,765 passed (1 pre-existing `test_issue1567` Nous-cli-unavailable flake, identical on clean master ΓÇö not introduced).
- **Codex:** SAFE-TO-SHIP ΓÇö zero leftover old-symbol refs, #5170 mirror preserved, legacy migration verified, send-path intact.
- **Opus (adaptive/max):** SHIP-WITH-FIXES = the CHANGELOG entry (added here). Verified all migration paths empirically (ran load/save against a scratch state dir). Confirmed intent: the flip reaches fresh installs only (grandfathering) ΓÇö maintainer-approved.

### Visual sign-off
Screenshots (new default = Steer for fresh installs; existing saved Queue preserved) reviewed and approved by the maintainer via Telegram.

stablyai/orca#1321.title: fix(browser): clean up closed browser sessions and webviews
stablyai/orca#1321.author: Nikolatesla-lj
stablyai/orca#1321.body:
## Summary

- Close the named `agent-browser` session when a browser tab closes.
- Track live browser webviews by browser page id, which is how the webview registry is keyed.
- Tear down webviews when browser page records disappear through store-only paths such as CLI tab close or worktree deletion.

## Why

Orca browser automation has two resources per browser page:

1. a named `agent-browser` session like `orca-tab-<browserPageId>` in the main process;
2. the renderer-owned `<webview>` DOM node and its Chromium guest process.

The tab close path could miss both layers in different cases:

- `AgentBrowserBridge.onTabClosed()` called `agent-browser close` without `--session`, which closes the default session instead of the page's named session.
- The renderer cleanup subscriber watched workspace ids, but actual webviews are keyed by browser page ids. When browser page records were removed through store-only paths, the corresponding webview could remain parked and continue holding Chromium/GPU resources.

This is intended to reduce leaked `agent-browser` daemon processes and leaked Chromium guest/GPU resources during long agent-browser runs that repeatedly create and close tabs.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-webview-cleanup.test.ts src/renderer/src/hooks/useIpcEvents.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.web.json --composite false`
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.node.json --composite false`
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.ts src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.test.ts src/renderer/src/components/Terminal.tsx src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-webview-cleanup.ts src/renderer/src/components/browser-pane/browser-webview-cleanup.test.ts`

Note: A full `pnpm test -- ...` run was not used for targeted verification because that command runs the entire suite in this environment. The full suite currently hits unrelated native-module failures caused by Node 22 running against dependencies rebuilt for Node 24 (`better-sqlite3` NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch).

Supersedes #1311.

stablyai/orca#1326.title: fix(runtime): add single-instance lock + owned-metadata clear (#1312)
stablyai/orca#1326.author: Jinwoo-H
stablyai/orca#1326.body:
## Summary

Closes #1312. Orca v1.3.24 never called `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`, so every AppImage/.app relaunch booted a fresh Electron main that clobbered `<userData>/orca-runtime.json` and `agent-hooks/endpoint.env`. When the newest instance quit, metadata pointed at a dead pid and `orca status` reported `stale_bootstrap` even though the original Orca was still running. SIGKILL'd predecessors also left orphaned `o-<pid>-*.sock` files accumulating in userData.

Three surgical changes:

1. **Single-instance lock** ΓÇö new `src/main/startup/single-instance-lock.ts` helper invoked after `configureDevUserDataPath(is.dev)` so dev (`orca-dev`) and packaged (`orca`) runs lock in separate namespaces. Losing instances focus the primary's window via `second-instance` and exit without touching userData.
2. **Ownership-guarded metadata clear on clean exit** ΓÇö `clearRuntimeMetadataIfOwned(userData, pid, runtimeId)` compares both pid AND runtimeId against the current file before clearing, so the auto-updater handoff window never erases the replacement process's fresh bootstrap. Called from a rewritten `will-quit` handler that folds `runtimeRpc.stop()` + owned-clear into the same `Promise.allSettled([disconnectDaemon, rpcStopAndClear]).then(app.quit)` chain ΓÇö all inside the `!daemonDisconnectDone` guard so the second-pass re-entry can't re-invoke stop+clear.
3. **Orphaned-socket sweep on startup** ΓÇö `sweepOrphanedRuntimeSockets()` runs at the top of `OrcaRuntimeRpcServer.start()` on POSIX, using `process.kill(pid, 0)` to probe liveness and remove `o-<dead-pid>-*.sock` orphans left by SIGKILL/OOM-kill. Named-pipe transports on Windows don't leave filesystem entries, so the sweep is a no-op there.

Design doc: `docs/fix-missing-single-instance-lock.md` (includes architecture diagrams, data flow for auto-updater handoff, testing strategy, and the regression-watch for the intended transient `not_running` window during an auto-update).

## Why the ownership guard is not over-engineering

`autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` quits the old process immediately and relaunches. The new process may already be starting (writing its own metadata) while the old `will-quit` is running. An unconditional clear would delete the new process's fresh metadata. The guard makes both orderings (old-clears-first and new-writes-first) safe by construction.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/startup/single-instance-lock.test.ts` ΓÇö 3 tests: lock-failed does not register listener; lock-acquired registers exactly one; callback dispatches.
- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/runtime-metadata.test.ts` ΓÇö +4 tests for `clearRuntimeMetadataIfOwned` (matched / pid-mismatch / runtimeId-mismatch / no-file).
- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/runtime-socket-sweep.test.ts` ΓÇö 4 tests: `ownPid=1` cleanly separates own-pid-skipped / alive-non-own-retained / dead-swept / regex-miss branches; two regex-invariant tests assert the sweep regex matches `createRuntimeTransportMetadata` output (real runtimeId + `'rt'` fallback).
- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/runtime-rpc.test.ts` ΓÇö existing 10 tests still pass; the new sweep step in `start()` does not regress any existing behavior.
- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` ΓÇö clean (node, cli, web).
- [x] `pnpm run lint` ΓÇö clean (oxlint).
- [ ] Manual repro on packaged macOS/Linux build:
  - [ ] Launch packaged Orca, note `~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json` mtime. Launch again: existing window focuses, mtime unchanged, no new window appears.
  - [ ] Quit cleanly: `~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json` is removed and `orca status --json` reports `runtime.state = 'not_running'` (not `'stale_bootstrap'`).
  - [ ] `kill -9` a running Orca; next launch removes the orphan `o-<killed-pid>-*.sock` from userData.
  - [ ] Auto-update: during `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()`, `orca status` transitions `ready` ΓåÆ `not_running` (~1s) ΓåÆ `starting` ΓåÆ `ready` (this `not_running` transient is intended, documented in the design doc's regression-watch).
- [ ] Manual dev-mode verification: run `pnpm dev` twice; second invocation exits immediately with `[single-instance] Another Orca instance is already running...` log, first stays running.

## Reviewer notes

- The will-quit chain uses `Promise.allSettled` (not `Promise.all`) so a `disconnectDaemon()` rejection still lets us quit instead of hanging the app.
- `ownedPid`/`ownedRuntimeId` are captured synchronously (before any `await`) so the ownership comparison is stable even if shutdown nulls globals mid-chain.
- The sweep regex `^o-(\d+)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.sock$` is covered by a dedicated invariant test so any future change to the `createRuntimeTransportMetadata` socket-name shape trips CI.
- At module top level TypeScript forbids a literal `return`, so losing instances gate the file-writing init (`initDataPath` et al.) behind `if (hasSingleInstanceLock)` and let lifecycle handlers register unconditionally. Functionally safe: `app.quit()` prevents `whenReady` from firing, so `runtime`/`runtimeRpc`/`store`/`stats` stay `null` and every shutdown handler short-circuits via optional chaining. The design doc reflects this pattern.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) ≡ƒÉï

stablyai/orca#1396.body:
## Summary
- add browser tab profile controls to the Orca CLI
- add browser tab inspection and profile automation primitives
- keep the command surface under `tab` / `tab profile`

## What changed
- added `orca tab create --profile <id>`
- added `orca tab list --show-profile`
- added `orca tab profile set --page <id> --profile <id>`
- added `orca tab show --page <id>`
- added `orca tab current [--worktree <selector|all>]`
- added `orca tab profile show --page <id>`
- added `orca tab profile use-default --page <id>`
- added `orca tab profile clone --profile <id> [--page <id>] [--worktree <selector>]`
- threaded `sessionProfileId` through guest registration so tab profile state is visible to CLI automation

## Why
Orca already has browser session profile support in the UI and runtime state, but the CLI could not reliably control or inspect that state.

This PR focuses on the tab-scoped controls that automation needs:
- choose a profile when opening a tab
- inspect the current tab and its bound profile
- switch a tab back to the default profile
- clone the current page into a different profile without mutating the original tab

It intentionally does not add profile lifecycle commands or any round-robin policy layer.

## Tests
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cli/browser.test.ts src/cli/index.test.ts src/main/browser/browser-manager.test.ts src/main/browser/agent-browser-bridge.test.ts`

stablyai/orca#2542.title: fix(linux): resolve symlink and probe orca-ide in CLI wrapper
stablyai/orca#2542.author: maco222
stablyai/orca#2542.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2539. The Linux CLI wrapper (`resources/linux/bin/orca`) has been broken on every `.deb`/AppImage since v1.4.2-rc.0 (#1306 / 543d9a6c). Two issues:

1. **Wrong binary name.** The wrapper probes `$APP_DIR/orca` and `$APP_DIR/Orca`, but #1306 set `executableName: 'orca-ide'` on Linux (to avoid Ubuntu's GNOME Orca package). Actual binary: `/opt/Orca/orca-ide`.
2. **Symlink not resolved.** `APP_DIR` is computed from `dirname BASH_SOURCE` without `readlink`. When invoked via the `~/.local/bin/orca` symlink that `CliInstaller` creates, `APP_DIR=$HOME`, and `[ -x "$HOME/orca" ]` matches `$HOME/orca/` as a directory (bash `-x` is true for traversable dirs), producing `Is a directory` on exec. `resources/darwin/bin/orca` already handles this via `app_realpath()`; Linux never got the equivalent.

Fix: walk the symlink chain (same shape as the macOS wrapper) before computing `APP_DIR`, probe `orca-ide` first, and gate the candidate with `-f` so a same-named directory cannot match.

## Screenshots

No visual change ΓÇö CLI shell script.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` ΓÇö clean.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` ΓÇö fails on `origin/main` as well, on unrelated `editor/RichMarkdown*` modules (missing `emoji-picker-react` / `@tiptap/extension-mathematics`). Pre-existing, not introduced here.
- [ ] `pnpm test` ΓÇö skipped: shell-only change, no JS/TS touched.
- [ ] `pnpm build` ΓÇö skipped for the same reason; the wrapper is shipped via electron-builder `extraResources` and isn't processed by the Vite/electron build.
- [x] **Local repro** of the packaged install layout, exercising all three paths:
  - Direct invocation (`$APP_DIR/resources/bin/orca --help`) ΓåÆ finds `orca-ide`, execs with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` and the expected CLI path.
  - Symlink invocation from `$HOME/.local/bin/orca` (with a `$HOME/orca/` directory trap present) ΓåÆ resolves the symlink, finds `orca-ide` in the real `$APP_DIR`, no longer falls through to the `$HOME/orca` directory.
  - Missing binary ΓåÆ exits 1 with the existing `Unable to locate the Orca executableΓÇª` message.
- [x] `bash -n resources/linux/bin/orca` ΓÇö syntax OK.

The packaged-install reproduction in #2539 is what was missing from CI: the `.deb` is built but never invoked with `--help`. Adding such a smoke test is out of scope here, but worth tracking ΓÇö happy to follow up.

## AI Review Report

Reviewed with Claude Opus 4.7. Risks checked:

- **Cross-platform compatibility:** change is confined to `resources/linux/bin/orca`. `resources/darwin/bin/orca` and `resources/win32/bin/orca.cmd` are untouched. The symlink-resolution loop matches the darwin wrapper's existing `app_realpath()` shape so the two platforms stay structurally aligned. Windows uses a separate `.cmd` launcher with its own path canonicalization (#282) and is unaffected.
- **Shell behavior:** `set -euo pipefail` preserved. The `ELECTRON=""` initialization is required because `set -u` would otherwise make the post-loop `[ -z "$ELECTRON" ]` check fault when no candidate matches. The probe order (`orca-ide` ΓåÆ `orca` ΓåÆ `Orca`) is conservative: it prefers the current Linux name first, but still works for any older artifact that may exist in the wild.
- **Directory-vs-file ambiguity:** the `-f` guard alongside `-x` rejects directories (the original `Is a directory` failure mode). Verified in the local repro by leaving a `$HOME/orca/` directory in place during the symlink-invocation test.
- **Symlink chain semantics:** the `while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]` loop is the same idiom used in `resources/darwin/bin/orca`, which is already in production.

## Security Audit

- **Path handling:** all path computation goes through `cd ΓÇª && pwd`, which fails closed on missing/permission-denied directories under `set -e`. No string concatenation of user-controlled input ΓÇö `BASH_SOURCE` is the only input and is bounded by the install layout.
- **Command execution:** the final `exec` target is gated by `-f && -x` checks, so the wrapper cannot accidentally exec a directory or a non-binary. Argument forwarding (`"$@"`) is already quoted correctly.
- **Symlink traversal:** the loop follows `readlink` one hop at a time; relative targets are resolved against the symlink's directory before re-checking, matching the macOS wrapper. No `realpath -e`/`-f` reliance, so behavior is consistent across coreutils variants.
- **Env handling:** unchanged. The existing `NODE_OPTIONS` / `NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE` save-and-unset dance is preserved.
- No new secrets, network, or IPC surfaces introduced.

## Notes

- Linux-only fix; macOS and Windows paths are untouched.
- The bug ships in every release from v1.4.2-rc.0 through v1.4.16 ΓÇö worth picking into the next patch.
- Related observation, not fixed here: `resources/linux/bin/orca` is checked into git with mode `100644`, while `resources/darwin/bin/orca` is `100755`. Doesn't affect the packaged artifact (electron-builder/CliInstaller end up handling the bit), but it's an inconsistency worth a follow-up.

stablyai/orca#6574.body:
## ≡ƒºæΓÇì≡ƒñ¥ΓÇì≡ƒºæ Impact & ELI5

**1) What's broken today (ELI5).** If you use "Add Project ΓåÆ Browse folder" and pick a folder _inside_ a git repository ΓÇö for example one package inside a monorepo like `/tmp/monorepo/packages/web` ΓÇö Orca ignores the folder you actually chose. Both the file/source-control panel and the first terminal silently jump up to the top of the repo (`/tmp/monorepo`) instead of staying in `packages/web`. The project even shows up under the wrong name (the repo's name, not the subfolder's). It's not a crash, but it's a confusing "I clicked X and got Y" surprise that hits anyone working in a monorepo or any nested project layout ΓÇö a common setup. Notably, doing the same thing through the macOS Finder "New Orca Workspace Here" menu already worked correctly, so the two ways of opening the same folder behaved differently.

**2) What this PR does (ELI5).** Two fixes working together. First, when you import a folder that lives inside a git repo, Orca now honestly records the project at the real top of the repo (because git operations only make sense from there) ΓÇö and if you'd already imported that repo, it just reuses it instead of creating a confusing duplicate. Second, and this is the part that fixes the surprise: it remembers the exact subfolder you picked and opens your _first_ terminal right there. So instead of "I picked `packages/web` and landed at the repo root," it's now "I picked `packages/web` and my terminal opens in `packages/web`," while the source-control view still tracks the whole repo (which is correct). The subfolder is used once, for that first terminal only; new split panes open at the repo root as before. If you pick the repo root itself, nothing special happens.

**3) Tradeoffs / regressions ΓÇö honest answer.** No regressions for existing behavior. Nothing is disabled, no flag is turned off, no setting changes, and you don't have to do anything new. A few honest nuances worth naming, none of them a downside for users:
  - The project's stored path and display name for a subfolder import now change from the subfolder to the repo root. That's the _intended_ correction (the old behavior was the bug), and it matches what already happened in practice ΓÇö git always snapped to the repo root anyway; now the project name and identity finally agree with that instead of mismatching.
  - Importing a subfolder of an already-imported repo now correctly returns the existing project instead of silently making a duplicate ΓÇö strictly better.
  - The "open my first terminal in the picked subfolder" behavior is one-shot by design: only the first terminal created during activation lands in the subfolder; later split panes open at the repo root. This is a deliberate scope choice, not a bug, and matches the existing Finder-menu behavior.
  - Each git import now runs one extra quick local git command (`rev-parse --show-toplevel`) to find the repo root. This is negligible and only happens at import time, not during normal use.
  - The fix is cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows) and also covers the SSH/remote import path, so no platform is left behind.

---

## Summary

Fixes #6336.

Add Project ΓåÆ Browse folder on a **monorepo subfolder** (e.g. `/tmp/monorepo/packages/web`) used to store the subfolder as `Repo.path`. Because `isGitRepo()` relies on `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` ΓÇö which returns `true` for *any* subdirectory of a worktree ΓÇö the subfolder was accepted as the repo path, but authoritative worktree resolution (`git worktree list` / `--show-toplevel`) then snapped activation back to the repo root. The result was a mismatched import identity and the first terminal opening at the repo root instead of the selected subfolder.

This change:

1. **Canonicalizes local git imports to the real repo root** via a new `getGitRepoRoot()` in `src/main/git/repo.ts` (`rev-parse --show-toplevel`, normalized with `normalizeRuntimePathSeparators`). `addLocalRepoFromPath` resolves the root before storing, mirroring the existing SSH import path that already snaps to `check.rootPath`, including the same post-resolution dedup so re-importing a subfolder of an existing project returns the existing repo instead of adding a duplicate.
2. **Preserves the user-selected subfolder as a one-shot initial terminal cwd** for *only* the first activation-created pane. The dialog now forwards `selectedPath`; `openProjectDefaultCheckout` keeps it only when it is genuinely *inside* the resolved worktree (`relativePathInsideRoot`), queues it via `queueTabInitialCwd`, and the terminal-pane lifecycle consumes it exactly once (cleared after the first pane and on orphan cleanup). Selecting the repo root itself applies **no** override.

This supersedes community PR #6362 (original author credited via `Co-authored-by`). I took over that PR, re-implemented/verified it against current `main`, and corrected one defect: the `getGitRepoRoot` worktree-root test asserted against a non-canonicalized tmp path, which fails on macOS where `--show-toplevel` resolves the `/var ΓåÆ /private/var` symlink. The test now derives its expected root from git's own `--show-toplevel` so it is correct on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

## Screenshots

Live Electron repro (dev build over CDP) against this branch. The terminal PTY could **not** spawn in this validation environment because `node_modules` is symlinked from the primary checkout and node-pty's native `spawn-helper` was built for a now-deleted worktree path (`DaemonProtocolError: ... spawn-helper ... ENOENT`), so the live terminal-cwd half is proven by unit tests + the live store one-shot queue/consume round-trip rather than a rendered prompt.

What the screenshot shows: importing the subfolder `/tmp/monorepo/packages/web` created a project rooted at the git repo root ΓÇö the source-control panel reports branch `master` / "No changes on this branch ΓÇª ahead of master" (git operations resolve against the repo root), and the project appears as `monorepo` (the repo-root basename), not `web`.

_Screenshots attached in a PR comment below._

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint` ΓÇö `oxlint` clean on changed files; full `oxlint` shows only one pre-existing warning in an untouched file (`useGitStatusPolling.ts`). No `max-lines` regressions.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` ΓÇö `tsgo -p config/tsconfig.node.json` and `tsgo -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json` both clean.
- [x] `pnpm test` ΓÇö ran the 8 targeted suites: `repo-detection.test.ts`, `repos-remote.test.ts`, `AddProjectFromFolderDialog.test.tsx`, `project-added-default-checkout.test.ts`, `worktree-activation.test.ts`, `use-terminal-pane-lifecycle.test.ts`, `terminal-link-handlers.test.ts`, `store-cascades.test.ts` ΓåÆ **333 passed**.
- [ ] `pnpm build` ΓÇö not run (full desktop build out of scope for this environment; typecheck for both projects is green).
- [x] Added/updated tests that catch this regression (worktree-root canonicalization + dedup, root-pick no-override, one-shot cwd queue/consume + orphan cleanup, pane-link cwd).

## AI Review Report

Reviewed for correctness, edge cases, cross-platform behavior, and elegance.

- **Correctness:** `getGitRepoRoot` only runs for `kind === 'git'` (folder imports keep their literal path). The post-resolution dedup fires only when the resolved key differs from the input key, exactly mirroring the SSH path. The one-shot cwd is consumed by the first pane, then reset to the default tab cwd so later splits land at the repo root; it is also deleted on orphan cleanup and tab teardown.
- **Cross-platform (macOS / Linux / Windows):** path handling goes through the existing Windows-aware helpers `normalizeRuntimePathSeparators` and `relativePathInsideRoot`; no hardcoded separators, no `metaKey`, no UI/shortcut changes. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns forward slashes on Windows, consistent with the normalizer.
- **SSH / remote:** the dialog passes `selectedPath` for `ssh_remote_path` too; remote root canonicalization already existed via `check.rootPath`, and `relativePathInsideRoot` works on remote-flavored paths.
- **Provider-agnostic:** no GitHub-specific assumptions; only git plumbing and renderer state.
- **Flagged & fixed:** the adopted test's worktree-root assertion was macOS-symlink-fragile; rewritten to derive the expected root from git.

## Security Audit

I re-audited the adopted code assuming the original author was hostile.

- **Command execution:** `getGitRepoRoot` calls `gitExecFileSync` with fixed argv (`['rev-parse', '--is-inside-work-tree']`, `['rev-parse', '--show-toplevel']`); `gitExecFileSync` uses `execFileSync` (no shell). User input is only the `cwd`. No injection vector. (On Windows/WSL the runner builds a `bash -c` string but escapes every token via `quotePosixShell`, and these args are hardcoded.)
- **Path handling:** no traversal ΓÇö the subfolder cwd override only applies when `relativePathInsideRoot` confirms containment inside the resolved worktree.
- **Secrets / network / eval / deps:** none touched. No new dependencies.
- **IPC:** `repos:add` is unchanged in shape; it now returns the canonical root path, which is the intended fix.

No follow-up required.

## Notes

- Supersedes community PR #6362; original author credited via `Co-authored-by`. Their PR is left open per process.
- **Future suggestions (out of scope, not in this diff):** the same `getGitRepoRoot` canonicalization could be applied to other local import entry points (e.g. drag-and-drop / recent-folder reopen) if any bypass `addLocalRepoFromPath`; worth a follow-up audit.

thedotmack/claude-mem#58.body:
## Summary

Adds a complete web-based viewer UI accessible at `http://localhost:37777/` that provides real-time visualization of claude-mem's memory stream. This allows users to see observations, summaries, and prompts as they are created, with live connection status and processing indicators.

## Key Features

### Real-Time Memory Stream
- **Live SSE updates**: Server-Sent Events stream all observations, summaries, and user prompts as they're created

thedotmack/claude-mem#754.title: Document MCP connection lifecycle - No constant uvx spawning
thedotmack/claude-mem#754.author: app/copilot-swe-agent
thedotmack/claude-mem#754.body:
Investigation revealed we **are** using MCP SDK correctly. ChromaSync spawns `uvx chroma-mcp` once per worker lifetime and reuses the connection for all operations via `ensureConnection()` guard clause.

## Changes

**Source code documentation**
- ChromaSync.ts: Header and method comments explaining singleton pattern and connection reuse
- DatabaseManager.ts: Lifecycle documentation for singleton ChromaSync instance

**Architecture documentation**
- `docs/architecture/mcp-connection-lifecycle.md`: Technical analysis of connection flow, MCP SDK behavior, performance implications
- `docs/investigations/2026-01-18-mcp-uvx-spawning.md`: Investigation summary and resolution

**Logging improvements**
- Debug logs now emit "Reusing existing MCP connection (no new spawn)" on cached path
- Info logs clarify subprocess spawn vs connection reuse

## Key Pattern

```typescript
private async ensureConnection(): Promise<void> {
  // Early return prevents respawn - connection reused for all operations
  if (this.connected && this.client) {
    logger.debug('CHROMA_SYNC', 'Reusing existing MCP connection (no new spawn)');
    return;
  }
  
  // Spawns uvx subprocess only on first call
  this.transport = new StdioClientTransport({ command: 'uvx', ... });
  await this.client.connect(this.transport);
  this.connected = true;
}
```

Worker spawns 1 uvx process, not N. This matches `StdioClientTransport` design for persistent stdio servers.

thedotmack/claude-mem#765.title: fix: prevent creation of spurious directories for CLAUDE.md files
thedotmack/claude-mem#765.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#765.body:
## Summary

Fixes the issue where `writeClaudeMdToFolder` would create entire directory structures even when paths were malformed, causing spurious folders like:
- `apps/backend/apps/web/...`
- `apps/web/apps/backend/...`
- `src/` at project root

## Problem

The function used `mkdirSync({ recursive: true })` which blindly creates any directory structure passed to it. When malformed or relative paths were passed (e.g., from JSON parsing errors in `files_modified`/`files_read`), this created garbage directory trees filled with empty CLAUDE.md files.

## Solution

Changed to check `existsSync(folderPath)` first and skip if the folder doesn't exist:

```typescript
// Before
mkdirSync(folderPath, { recursive: true });

// After
if (!existsSync(folderPath)) {
  logger.debug('FOLDER_INDEX', 'Skipping non-existent folder', { folderPath });
  return;
}
```

This is safer because:
1. CLAUDE.md context files should only exist in actual project folders
2. Malformed paths won't create garbage directory structures
3. The function remains idempotent for existing folders

## Related Issues

- Fixes #641 - Observation system creates CLAUDE.md files in duplicate nested directories
- Fixes #582 - Tilde paths create literal ~ directories instead of expanding to home
- Related to #758 - Creates empty CLAUDE.md files in all folders

- [x] All 36 tests passing

thedotmack/claude-mem#739.title: fix: prevent orphaned Claude/chroma-mcp process accumulation with periodic cleanup
thedotmack/claude-mem#739.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#739.body:
## Summary

This PR comprehensively fixes orphaned process accumulation that causes OOM crashes over time. It addresses three related issues:

### 1. Periodic orphan cleanup (NEW)
- Added `setInterval` that runs cleanup every **15 minutes**
- Cleans both `chroma-mcp` and `Claude CLI` orphaned processes automatically
- Prevents accumulation even when worker daemon runs for days without restart
- Interval is properly cleared on graceful shutdown

### 2. Startup orphan cleanup
- On worker daemon startup, immediately clean any orphaned processes from previous sessions
- Extends existing `cleanupOrphanedProcesses()` for chroma-mcp
- Adds new `cleanupOrphanedClaudeProcesses()` for Claude CLI subprocesses
- Uses `pgrep -f` pattern matching for reliable process detection

### 3. Race condition fix in crash recovery
- Added `restartPending` flag to ActiveSession to track when a crash-recovery restart is scheduled
- `ensureGeneratorRunning` now checks this flag and skips starting a new generator if restart is pending
- Prevents multiple generators (and Claude processes) from being spawned during 1-second restart delay

## Root cause

The worker daemon spawns Claude CLI subprocesses for SDK agents. These subprocesses were not being cleaned up when:
1. Sessions ended abnormally (crash, SIGKILL, etc.)
2. Worker daemon ran for extended periods without restart
3. Race conditions during crash recovery spawned duplicate processes

Over time, dozens of orphaned processes would accumulate, each consuming 50-100MB RAM, eventually causing OOM.

## Solution

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Worker Daemon                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  On Startup:                                            │
│    → cleanupOrphanedProcesses() [chroma-mcp]            │
│    → cleanupOrphanedClaudeProcesses() [Claude CLI]      │
│                                                         │
│  Every 15 minutes:                                      │
│    → setInterval runs both cleanup functions            │
│                                                         │
│  On Shutdown:                                           │
│    → clearInterval() stops periodic cleanup             │
│    → graceful shutdown of active sessions               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Files changed
- `worker-service.ts`: Add periodic cleanup with setInterval (15 min)
- `ProcessManager.ts`: Add `cleanupOrphanedClaudeProcesses()` function
- `GracefulShutdown.ts`: Ensure cleanup on shutdown
- `SessionRoutes.ts`: Add `restartPending` flag for race condition fix
- `worker-types.ts`: Add `restartPending` to ActiveSession interface

- [x] Verify periodic cleanup logs appear every 15 minutes
- [x] Run worker daemon for extended period (24h+) without accumulation

- Ubuntu Linux (6.8 kernel)
- Node.js v22
- Bun 1.3.5
- Claude Code 2.1.11

**Before (after 24h of usage):**

$ ps aux | grep claude | wc -l

```

**After (with periodic cleanup):**

```

## Related Issues

> **Upstream fix proposed:** [anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript#142](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/issues/142)

This PR implements a **workaround** (periodic cleanup) for orphaned processes. The **root cause fix** would be in the Claude Agent SDK itself, using `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` to auto-terminate child processes when the parent dies.

thedotmack/claude-mem#790.title: fix: reset aborted controller when reusing cached session
thedotmack/claude-mem#790.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#790.body:
## Summary

- Fixes a bug where the Generator would immediately abort after a previous failure
- When a Generator fails, the session's `abortController` gets aborted but was never reset when the session was reused
- New Generator starts would immediately exit because `signal.aborted` was still `true`

## Root Cause

When a cached session is returned from `SessionManager.initializeSession()`, the `abortController` was not being checked/reset. This caused a loop where:

1. Generator fails → abortController.abort() is called
2. New request comes → session is reused from cache
3. New Generator starts → immediately sees `signal.aborted = true` → exits
4. Log shows: "Generator auto-starting" → "Generator aborted" (8ms apart)

## Fix

- Check if `abortController.signal.aborted` is `true` when returning a cached session
- Only reset if `generatorPromise === null` (to avoid race conditions with active generators)
- Log a warning if aborted controller found but generator still active (shouldn't happen, but useful for diagnostics)

- [ ] Manually test: cause a Generator failure, then send new observation, verify Generator restarts successfully
- [ ] Verify no "Generator aborted" immediately after "Generator auto-starting" in logs
- [ ] Check for new log message: "Resetting aborted controller for existing session"

thedotmack/claude-mem#771.title: fix: handle stdin unavailability and timeout to prevent hook hangs
thedotmack/claude-mem#771.author: rajivsinclair
thedotmack/claude-mem#771.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the critical issue where PostToolUse hooks hang indefinitely at "Running PostToolUse hooks… (1/2 done)", making claude-mem unusable.

**Fixes:** #727, Addresses #646

## Root Cause Analysis

Two distinct issues cause hooks to hang or crash:

1. **Bun stdin crash (#646)**: When Claude Code spawns a hook process, it may not provide a valid stdin file descriptor. Bun's lazy initialization calls `fstat()` on stdin, which fails with `EINVAL`, crashing the process before any user code runs.

2. **Missing EOF event (#727)**: Even when stdin is valid, Claude Code may not properly close the pipe after writing data. The previous implementation waited indefinitely for `stdin.on('end')`, which never fires in this scenario.

## Changes

### `src/cli/stdin-reader.ts`

- **Added `isStdinAvailable()` function**: Safely probes stdin by wrapping access in try-catch, catching Bun's `EINVAL` crash before it propagates
- **Added 5-second timeout**: Uses `setTimeout` + `Promise` pattern to resolve with available data if `stdin.on('end')` doesn't fire
- **Graceful error handling**: Returns `undefined` instead of crashing when stdin is unavailable or errors occur
- **Proper cleanup**: Removes event listeners after resolution to prevent memory leaks

## Testing

Verified the following scenarios work correctly:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Normal stdin input | ✅ Works | ✅ Works |
| Empty stdin (`< /dev/null`) | ❌ Hangs | ✅ Returns validation error |
| Stdin pipe stays open | ❌ Hangs forever | ✅ Timeout after 5s |
| Invalid stdin fd (Bun crash) | ❌ EINVAL crash | ✅ Graceful fallback |

## Impact

- **No breaking changes**: Hooks that work today continue working
- **Defensive improvement**: Adds multiple layers of protection against stdin edge cases
- **Backwards compatible**: Falls back gracefully, allowing handlers to validate input as needed

thedotmack/claude-mem#804.title: fix: CLAUDE.md generation improvements (spurious directories + path matching)
thedotmack/claude-mem#804.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#804.body:
## ⚠️ Critical: This Fix Addresses a Regression in v9.0.8

In v9.0.8, the directory existence check was **reverted** to use `mkdirSync()`, reintroducing the bug of creating spurious directories from malformed paths.

### Technical Comparison

| Aspect | v9.0.8 (Upstream) | This PR |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| **Directory handling** | ❌ `mkdirSync(folderPath, { recursive: true })` | ✅ `existsSync()` check first |
| **Malformed path protection** | ❌ Creates any directory | ✅ Skips non-existent folders |
| **Empty content handling** | ❌ Removed check | ✅ Skips "No recent activity" |
| **Filesystem pollution** | ❌ Creates spurious folders | ✅ Only writes to valid paths |

### What v9.0.8 Did (Problematic)

```diff
- // Only write to folders that already exist - never create new directories
- // This prevents creating spurious folder structures from malformed paths
- if (!existsSync(folderPath)) {
-   logger.debug('FOLDER_INDEX', 'Skipping non-existent folder', { folderPath });
-   return;
- }
+ // Ensure directory exists
+ mkdirSync(folderPath, { recursive: true });
```

And also removed:
```diff
- // Skip if no meaningful observations
- if (formatted.includes('*No recent activity*')) {
-   continue;
- }
```

The reversion means:
1. **Security risk**: Malformed paths (e.g., from path traversal bugs) will create arbitrary directories
2. **Filesystem pollution**: Spurious folder structures appear in the project
3. **Noise**: Empty CLAUDE.md files with "No recent activity" are created everywhere

### What This PR Does (Correct)

```typescript
// Only write to folders that already exist - never create new directories
if (!existsSync(folderPath)) {
  logger.debug('FOLDER_INDEX', 'Skipping non-existent folder', { folderPath });
  return;
}

// Skip empty content
if (formatted.includes('*No recent activity*')) {
  continue;
}
```

This ensures:
1. ✅ **Defensive coding**: Never create directories from potentially malformed paths
2. ✅ **Clean filesystem**: Only writes to existing, valid project folders
3. ✅ **Reduced noise**: Skips files with no meaningful content
4. ✅ **Bug detection**: If a folder doesn't exist, it's likely a bug in path calculation

### Real-World Bug This Fixes

The original issue (#794) was that malformed paths like `/home/user/project/src//components` (note the double slash) or mismatched absolute/relative paths would cause the system to create incorrect directory structures in the user's project.

---

## Original Summary

Fixes two issues with CLAUDE.md file generation:

1. **Spurious directory creation** - `writeClaudeMdToFolder()` was creating directories for malformed paths. Now checks `existsSync()` first and skips non-existent folders.

2. **Empty folder CLAUDE.md** - Path format mismatch where `isDirectChild()` compared absolute paths (from API) with relative paths (from database). Fixes #794.

**Changes:**
- Check folder existence before attempting to write CLAUDE.md
- Skip writing when timeline shows "No recent activity"
- Add `normalizePath()` helper to handle path separators and trailing slashes
- Fix double-slash handling (`src//file.ts` → `src/file.ts`)
- Implement suffix-based matching for absolute/relative path comparison
- Add comprehensive test suite for path matching scenarios

thedotmack/claude-mem#812.title: fix: restore SessionEnd hook for SDK agent cleanup (Issue #737)
thedotmack/claude-mem#812.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#812.body:
## Summary

Restores the SessionEnd hook that was removed in December 2025, enabling proper cleanup of SDK agent subprocesses when Claude Code sessions close.

### Problem

When Claude Code sessions close, SDK agent subprocesses were not being terminated because the SessionEnd hook was removed (#32198 "Removed redundant SessionEnd cleanup hook"). This caused orphaned processes to accumulate:
- Observed **14 orphaned SDK agents** consuming **5.6GB RAM**
- Orphans persist indefinitely until manually killed or system reboot
- File descriptor leak from unclosed stdin/stdout/stderr pipes

### Root Cause

The removal of SessionEnd hook on Dec 27, 2025 broke the cleanup chain:
```
SessionEnd (removed) → deleteSession() never called → SDK agents never terminated
```

### Solution

- Add `session-end` handler that calls `/api/sessions/cleanup` endpoint
- Add `/api/sessions/cleanup` endpoint to SessionRoutes  
- Add `getSessionIdByContentSessionId()` to lookup session without creating
- Add `SessionEnd` hook entry to `hooks.json`
- Add `cleanupProcessStreams()` to ProcessRegistry for FD leak prevention

### Cleanup Flow

```
1. Claude Code fires SessionEnd hook
2. Handler calls POST /api/sessions/cleanup with contentSessionId
3. Endpoint looks up sessionDbId, calls completionHandler.completeByDbId()
4. SessionManager.deleteSession() aborts SDK agent via AbortController
5. ProcessRegistry.ensureProcessExit() waits 5s then SIGKILLs if needed
6. cleanupProcessStreams() destroys pipes to release FDs
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/handlers/session-end.ts` | **New** - SessionEnd handler |
| `src/cli/handlers/index.ts` | Register session-end event type |
| `src/services/sqlite/SessionStore.ts` | Add getSessionIdByContentSessionId() |
| `src/services/worker/http/routes/SessionRoutes.ts` | Add /api/sessions/cleanup endpoint |
| `src/services/worker-service.ts` | Update help text |
| `src/services/worker/ProcessRegistry.ts` | Add stream cleanup for FD leak |
| `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` | Add SessionEnd hook |

## Security

✅ Endpoint is safe:
- Localhost only (127.0.0.1)
- SQL injection safe (parameterized query)
- No sensitive data exposure
- Input validation present

## Future Improvements

The following improvements were identified during code review but are non-blocking:

1. **Add fetch timeout** - Use Promise.race with 5s timeout to prevent hang if worker is slow
2. **Increase hook timeout** - Consider 45-60s instead of 30s for slow Windows systems
3. **Enhanced logging** - Return sessionDbId in response for debugging
4. **Debug logging for FD cleanup** - Add debug log for unexpected stream cleanup errors

- [ ] Close Claude Code session

- [ ] Check worker logs for "Session cleanup triggered" message

thedotmack/claude-mem#833.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#833.body:
## Summary

The `scripts/cleanup-duplicates.ts` script was missing `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` after creating the database connection. This caused CASCADE DELETE to not trigger when deleting duplicate observations, leaving orphan records in `observation_files` and `observation_concepts` tables.

## Root Cause

SQLite defaults to `foreign_keys = OFF`. Without explicitly enabling it, the `ON DELETE CASCADE` constraints don't fire, leaving orphaned child records.

## Changes

Added `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` after database connection (only in write mode, not dry-run):

```typescript
if (!dryRun) {
  db.run('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON');
}
```

## Impact

Users who ran the cleanup script previously may have orphaned records causing "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" errors. They can clean these manually:

```sql
DELETE FROM observation_files WHERE observation_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM observations);
DELETE FROM observation_concepts WHERE observation_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM observations);
```

thedotmack/claude-mem#802.title: fix: session recovery with AbortController reset and stale resume handling
thedotmack/claude-mem#802.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#802.body:
## ⚠️ Critical: This Fix Addresses a Regression in v9.0.8

In v9.0.8, the AbortController reset logic was **removed entirely** from `SessionManager.ts`. This creates a regression where sessions cannot recover from generator failures.

### Technical Comparison

| Aspect | v9.0.8 (Upstream) | This PR |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| **AbortController handling** | ❌ Removed entirely | ✅ Controlled reset when safe |
| **Race condition protection** | N/A (code removed) | ✅ Only reset if `generatorPromise === null` |
| **Session recovery** | ❌ Dead sessions after failure | ✅ Sessions can continue |
| **Diagnostic logging** | ❌ None | ✅ Logs reset and edge cases |

### What v9.0.8 Did (Problematic)

```diff
- // CRITICAL: Reset abortController if it was aborted
- if (session.abortController.signal.aborted) {
-   if (session.generatorPromise === null) {
-     session.abortController = new AbortController();
-   }
- }
+ // (code completely removed)
```

The removal means:
1. When a generator fails and aborts the controller, the session becomes permanently "dead"
2. Subsequent `queueObservation()` calls will create sessions that immediately exit
3. No recovery path exists for sessions with aborted controllers

### What This PR Does (Correct)

```typescript
// CRITICAL: Reset abortController if it was aborted
if (session.abortController.signal.aborted) {
  if (session.generatorPromise === null) {
    // Safe to reset - generator has finished
    session.abortController = new AbortController();
  } else {
    // Race condition warning - generator still active
    logger.warn('SESSION', 'Aborted controller found but generator still active');
  }
}
```

This ensures:
1. ✅ Sessions can recover from generator failures
2. ✅ Race conditions are detected and logged
3. ✅ Conversation history and context are preserved
4. ✅ Stale resume session IDs are handled gracefully

---

## Original Summary

Implements session recovery improvements to handle two failure modes:

1. **AbortController reset** - When a cached session has an aborted controller (from previous generator failure), reset it before reuse
2. **Stale resume session handling** - Detect and recover from stale `memorySessionId` when SDK exits with code 1 during resume

**Changes:**
- Reset aborted AbortController when reusing cached session (if generator is null)
- Detect resume failure (exit code 1) and clear stale memorySessionId
- Update SessionStore.updateMemorySessionId to handle FK constraints with transaction
- Add row count verification for parent session updates
- Graceful skip when memorySessionId is null (allows recovery instead of crash)

**Safety guarantees:**
- Only reset AbortController when generatorPromise is null (no race condition)
- FK constraints temporarily disabled in transaction, re-enabled after
- Orphaned child records retained for forensic analysis

thedotmack/claude-mem#84.body:
The claude-mem search skill had four usability issues: unclear auto-invoke triggers, excessive permission prompts (10+ per multi-query session), risk of documentation truncation, and no date range filtering for temporal queries like "what did we do yesterday".

## Changes

### Wrapper script eliminates permission prompt spam
- Created `claude-mem-search.cjs` - unified CLI wrapping all 10 HTTP search endpoints
- Single permission prompt, whitelist once, reuse indefinitely
- Native Node.js HTTP client (no dependencies), proper error handling

```bash

curl "http://localhost:37777/api/search/observations?query=bug"
curl "http://localhost:37777/api/search/by-type?type=feature"

# After: single script permission
claude-mem-search.cjs observations "bug" --format=index
claude-mem-search.cjs by-type feature --from=2025-11-09
```

### Date range filtering across all search endpoints
- Added `parseDateRange()` helper parsing ISO strings or Unix timestamps
- Extended 6 endpoints: observations, sessions, prompts, by-type, by-concept, by-file
- Query params: `?from=2025-11-09T00:00:00&to=2025-11-09T23:59:59`
- Schema already supported date filtering; now exposed via HTTP API

```typescript
// Worker service now parses and forwards date range
const dateRange = parseDateRange(req.query.from, req.query.to);
sessionSearch.searchObservations(query, { limit, project, dateRange });
```

### Enhanced auto-invoke reliability
- Skill description now explicit: `**AUTO-INVOKE THIS SKILL** when users ask about past work, history, what was done before...`
- Added trigger phrases: "what did we", "how did we", "yesterday", "last week", temporal queries

### Documentation safety guard
- Added warning in SKILL.md: never truncate documentation endpoints with `head`/`tail`
- Only truncate data responses; always read API help completely

## Testing
- 3 new tests for date range filtering (ISO strings, Unix timestamps, combined with type filter)
- All 9 tests passing (6 existing + 3 new)

thedotmack/claude-mem#85.title: feat: Add MCP search server toggle with dedicated API architecture
thedotmack/claude-mem#85.author: thedotmack
thedotmack/claude-mem#85.body:
## Summary
- Added user-controllable MCP search server toggle in viewer settings UI
- **Architectural improvement**: MCP toggle now completely separate from general settings system
- Implements dedicated API endpoints for MCP control (`/api/mcp/status`, `/api/mcp/toggle`)
- File-based enable/disable mechanism (`.mcp.json` ↔ `.mcp.json.disabled`)
- Defaults to enabled for backward compatibility
- Independent state management prevents MCP toggle from interfering with settings persistence

## Architecture

**Dedicated MCP API Endpoints:**
- `GET /api/mcp/status` - Returns current MCP enabled state
- `POST /api/mcp/toggle` - Toggles MCP on/off with validation

**Separation of Concerns:**
- MCP toggle is **not** part of the Settings interface, useSettings hook, or settings constants
- Sidebar manages MCP state independently with its own useState hooks
- MCP toggle has dedicated handler (`handleMcpToggle`) separate from settings save
- Prevents coupling between MCP toggle and settings persistence

**Why This Matters:**
This architectural separation ensures:
1. MCP toggle responds immediately without affecting settings save flow
2. Cleaner error handling and status feedback for MCP operations
3. No risk of MCP state interfering with other settings
4. More maintainable code with clear boundaries

## Changes

**Worker Service** (`src/services/worker-service.ts`):
- Added `GET /api/mcp/status` endpoint to check MCP enabled state
- Added `POST /api/mcp/toggle` endpoint to toggle MCP on/off
- Added `isMcpEnabled()` helper to check MCP status by file existence
- Added `toggleMcp(enabled: boolean)` helper to rename config file
- **Note:** MCP state is **not** included in general settings endpoints

**Viewer UI** (`src/ui/viewer/components/Sidebar.tsx`):
- Added separate "MCP Search Server" section (independent from Settings form)
- Added `mcpEnabled` state with dedicated useState hook
- Added `mcpToggling` and `mcpStatus` state for toggle feedback
- Added `handleMcpToggle` handler for immediate MCP control
- Fetches MCP status on mount via `/api/mcp/status`
- Help text: "claude-mem suggests using skill-based search (saves ~2,500 tokens at session start), but some users prefer MCP. Disable to only use skill-based search. Requires Claude Code restart to apply changes."
- Status feedback: "✓ Updated (restart Claude Code to apply)" or error messages

**Types & Constants:**
- Settings interface, useSettings hook, and DEFAULT_SETTINGS remain unchanged
- MCP state managed independently outside the settings system

## Technical Details

**Enable/Disable Mechanism:**
- Enabled: `plugin/.mcp.json` exists
- Disabled: `plugin/.mcp.json` renamed to `plugin/.mcp.json.disabled`
- File renaming prevents Claude Code from loading MCP tools at session start

**User Flow:**
1. User opens viewer settings sidebar (http://localhost:37777)
2. User unchecks "Enable MCP Search Server" checkbox
3. Toggle immediately calls `/api/mcp/toggle` endpoint
4. Worker service renames `.mcp.json` → `.mcp.json.disabled`
5. User sees "✓ Updated (restart Claude Code to apply)" status message
6. User restarts Claude Code session
7. MCP search tools no longer loaded (saves ~2,500 tokens at session start)

**Error Handling:**
- Validation: `enabled` must be boolean (400 Bad Request if invalid)
- Proper error responses with success/failure status
- UI displays error messages with automatic timeout
- Toggle button disabled during operation to prevent race conditions

## Why This Matters

With v5.4.0's skill-based search migration, MCP tools are technically redundant. However, some users may prefer MCP tools for:
- Familiarity with existing workflows
- Direct tool invocation vs. skill-based indirection
- Testing/debugging purposes

This toggle gives users choice while defaulting to the recommended configuration (MCP enabled for backward compatibility, with UI guidance suggesting skill-based search).

- [ ] Verify unchecking checkbox immediately calls toggle API
- [ ] Verify toggle renames `.mcp.json` to `.mcp.json.disabled`
- [ ] Verify checking checkbox renames `.mcp.json.disabled` back to `.mcp.json`
- [ ] Verify status messages appear and auto-dismiss after 3 seconds
- [ ] Verify MCP status persists independently of settings changes
- [ ] Verify MCP tools disappear/reappear in Claude Code after restart
- [ ] Verify error handling for invalid requests

thedotmack/claude-mem#856.title: fix: add idle timeout to prevent zombie observer processes
thedotmack/claude-mem#856.author: thedotmack
thedotmack/claude-mem#856.body:
## Problem

Observer subprocesses accumulate because `SessionQueueProcessor.createIterator()` waits forever when the queue is empty. If the `session-complete` hook doesn't fire (terminal closed, crash, network issue), processes never exit.

**User reported:** 79 processes consuming 13.4GB swap (same issue PR #848 addresses).

## Root Cause Analysis

```typescript
// SessionQueueProcessor.ts - BEFORE
while (!signal.aborted) {
  await this.waitForMessage(signal);  // ← Waits FOREVER
}
```

The iterator only exits when `abortController.abort()` is called via `deleteSession()`. No timeout = infinite wait.

## Solution

Add idle timeout to `SessionQueueProcessor`:

1. **`waitForMessage()`** now accepts timeout and returns `boolean` (true = message, false = timeout)
2. **`createIterator()`** tracks `lastActivityTime` and exits gracefully after 3 minutes of inactivity
3. When iterator returns → SDK query completes → subprocess exits cleanly

```typescript
// SessionQueueProcessor.ts - AFTER
const IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 * 60 * 1000; // 3 minutes

// In createIterator:
const receivedMessage = await this.waitForMessage(signal, IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
if (!receivedMessage && !signal.aborted) {
  const idleDuration = Date.now() - lastActivityTime;
  if (idleDuration >= IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS) {
    logger.info('SESSION', 'Exiting queue iterator due to idle timeout', ...);
    return; // Exit gracefully
  }
}
```

## Why This Instead of PR #848

PR #848 adds pattern-matching cleanup (`killDuplicatesByResumeId`, `killStaleObservers`) to kill processes after they become zombies. This PR fixes the **root cause** so processes exit on their own.

| Approach | PR #848 | This PR |
|----------|---------|---------
| Strategy | Reactive cleanup | Preventive timeout |
| Detection | Pattern matching (`--disallowedTools`) | N/A (self-exit) |
| Timing | After zombie (30 min) | Before zombie (3 min idle) |
| State | External kill (may leave inconsistent state) | Graceful exit |

## Changes

- `src/services/queue/SessionQueueProcessor.ts`: Add idle timeout with graceful exit

## Review Feedback Addressed

- Fixed race condition: Reset `lastActivityTime` on spurious wakeup when timeout fires but duration check fails
- Added optional chaining for `onIdleTimeout` callback
- Enhanced logging with `thresholdMs` parameter
- Added comprehensive unit tests (11 test cases covering timeout behavior, abort handling, event cleanup)

## Test Plan

- [x] Build succeeds
- [x] Observer exits after 3 minutes of no messages
- [x] Normal message processing unaffected
- [x] No zombie accumulation over extended usage
- [x] Unit tests pass (11 test cases)

---

Supersedes #848

thedotmack/claude-mem#87.title: Remove PM2 restart logic from hooks to fix race condition with watch mode
thedotmack/claude-mem#87.author: app/copilot-swe-agent
thedotmack/claude-mem#87.body:
PostToolUse hook called `pm2 start` on unhealthy worker checks, racing with PM2's watch mode auto-restart on file changes. This caused `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'pm2_env')` and accumulated unnecessary restarts.

## Changes

**`src/shared/worker-utils.ts`**
- Removed PM2 restart orchestration from `ensureWorkerRunning()` 
- Function now only checks worker health via HTTP endpoint
- Removed unused imports (`execSync`, `getPackageRoot`) and helper functions (`waitForWorkerHealth`)
- Updated error message to explain PM2 watch mode handles restarts automatically

**Before:**
```typescript
export async function ensureWorkerRunning(): Promise<void> {
  if (await isWorkerHealthy()) return;
  
  // Calls pm2 start, waits for health - races with watch mode
  execSync(`"${pm2Path}" start "${ecosystemPath}"`, { cwd: packageRoot, stdio: 'pipe' });
  if (!await waitForWorkerHealth()) {
    throw new Error("Worker failed to become healthy after restart");
  }
}
```

**After:**
```typescript
export async function ensureWorkerRunning(): Promise<void> {
  if (await isWorkerHealthy()) return;
  
  const port = getWorkerPort();
  throw new Error(
    `Worker service is not responding on port ${port}.\n\n` +
    `If you just updated the plugin, PM2's watch mode should restart automatically.\n` +
    `If the problem persists, run: pm2 restart claude-mem-worker`
  );
}
```

PM2's watch mode (intentionally enabled in `ecosystem.config.cjs`) handles all restarts on file changes. Hooks now only verify worker health, eliminating the race condition entirely.

thedotmack/claude-mem#835.title: fix: handle nested XML tags in parser extractField and extractArrayElements
thedotmack/claude-mem#835.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#835.body:
## Summary

The parser's regex patterns used `[^<]*` and `[^<]+` which fail immediately when content contains any `<` character (like nested tags or code snippets).

## Root Cause

**File:** `src/sdk/parser.ts`

```typescript
// Before: Stops at first < character
const regex = new RegExp(`<${fieldName}>([^<]*)</${fieldName}>`);
```

Example failure case from Gemini output:
```xml
<investigated>
  <item>Checked parser.ts</item>
  <item>Reviewed project context</item>
</investigated>
```

| Input Content | Regex `[^<]*` Behavior | Result |
|---------------|----------------------|--------|
| `Simple text` | Matches "Simple text" | ✅ Success |
| `<item>Text</item>` | Stops at first `<` | ❌ NULL |

## Solution

Changed regex from `[^<]*` to `[\s\S]*?` (non-greedy match any character including newlines):

```typescript
// After: Matches any content including nested tags
const regex = new RegExp(`<${fieldName}>([\\s\\S]*?)</${fieldName}>`);
```

## Changes

- `extractField()`: `[^<]*` → `[\s\S]*?`
- `extractArrayElements()`: 
  - Array block: `(.*?)` → `([\s\S]*?)`
  - Element pattern: `[^<]+` → `[\s\S]*?`

thedotmack/claude-mem#90.title: Fix: Pass CWD context to SDK agent for spatial awareness
thedotmack/claude-mem#90.author: app/copilot-swe-agent
thedotmack/claude-mem#90.body:
The SDK agent lacked working directory context, causing it to search wrong repositories and report false "file not found" errors when files existed in different projects.

## Changes

### Data Flow
Added CWD propagation through the entire pipeline:
```
PostToolUseInput.cwd → save-hook → worker API → SessionManager → SDK agent → <tool_cwd> in prompt XML
```

### Type Definitions
- Added `cwd?: string` to `ObservationData` and `PendingMessage` interfaces

### Hook & Worker Layer
- `save-hook.ts`: Extract `cwd` from input, pass to worker API
- `worker-service.ts`: Accept `cwd` in observations endpoint
- `SessionManager.ts`: Include `cwd` in queued messages

### SDK Agent & Prompts
- `SDKAgent.ts`: Pass `cwd` to prompt builder
- `prompts.ts`: Inject `<tool_cwd>` element in observation XML
- `buildInitPrompt()`: Added "SPATIAL AWARENESS" section documenting `tool_cwd` semantics

### Example
```xml
<tool_used>
  <tool_name>ReadTool</tool_name>
  <tool_time>2025-11-10T19:18:03Z</tool_time>
  <tool_cwd>/home/user/my-project</tool_cwd>  <!-- NEW -->
  <tool_input>{"path":"src/index.ts"}</tool_input>
  <tool_output>{"content":"..."}</tool_output>
</tool_used>
```

SDK agent now knows which repository it's observing and can match requested paths to execution context.

## Testing
- 8 unit tests validating end-to-end CWD propagation
- Backward compatible: optional field, graceful when missing

> The SDK agent has no spatial awareness because working directory (CWD) information is captured at the hook level but deliberately not passed to the worker service. This causes the SDK agent to search wrong repositories and generate false "file not found" reports even when files exist and are successfully read.
>

> 
> **Location:** `src/hooks/save-hook.ts` lines 14 and 64-69

> - Match user-requested file paths to tool execution paths
> - Determine which directory was actually searched
> - Verify if files exist in the correct location
> 
> **Result:** SDK agent searches wrong directories and confidently reports "file does not exist" even when:
> - File actually exists
> - Read tool successfully read the file
> - User saw the file content
>

> 
> **Test case:** User requested "Review and understand ai_docs/continuous-improvement/rules.md"

> 2. Read tool successfully read the file ✅
> 3. SDK agent received tool executions but no CWD

> 5. Summary reported: "File does not exist" ❌

> - Confidently reported success while looking at wrong codebase
> - No way to know it was searching the wrong directory
>

> - **Haiku 4.5:** Complete failure - self-contradictory observations
> - **Sonnet 4.5:** Accurate observations with correct paths, but summaries fail
> - **Opus 4:** Can compensate through superior reasoning (at 10-20x cost)
> 
> **Key finding:** Opus works around the architectural issue, but you're paying premium to compensate for missing data plumbing.
> 
> ## Proposed Solution
> 
> ### Step 1: Update save-hook to pass CWD

> // Update POST /sessions/:sessionDbId/observations endpoint
> // Accept cwd in request body
> ```

> 
> ```typescript

> // Add cwd to context so SDK agent knows:
> // - Which directory tool executions happened in
> // - Which repository is being worked on
> // - How to match relative paths
> ```
> 
> ## Benefits
> 
> 1. **Spatial awareness:** SDK agent knows which directory/repository it's observing
> 2. **Accurate path matching:** Can verify if requested paths match executed paths
> 3. **Better summaries:** Won't search wrong repositories or report false negatives
> 4. **Works with all models:** Even Haiku benefits from correct context (no need for Opus)
> 
> ## Questions
> 
> 1. Is there a reason `cwd` was deliberately excluded from worker API?
> 2. Any concerns with passing working directory to SDK agent?

## Summary
This PR includes two key enhancements:
1. **Summary Hook Enhancement**: Extracts and includes the last user message from the Claude Code session transcript when generating session summaries
2. **Activity Indicator Improvements**: Enhanced session manager to track and broadcast processing status based on active sessions and queue depth

## Summary Hook Changes
- **Added transcript reading capability**: New function to read and parse the transcript file to extract the last user message
- **Enhanced summary request**: Modified summary hook to read the transcript file and extract the final user message before sending to worker service
- **Improved context**: Session summaries now include what the user's last request was, providing better continuity and understanding
- **Updated SDKSession interface**: Added optional `last_user_message` field
- **Enhanced summary prompt**: Modified to incorporate the last user message in the output format

- **Enhanced SessionManager**: Now tracks and broadcasts processing status based on active sessions and queue depth
- **Better status broadcasting**: Improved logic for when to signal activity to users
- **Queue-aware indicators**: Activity indicator now reflects actual work being processed

### Summary Hook
The summary hook now:
1. Locates the Claude Code transcript file for the current session
2. Parses the JSON-lines transcript format
3. Extracts the last message with `role: "user"` 
4. Includes this message in the summary generation request
5. Passes the message through the worker service to the SDK agent

### Activity Indicator
The SessionManager:
1. Monitors active sessions and queue depth
2. Broadcasts processing status when work is being performed
3. Provides more accurate user feedback about system activity

## Benefits
- **Better session continuity**: Summaries now capture what the user's final intent was
- **Improved context injection**: Future sessions can see what users were asking for
- **Enhanced memory persistence**: Last user messages preserved in session summaries
- **More accurate status feedback**: Users get better visibility into system activity
- **Improved user experience**: Activity indicators reflect actual processing state

thedotmack/claude-mem#836.title: fix: prevent nested duplicate directory creation in CLAUDE.md paths
thedotmack/claude-mem#836.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#836.body:
## Summary

When the current working directory (cwd) is already inside a subdirectory, claude-mem was creating nested duplicate directories when processing relative file paths.

## Root Cause

If cwd is `/project/frontend/` and a file path `frontend/src/components/Header.jsx` is received, the path resolution creates `/project/frontend/frontend/src/components/`.

The existing `isValidPathForClaudeMd()` validation didn't check for this pattern.

## Solution

Added `hasConsecutiveDuplicateSegments()` function that detects consecutive duplicate path segments:

```typescript
function hasConsecutiveDuplicateSegments(resolvedPath: string): boolean {
  const segments = resolvedPath.split(path.sep).filter(s => s && s !== '.' && s !== '..');
  for (let i = 1; i < segments.length; i++) {
    if (segments[i] === segments[i - 1]) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
```

This check is applied in `isValidPathForClaudeMd()` when a projectRoot is provided.

## Examples Rejected

| Path | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `frontend/frontend/src/` | Consecutive "frontend" |
| `backend/backend/services/` | Consecutive "backend" |
| `src/src/components/` | Consecutive "src" |

## Examples Still Allowed

| Path | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `/home/user/projects/user/app/` | Non-consecutive "user" |
| `/src/components/src/utils/` | Non-consecutive "src" |

## Test plan

- [x] Build succeeds
- [ ] Verify paths with consecutive duplicates are rejected
- [ ] Verify legitimate paths with non-consecutive duplicates still work

Fixes #814

thedotmack/claude-mem#837.title: fix: isolate observer sessions to prevent polluting claude --resume list
thedotmack/claude-mem#837.author: Glucksberg
thedotmack/claude-mem#837.body:
## Summary

Observer sessions created by claude-mem were appearing in the main Claude Code session picker (`claude --resume`), cluttering the list with internal plugin sessions that users never intend to resume.

**Impact:** In one user's case, 74 observer sessions out of ~220 total sessions (34% noise).

## Root Cause

The SDK agent spawns Claude subprocesses using the default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (`~/.claude/`), causing observer session files to be stored alongside user sessions in `~/.claude/projects/*/`.

## Solution

Inject `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-mem/observer-config/` when spawning observer processes via `createPidCapturingSpawn()`.

### Changes

1. **`src/shared/paths.ts`**: Added `OBSERVER_CONFIG_DIR` constant
2. **`src/services/worker/ProcessRegistry.ts`**: Modified spawn to inject isolated config dir

### Result

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Observer sessions in `~/.claude/projects/*/` | Observer sessions in `~/.claude-mem/observer-config/projects/*/` |
| Mixed with user sessions in `claude --resume` | Completely isolated from user sessions |
| 34% noise in resume picker | 0% noise |

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify observer sessions are created in `~/.claude-mem/observer-config/`
