thedotmack/claude-mem#964.title: Add fetch timeouts to Stop hook and health checks
thedotmack/claude-mem#964.author: rodboev
thedotmack/claude-mem#964.body:
## Summary

- Adds `fetchWithTimeout()` helper using `Promise.race` + `setTimeout` (avoids `AbortSignal.timeout()` which causes libuv assertion crashes in Bun on Windows)
- Applies the already-defined `HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s / 45s on Windows) to `isWorkerHealthy()` and `getWorkerVersion()` — previously unused
- Applies `HOOK_TIMEOUTS.DEFAULT` to the summarize POST request

## Problem

When the worker is unreachable (crashed, zombie process, not started), the Stop hook hangs for the full hook timeout (up to 120s) because all `fetch()` calls in `worker-utils.ts` and `summarize.ts` have **no timeout** — `AbortSignal.timeout()` was removed to avoid a Bun/Windows libuv assertion crash.

This means every session exit (`/exit`, Ctrl+C) blocks for 2+ minutes when the worker is down.

## Solution

`Promise.race` with `setTimeout` provides the same timeout behavior without `AbortSignal`, so no libuv assertion:

```typescript
export function fetchWithTimeout(url: string, init: RequestInit = {}, timeoutMs: number): Promise<Response> {
  return Promise.race([
    fetch(url, init),
    new Promise<never>((_, reject) =>
      setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Request timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`)), timeoutMs)
    ),
  ]);
}
```

The orphaned fetch after timeout is harmless since the hook process exits shortly after.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify Stop hook completes in <5s when worker is running
- [ ] Verify Stop hook exits within HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS when worker is down (not the full hook timeout)
- [ ] Verify no libuv assertion crash on Windows with Bun
- [ ] Verify `ensureWorkerRunning()` returns `false` promptly when worker is unreachable

Fixes #963

thedotmack/claude-mem#960.title: fix: remove user-message hook from SessionStart to prevent startup error
thedotmack/claude-mem#960.author: rodboev
thedotmack/claude-mem#960.body:
## Summary

- Removes the `user-message` hook from SessionStart hooks
- Eliminates the "SessionStart:startup hook error" message on every session start

## Problem

The `user-message` hook handler exits with code 3 (`USER_MESSAGE_ONLY`), which is intentional for terminal-only output. However, Claude Code interprets any non-zero exit code as a failure and displays an error message.

**Exit code definitions in the codebase:**
```javascript
var d = {
  SUCCESS: 0,        // Hook ran successfully
  FAILURE: 1,        // Hook failed with error
  USER_MESSAGE_ONLY: 3  // Output to terminal only, don't inject
};
```

The `context` hook (exit code 0) already handles injecting context into the conversation, making the `user-message` hook redundant for SessionStart.

## Fix

Remove the `user-message` hook entry from the SessionStart hooks array. This:
1. Eliminates the spurious error message
2. Saves up to 60 seconds of potential timeout on slow systems
3. No behavior change — context injection still works via the `context` hook

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` | Remove `user-message` hook from SessionStart array |

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify no "SessionStart:startup hook error" message on session start
- [ ] Verify context injection still works via the `context` hook
- [ ] Verify `user-message` hook still works in other contexts where it's used

## Related Issues

- Closes #905
- Related: #918 (SessionStart hooks block terminal)
- Related: #957 (unnecessary stop in hook chain)

thedotmack/claude-mem#959.title: fix: fail open on /api/context/inject during initialization
thedotmack/claude-mem#959.author: rodboev
thedotmack/claude-mem#959.body:
## Summary

- `/api/context/inject` now returns empty context immediately if the worker hasn't finished initializing, instead of blocking for up to 5 minutes
- Prevents SessionStart hooks from hanging on Windows where MCP connection setup can stall indefinitely

## Problem

The `/api/context/inject` endpoint blocks on `initializationComplete`, which includes MCP connection setup that can take 5+ minutes (per v9.0.16 release notes). On Windows with the `child_process.spawn` daemon fix (#933), the MCP connection hangs indefinitely, causing:

1. `hook claude-code context` never returns
2. Synchronous SessionStart hooks block Claude Code startup for the full timeout (300s)
3. Even with `async: true` workaround, turn-0 context is never delivered

**Debug trace** shows the MCP server's TCP connection to the worker establishes then immediately drops:
```
[0.13s] NET: connect: attempting to connect to 127.0.0.1:37777
[0.13s] NET: afterConnect    ← TCP established
[0.13s] NET: destroy          ← immediately torn down
```

## Fix

Replace the blocking `await initializationComplete` with a synchronous check of `initializationCompleteFlag`. If not ready, return `200` with empty context instead of blocking. Context becomes available on subsequent prompts once background initialization completes.

**Before:** Blocks up to 5 minutes → hook times out → no context at turn 0
**After:** Returns immediately → hook completes fast → context available from turn 1+

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/services/worker-service.ts` | Replace blocking await with fail-open check |

## Test Plan

- [ ] Start Claude Code on Windows with fresh worker (no existing process on port)
- [ ] Verify SessionStart hook completes within seconds (not minutes)
- [ ] Verify context injection works on subsequent prompts after initialization completes
- [ ] Verify no regression on macOS/Linux where MCP connection succeeds quickly

## Related Issues

- Closes #958
- Related: #918 (SessionStart hooks block terminal)
- Related: #922 (async:true workaround)
- Related: #930 (defer worker initialization)
- Related: v9.0.16 (readiness → health check fix for same root cause)
